#include "micro_wake_word.h"

#ifdef USE_ESP_IDF

#include "esphome/core/application.h"
#include "esphome/core/hal.h"
#include "esphome/core/helpers.h"
#include "esphome/core/log.h"

#include "esphome/components/audio/audio_transfer_buffer.h"

#ifdef USE_OTA
#include "esphome/components/ota/ota_backend.h"
#endif

namespace esphome {
namespace micro_wake_word {

static const char *const TAG = "micro_wake_word";

static const ssize_t DETECTION_QUEUE_LENGTH = 5;

static const size_t DATA_TIMEOUT_MS = 50;

static const uint32_t RING_BUFFER_DURATION_MS = 120;

static const uint32_t INFERENCE_TASK_STACK_SIZE = 3072;
static const UBaseType_t INFERENCE_TASK_PRIORITY = 3;

enum EventGroupBits : uint32_t {
  COMMAND_STOP = (1 << 0),  // Signals the inference task should stop

  TASK_STARTING = (1 << 3),
  TASK_RUNNING = (1 << 4),
  TASK_STOPPING = (1 << 5),
  TASK_STOPPED = (1 << 6),

  ERROR_MEMORY = (1 << 9),
  ERROR_INFERENCE = (1 << 10),

  WARNING_FULL_RING_BUFFER = (1 << 13),

  ERROR_BITS = ERROR_MEMORY | ERROR_INFERENCE,
  ALL_BITS = 0xfffff,  // 24 total bits available in an event group
};

float MicroWakeWord::get_setup_priority() const { return setup_priority::AFTER_CONNECTION; }

static const LogString *micro_wake_word_state_to_string(State state) {
  switch (state) {
    case State::STARTING:
      return LOG_STR("STARTING");
    case State::DETECTING_WAKE_WORD:
      return LOG_STR("DETECTING_WAKE_WORD");
    case State::STOPPING:
      return LOG_STR("STOPPING");
    case State::STOPPED:
      return LOG_STR("STOPPED");
    default:
      return LOG_STR("UNKNOWN");
  }
}

void MicroWakeWord::dump_config() {
  ESP_LOGCONFIG(TAG, "microWakeWord:");
  ESP_LOGCONFIG(TAG, "  models:");
  for (auto &model : this->wake_word_models_) {
    model->log_model_config();
  }
#ifdef USE_MICRO_WAKE_WORD_VAD
  this->vad_model_->log_model_config();
#endif
}

void MicroWakeWord::setup() {
  this->frontend_config_.window.size_ms = FEATURE_DURATION_MS;
  this->frontend_config_.window.step_size_ms = this->features_step_size_;
  this->frontend_config_.filterbank.num_channels = PREPROCESSOR_FEATURE_SIZE;
  this->frontend_config_.filterbank.lower_band_limit = FILTERBANK_LOWER_BAND_LIMIT;
  this->frontend_config_.filterbank.upper_band_limit = FILTERBANK_UPPER_BAND_LIMIT;
  this->frontend_config_.noise_reduction.smoothing_bits = NOISE_REDUCTION_SMOOTHING_BITS;
  this->frontend_config_.noise_reduction.even_smoothing = NOISE_REDUCTION_EVEN_SMOOTHING;
  this->frontend_config_.noise_reduction.odd_smoothing = NOISE_REDUCTION_ODD_SMOOTHING;
  this->frontend_config_.noise_reduction.min_signal_remaining = NOISE_REDUCTION_MIN_SIGNAL_REMAINING;
  this->frontend_config_.pcan_gain_control.enable_pcan = PCAN_GAIN_CONTROL_ENABLE_PCAN;
  this->frontend_config_.pcan_gain_control.strength = PCAN_GAIN_CONTROL_STRENGTH;
  this->frontend_config_.pcan_gain_control.offset = PCAN_GAIN_CONTROL_OFFSET;
  this->frontend_config_.pcan_gain_control.gain_bits = PCAN_GAIN_CONTROL_GAIN_BITS;
  this->frontend_config_.log_scale.enable_log = LOG_SCALE_ENABLE_LOG;
  this->frontend_config_.log_scale.scale_shift = LOG_SCALE_SCALE_SHIFT;

  this->event_group_ = xEventGroupCreate();
  if (this->event_group_ == nullptr) {
    ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to create event group");
    this->mark_failed();
    return;
  }

  this->detection_queue_ = xQueueCreate(DETECTION_QUEUE_LENGTH, sizeof(DetectionEvent));
  if (this->detection_queue_ == nullptr) {
    ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to create detection event queue");
    this->mark_failed();
    return;
  }

  this->microphone_source_->add_data_callback([this](const std::vector<uint8_t> &data) {
    if (this->state_ == State::STOPPED) {
      return;
    }
    std::shared_ptr<RingBuffer> temp_ring_buffer = this->ring_buffer_.lock();
    if (this->ring_buffer_.use_count() > 1) {
      size_t bytes_free = temp_ring_buffer->free();

      if (bytes_free < data.size()) {
        xEventGroupSetBits(this->event_group_, EventGroupBits::WARNING_FULL_RING_BUFFER);
        temp_ring_buffer->reset();
      }
      temp_ring_buffer->write((void *) data.data(), data.size());
    }
  });

#ifdef USE_OTA
  ota::get_global_ota_callback()->add_on_state_callback(
      [this](ota::OTAState state, float progress, uint8_t error, ota::OTAComponent *comp) {
        if (state == ota::OTA_STARTED) {
          this->suspend_task_();
        } else if (state == ota::OTA_ERROR) {
          this->resume_task_();
        }
      });
#endif
}

void MicroWakeWord::inference_task(void *params) {
  MicroWakeWord *this_mww = (MicroWakeWord *) params;

  xEventGroupSetBits(this_mww->event_group_, EventGroupBits::TASK_STARTING);

  {  // Ensures any C++ objects fall out of scope to deallocate before deleting the task

    const size_t new_bytes_to_process =
        this_mww->microphone_source_->get_audio_stream_info().ms_to_bytes(this_mww->features_step_size_);
    std::unique_ptr<audio::AudioSourceTransferBuffer> audio_buffer;
    int8_t features_buffer[PREPROCESSOR_FEATURE_SIZE];

    if (!(xEventGroupGetBits(this_mww->event_group_) & ERROR_BITS)) {
      // Allocate audio transfer buffer
      audio_buffer = audio::AudioSourceTransferBuffer::create(new_bytes_to_process);

      if (audio_buffer == nullptr) {
        xEventGroupSetBits(this_mww->event_group_, EventGroupBits::ERROR_MEMORY);
      }
    }

    if (!(xEventGroupGetBits(this_mww->event_group_) & ERROR_BITS)) {
      // Allocate ring buffer
      std::shared_ptr<RingBuffer> temp_ring_buffer = RingBuffer::create(
          this_mww->microphone_source_->get_audio_stream_info().ms_to_bytes(RING_BUFFER_DURATION_MS));
      if (temp_ring_buffer.use_count() == 0) {
        xEventGroupSetBits(this_mww->event_group_, EventGroupBits::ERROR_MEMORY);
      }
      audio_buffer->set_source(temp_ring_buffer);
      this_mww->ring_buffer_ = temp_ring_buffer;
    }

    if (!(xEventGroupGetBits(this_mww->event_group_) & ERROR_BITS)) {
      this_mww->microphone_source_->start();
      xEventGroupSetBits(this_mww->event_group_, EventGroupBits::TASK_RUNNING);

      while (!(xEventGroupGetBits(this_mww->event_group_) & COMMAND_STOP)) {
        audio_buffer->transfer_data_from_source(pdMS_TO_TICKS(DATA_TIMEOUT_MS));

        if (audio_buffer->available() < new_bytes_to_process) {
          // Insufficient data to generate new spectrogram features, read more next iteration
          continue;
        }

        // Generate new spectrogram features
        uint32_t processed_samples = this_mww->generate_features_(
            (int16_t *) audio_buffer->get_buffer_start(), audio_buffer->available() / sizeof(int16_t), features_buffer);
        audio_buffer->decrease_buffer_length(processed_samples * sizeof(int16_t));

        // Run inference using the new spectorgram features
        if (!this_mww->update_model_probabilities_(features_buffer)) {
          xEventGroupSetBits(this_mww->event_group_, EventGroupBits::ERROR_INFERENCE);
          break;
        }

        // Process each model's probabilities and possibly send a Detection Event to the queue
        this_mww->process_probabilities_();
      }
    }
  }

  xEventGroupSetBits(this_mww->event_group_, EventGroupBits::TASK_STOPPING);

  this_mww->unload_models_();
  this_mww->microphone_source_->stop();
  FrontendFreeStateContents(&this_mww->frontend_state_);
```
</details></tool-use>

Based on my search, here's what I found related to ESP32 Arduino audio preprocessing with TensorFlow Lite:

## TensorFlow Lite Audio Processing on ESP32

### Arduino Audio Tools Library with TFLite
The TfLiteAudioOutput class uses Fast Fourier transform (FFT) to calculate the FFT result which is an array of frequencies with the length of kFeatureSliceSize using slices of audio data. This is then used to update a spectrogram (with the length of kFeatureSliceSize x kFeatureSliceCount). After adding new FFT results to the end, TensorFlow evaluates the updated spectrogram to calculate the classification result.(no content)Phil Schatzmann has adapted the MicroSpeech example from TensorFlow Lite for his arduino-audio-tools framework. The example uses a TensorFlow model which can recognize the words 'yes' and 'no', and works with ESP32 AudioKit boards or any processor with a microphone.

### Spectrogram Generation for Speech Recognition
To process audio samples, they need to be turned into something that looks like an image using a spectrogram. To get a spectrogram, audio samples are broken into small sections and a discrete Fourier transform is performed on each section, giving the frequencies present in that slice of audio. Putting these frequency slices together gives the spectrogram.

### ESPHome Wake Word Detection
The preprocessor generates 40 features over 30 ms (the window duration) of audio data. The preprocessor generates these features every 20 ms (the stride duration), so the first 10 ms of audio data is part of the previous window.(no content)Wake word detection is done entirely with TensorFlow Lite Micro. Wake word models are trained without using Espressif's proprietary Skainet and can be customized without samples from different speakers.

### Key Libraries and Resources
- The Arduino_TensorFlowLite_ESP32 library references the official tflite-micro-esp-examples from Espressif, allowing you to run TensorFlow machine learning models on microcontrollers.
- Espressif provides specific support for tflite-micro, and models are integrated by converting the .tflite file to a C array and writing an Arduino sketch to load and run it.

**Note:** The specific `audio_frontend` library with `FrontendPopulateState` for mel spectrogram preprocessing (from TensorFlow's micro_features frontend) wasn't directly referenced in the search results. This is typically part of TensorFlow Lite Micro's signal processing library, which may require a more targeted search or checking the official TensorFlow Lite Micro repository for the `tensorflow/lite/experimental/microfrontend` component.

# TensorFlow Lite with Arduino for Wake Word Detection

## Overview
The arduino-audio-tools framework adapts TensorFlow Lite's MicroSpeech example for speech recognition on microcontroller boards. The system recognizes specific words like "yes" and "no" using a pre-trained model.

## Key Components

**Audio Input/Output Setup:**
The implementation uses `AudioBoardStream` (microphone input) connected to `TfLiteAudioStream` (model processing) via `StreamCopy`. For the example, an ESP32 AudioKit board captures audio at 16kHz mono.

**Configuration Parameters:**
Essential settings include sample rate, channel count, tensor arena size (typically 10KB), category labels, and the compiled model. The callback function `respondToCommand` handles recognition results.

## Signal Processing Pipeline

The framework processes audio through these stages:

1. **FFT Analysis**: "Fast Fourier transform (FFT) to calculate the FFT result which is an array of frequencies"
2. **Spectrogram Creation**: FFT results build a spectrogram matrix updated with new frequency data
3. **Model Inference**: After accumulating sufficient slices, TensorFlow evaluates the spectrogram
4. **Post-Processing**: Results stabilize through the `TfLiteRecognizeCommands` class

## Dependencies

- Arduino Audio Tools library
- tflite-micro-arduino-examples
- arduino-audio-driver (optional, for AudioKit support)

## Implementation Resource

Complete working example available at the project's GitHub repository under `examples/examples-audiokit/streams-audiokit-tf`.

# Porcupine SDK for Arduino: Key Information

## Supported Boards
**ESP32-S3 is NOT supported.** The documentation explicitly lists only:
- Arduino Nano 33 BLE Sense

## Getting an AccessKey

To obtain credentials for the Porcupine SDK:

1. "Login or Signup for a free account on the Picovoice Console"
2. Navigate to the AccessKey tab and create one or use an existing key
3. Keep your AccessKey confidential

## Adding Custom Wake Words

The process involves three steps:

**1. Get Board UUID:**
Upload the `Porcupine_EN/GetUUID` sketch and copy the printed UUID from the serial monitor.

**2. Train Model:**
Visit Picovoice Console, select "Arm Cortex M" as the platform, specify your board type, and provide the UUID. Training completes within hours.

**3. Import Model:**
Download the trained model (contains `.ppn` binary and `.h` header files), then "Copy the contents of the array inside the `.h` header file and update the `DEFAULT_KEYWORD_ARRAY` values in `params.h`"

## Complete Example Code Structure

```cpp

#define MEMORY_BUFFER_SIZE ...
static uint8_t memory_buffer[MEMORY_BUFFER_SIZE] __attribute__((aligned(16));
static const char* ACCESS_KEY = ...;
const uint8_t keyword_array[] = {...};
static const float SENSITIVITY = 0.75f;
pv_porcupine_t *handle = NULL;

void setup() {
  const pv_status_t status = pv_porcupine_init(
    ACCESS_KEY, MEMORY_BUFFER_SIZE, memory_buffer, 1,
    &keyword_model_sizes, &keyword_models, &SENSITIVITY, &handle);
}

void loop() {
  const int16_t *pcm = pv_audio_rec_get_new_buffer();
  int32_t keyword_index;
  const pv_status_t status = pv_porcupine_process(handle, pcm, &keyword_index);
  if (keyword_index != -1) {
    // Detection event logic
  }
}
```

Based on my search, here's what I found about TensorFlow Lite Micro, ESP32/Arduino, and spectrogram generation:

## General TensorFlow Lite Micro + ESP32 Resources

There's an Arduino library (Arduino_TensorFlowLite_ESP32) that runs TensorFlow machine learning models on microcontrollers for AI/ML applications powered by deep learning and neural networks.(no content)With the included examples, you can recognize speech, detect people using a camera, and recognize "magic wand" gestures. The examples work best with the M5StickC (ESP32) board, which has a microphone and accelerometer.

## Spectrogram Generation Approach

The TfLiteAudioOutput class uses Fast Fourier transform (FFT) to calculate the FFT result as an array of frequencies with length kFeatureSliceSize using slices of audio data. This is then used to update a spectrogram (with length kFeatureSliceSize x kFeatureSliceCount). After adding 2 (kSlicesToProcess) new FFT results to the end, TensorFlow evaluates the updated spectrogram to calculate classification results.(no content)To turn audio samples into something that looks like an image, you can take a spectrogram. To get a spectrogram of an audio sample, you break the sample into small sections and then perform a discrete Fourier transform on each section. This gives the frequencies present in that slice of audio. Putting these frequency slices together gives the spectrogram of the sample.

## Alternative Libraries

You can use libraries such as ArduinoFFT for FFT computation.(no content)For the micro speech example, you set 1960 bytes on input tensor corresponding to 1 second worth of spectrogram, then run inference on model 3-4 times per second and average scores.

---

**Note:** The search did not return specific results for the `FrontendPopulateState` function. This is a lower-level function in the TensorFlow Lite Micro audio frontend (microfrontend) library used for audio preprocessing. You may need to look directly at the [tflite-micro-esp-examples](https://github.com/espressif/tflite-micro-esp-examples) repository or the original TensorFlow Lite Micro source code for documentation on this specific function. The microfrontend module handles Mel-frequency spectrogram generation internally.

// extern const uint8_t no_30ms_start[]          asm("_binary_no_30ms_wav_start");
// extern const uint8_t yes_30ms_start[]         asm("_binary_yes_30ms_wav_start");
extern const uint8_t yes_1000ms_start[]       asm("_binary_yes_1000ms_wav_start");
extern const uint8_t no_1000ms_start[]        asm("_binary_no_1000ms_wav_start");
extern const uint8_t noise_1000ms_start[]     asm("_binary_noise_1000ms_wav_start");
extern const uint8_t silence_1000ms_start[]   asm("_binary_silence_1000ms_wav_start");

Features g_features;
const char *TAG = "feature_provider";

FeatureProvider::FeatureProvider(int feature_size, int8_t* feature_data)
    : feature_size_(feature_size),
      feature_data_(feature_data),
      is_first_run_(true) {
  // Initialize the feature data to default values.
  for (int n = 0; n < feature_size_; ++n) {
    feature_data_[n] = 0;
  }
}

FeatureProvider::~FeatureProvider() {}

TfLiteStatus FeatureProvider::PopulateFeatureData(
    int32_t last_time_in_ms, int32_t time_in_ms, int* how_many_new_slices) {
  if (feature_size_ != kFeatureElementCount) {
    MicroPrintf("Requested feature_data_ size %d doesn't match %d",
                feature_size_, kFeatureElementCount);
    return kTfLiteError;
  }

  // Quantize the time into steps as long as each window stride, so we can
  // figure out which audio data we need to fetch.
  const int last_step = (last_time_in_ms / kFeatureStrideMs);
  const int current_step = (time_in_ms / kFeatureStrideMs);

  int slices_needed = current_step - last_step;
  // If this is the first call, make sure we don't use any cached information.
  if (is_first_run_) {
    TfLiteStatus init_status = InitializeMicroFeatures();
    if (init_status != kTfLiteOk) {
      return init_status;
    }
    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "InitializeMicroFeatures successful");
    is_first_run_ = false;
    slices_needed = kFeatureCount;
  }
#if 1
  if (slices_needed > kFeatureCount) {
    slices_needed = kFeatureCount;
  }
  *how_many_new_slices = slices_needed;

  const int slices_to_keep = kFeatureCount - slices_needed;
  const int slices_to_drop = kFeatureCount - slices_to_keep;
  // If we can avoid recalculating some slices, just move the existing data
  // up in the spectrogram, to perform something like this:
  // last time = 80ms          current time = 120ms
  // +-----------+             +-----------+
  // | data@20ms |         --> | data@60ms |
  // +-----------+       --    +-----------+
  // | data@40ms |     --  --> | data@80ms |
  // +-----------+   --  --    +-----------+
  // | data@60ms | --  --      |  <empty>  |
  // +-----------+   --        +-----------+
  // | data@80ms | --          |  <empty>  |
  // +-----------+             +-----------+
  if (slices_to_keep > 0) {
    for (int dest_slice = 0; dest_slice < slices_to_keep; ++dest_slice) {
      int8_t* dest_slice_data =
          feature_data_ + (dest_slice * kFeatureSize);
      const int src_slice = dest_slice + slices_to_drop;
      const int8_t* src_slice_data =
          feature_data_ + (src_slice * kFeatureSize);
      for (int i = 0; i < kFeatureSize; ++i) {
        dest_slice_data[i] = src_slice_data[i];
      }
    }
  }
  // Any slices that need to be filled in with feature data have their
  // appropriate audio data pulled, and features calculated for that slice.
  if (slices_needed > 0) {
    for (int new_slice = slices_to_keep; new_slice < kFeatureCount;
         ++new_slice) {
      const int new_step = (current_step - kFeatureCount + 1) + new_slice;
      const int32_t slice_start_ms = (new_step * kFeatureStrideMs);
      int16_t* audio_samples = nullptr;
      int audio_samples_size = 0;
      // TODO(petewarden): Fix bug that leads to non-zero slice_start_ms
      GetAudioSamples((slice_start_ms > 0 ? slice_start_ms : 0),
                      kFeatureDurationMs, &audio_samples_size,
                      &audio_samples);
      if (audio_samples_size < kMaxAudioSampleSize) {
        MicroPrintf("Audio data size %d too small, want %d",
                    audio_samples_size, kMaxAudioSampleSize);
        return kTfLiteError;
      }
      int8_t* new_slice_data = feature_data_ + (new_slice * kFeatureSize);
      // size_t num_samples_read;
      // TfLiteStatus generate_status = GenerateMicroFeatures(
      //     audio_samples, audio_samples_size, kFeatureSize,
      //     new_slice_data, &num_samples_read);
      TfLiteStatus generate_status = GenerateFeatures(

# ESP32-S3 Wakeword Detection Project Summary

## Overview
This is a starter template for keyword/wakeword detection on the ESP32-S3 microcontroller, leveraging machine learning for voice-activated applications.

## Hardware Target
- **Primary Board:** ESP32-S3-DevKitC-1
- **Processor:** Dual-core at 240 MHz with integrated Neural Network Accelerator (NNA)
- **Audio Input:** I2S microphone (example: SKU 107990153)

## ML Model & Framework
- **Training Platform:** Edge Impulse
- **Public Reference Model:** "Wakeword-Computer" available at Edge Impulse Studio
- **Default Keyword:** Recognizes the word "computer"
- **Neural Network Library:** `esp-nn` (optimized for Espressif devices)

## Key Features
The implementation includes:
- "Crystal-Clear Audio" with I2S microphone input
- "Software Automatic Gain Control (AGC) for robust performance in varying acoustic environments"
- LED feedback (turns red on detection)
- Model-agnostic C++ library design for easy model swapping

## Build Instructions
```bash
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/klumw/wakeword.git
idf.py set-target esp32s3
idf.py build
```

## Requirements
- ESP-IDF version >= v5.3.2
- Compatible I2S microphone hardware

## Project Structure
Directories include `components/edge_impulse/`, `main/`, and `docs/` with circuit diagrams.

**License:** Apache-2.0
```
</details></tool-use>

   101→void sr_handler_task(void *pvParam) {
   102→  while (true) {
   103→    sr_result_t result;
   104→    if (xQueueReceive(g_sr_data->result_que, &result, portMAX_DELAY) != pdTRUE) {
   105→      continue;
   106→    }
   107→
   108→    if (WAKENET_DETECTED == result.wakenet_mode) {
   109→      if (g_sr_data->user_cb) {
   110→        g_sr_data->user_cb(g_sr_data->user_cb_arg, SR_EVENT_WAKEWORD, -1, -1);
   111→      }
   112→      continue;
   113→    }
   114→
   115→    if (WAKENET_CHANNEL_VERIFIED == result.wakenet_mode) {
   116→      if (g_sr_data->user_cb) {
   117→        g_sr_data->user_cb(g_sr_data->user_cb_arg, SR_EVENT_WAKEWORD_CHANNEL, result.command_id, -1);
   118→      }
   119→      continue;
   120→    }
   121→
   122→    if (ESP_MN_STATE_DETECTED == result.state) {
   123→      if (g_sr_data->user_cb) {
   124→        g_sr_data->user_cb(g_sr_data->user_cb_arg, SR_EVENT_COMMAND, result.command_id, result.phrase_id);
   125→      }
   126→      continue;
   127→    }
   128→
   129→    if (ESP_MN_STATE_TIMEOUT == result.state) {
   130→      if (g_sr_data->user_cb) {
   131→        g_sr_data->user_cb(g_sr_data->user_cb_arg, SR_EVENT_TIMEOUT, -1, -1);
   132→      }
   133→      continue;
   134→    }
   135→  }
   136→  vTaskDelete(NULL);
   137→}

   139→static void audio_feed_task(void *arg) {
   140→  size_t bytes_read = 0;
   141→  int audio_chunksize = g_sr_data->afe_handle->get_feed_chunksize(g_sr_data->afe_data);
   142→  log_i("audio_chunksize=%d, feed_channel=%d", audio_chunksize, SR_CHANNEL_NUM);
   143→
   144→  /* Allocate audio buffer and check for result */
   145→  int16_t *audio_buffer = heap_caps_malloc(audio_chunksize * sizeof(int16_t) * SR_CHANNEL_NUM, MALLOC_CAP_INTERNAL | MALLOC_CAP_8BIT);
   146→  if (NULL == audio_buffer) {
   147→    esp_system_abort("No mem for audio buffer");
   148→  }
   149→  g_sr_data->afe_in_buffer = audio_buffer;
   150→
   151→  while (true) {
   152→    EventBits_t bits = xEventGroupGetBits(g_sr_data->event_group);
   153→    if (NEED_DELETE & bits) {
   154→      xEventGroupSetBits(g_sr_data->event_group, FEED_DELETED);
   155→      break;
   156→    }
   157→    if (PAUSE_FEED & bits) {
   158→      xEventGroupWaitBits(g_sr_data->event_group, PAUSE_FEED | RESUME_FEED, 1, 1, portMAX_DELAY);
   159→    }
   160→
   161→    /* Read audio data from I2S bus */
   162→    //ToDo: handle error
   163→    if (g_sr_data->fill_cb == NULL) {
   164→      vTaskDelay(100);
   165→      continue;
   166→    }
   167→    esp_err_t err = g_sr_data->fill_cb(
   168→      g_sr_data->fill_cb_arg, (char *)audio_buffer, audio_chunksize * g_sr_data->i2s_rx_chan_num * sizeof(int16_t), &bytes_read, portMAX_DELAY
   169→    );
   170→    if (err != ESP_OK) {
   171→      vTaskDelay(100);
   172→      continue;
   173→    }
   174→
   175→    /* Channel Adjust */
   176→    if (g_sr_data->i2s_rx_chan_num == 1) {
   177→      for (int i = audio_chunksize - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
   178→        audio_buffer[i * SR_CHANNEL_NUM + 2] = 0;
   179→        audio_buffer[i * SR_CHANNEL_NUM + 1] = 0;
   180→        audio_buffer[i * SR_CHANNEL_NUM + 0] = audio_buffer[i];
   181→      }
   182→    } else if (g_sr_data->i2s_rx_chan_num == 2) {
   183→      for (int i = audio_chunksize - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
   184→        audio_buffer[i * SR_CHANNEL_NUM + 2] = 0;
   185→        audio_buffer[i * SR_CHANNEL_NUM + 1] = audio_buffer[i * 2 + 1];
   186→        audio_buffer[i * SR_CHANNEL_NUM + 0] = audio_buffer[i * 2 + 0];
   187→      }
   188→    } else {
   189→      vTaskDelay(100);
   190→      continue;
   191→    }
   192→
   193→    /* Feed samples of an audio stream to the AFE_SR */
   194→    g_sr_data->afe_handle->feed(g_sr_data->afe_data, audio_buffer);
   195→    vTaskDelay(2);
   196→  }
   197→  vTaskDelete(NULL);
   198→}
   199→
   200→static void audio_detect_task(void *arg) {
   201→  int afe_chunksize = g_sr_data->afe_handle->get_fetch_chunksize(g_sr_data->afe_data);
   202→  int mu_chunksize = g_sr_data->multinet->get_samp_chunksize(g_sr_data->model_data);
   203→  assert(mu_chunksize == afe_chunksize);
   204→  log_i("------------detect start------------");
   205→
   206→  while (true) {
   207→    EventBits_t bits = xEventGroupGetBits(g_sr_data->event_group);
   208→    if (NEED_DELETE & bits) {
   209→      xEventGroupSetBits(g_sr_data->event_group, DETECT_DELETED);
   210→      break;
   211→    }
   212→    if (PAUSE_DETECT & bits) {
   213→      xEventGroupWaitBits(g_sr_data->event_group, PAUSE_DETECT | RESUME_DETECT, 1, 1, portMAX_DELAY);
   214→    }
   215→
   216→    afe_fetch_result_t *res = g_sr_data->afe_handle->fetch(g_sr_data->afe_data);
   217→    if (!res || res->ret_value == ESP_FAIL) {
   218→      continue;
   219→    }
   220→
   221→    if (g_sr_data->mode == SR_MODE_WAKEWORD) {
   222→      if (res->wakeup_state == WAKENET_DETECTED) {
   223→        log_d("wakeword detected");
   224→        sr_result_t result = {
   225→          .wakenet_mode = WAKENET_DETECTED,
   226→          .state = ESP_MN_STATE_DETECTING,
   227→          .command_id = 0,
   228→          .phrase_id = 0,
   229→        };
   230→        xQueueSend(g_sr_data->result_que, &result, 0);
   231→      } else if (res->wakeup_state == WAKENET_CHANNEL_VERIFIED) {
   232→        sr_set_mode(SR_MODE_OFF);
   233→        log_d("AFE_FETCH_CHANNEL_VERIFIED, channel index: %d", res->trigger_channel_id);
   234→        sr_result_t result = {
   235→          .wakenet_mode = WAKENET_CHANNEL_VERIFIED,
   236→          .state = ESP_MN_STATE_DETECTING,
   237→          .command_id = res->trigger_channel_id,
   238→          .phrase_id = 0,
   239→        };
   240→        xQueueSend(g_sr_data->result_que, &result, 0);
   241→      }
   242→    }
   243→
   244→    if (g_sr_data->mode == SR_MODE_COMMAND) {
   245→
   246→      esp_mn_state_t mn_state = ESP_MN_STATE_DETECTING;
   247→      mn_state = g_sr_data->multinet->detect(g_sr_data->model_data, res->data);
   248→
   249→      if (ESP_MN_STATE_DETECTING == mn_state) {
   250→        continue;
   251→      }
   252→
   253→      if (ESP_MN_STATE_TIMEOUT == mn_state) {
   254→        sr_set_mode(SR_MODE_OFF);
   255→        log_d("Time out");
   256→        sr_result_t result = {
   257→          .wakenet_mode = WAKENET_NO_DETECT,
   258→          .state = mn_state,
   259→          .command_id = 0,
   260→          .phrase_id = 0,
   261→        };
   262→        xQueueSend(g_sr_data->result_que, &result, 0);
   263→        continue;
   264→      }
   265→
   266→      if (ESP_MN_STATE_DETECTED == mn_state) {
   267→        sr_set_mode(SR_MODE_OFF);
   268→        esp_mn_results_t *mn_result = g_sr_data->multinet->get_results(g_sr_data->model_data);
   269→        for (int i = 0; i < mn_result->num; i++) {
   270→          log_d("TOP %d, command_id: %d, phrase_id: %d, prob: %f", i + 1, mn_result->command_id[i], mn_result->phrase_id[i], mn_result->prob[i]);
   271→        }
   272→
   273→        int sr_command_id = mn_result->command_id[0];
   274→        int sr_phrase_id = mn_result->phrase_id[0];
   275→        log_d("Detected command : %d, phrase: %d", sr_command_id, sr_phrase_id);
   276→        sr_result_t result = {
   277→          .wakenet_mode = WAKENET_NO_DETECT,
   278→          .state = mn_state,
   279→          .command_id = sr_command_id,
   280→          .phrase_id = sr_phrase_id,
   281→        };
   282→        xQueueSend(g_sr_data->result_que, &result, 0);
   283→        continue;
   284→      }
   285→      log_e("Exception unhandled");
   286→    }
   287→  }
   288→  vTaskDelete(NULL);
   289→}
   290→
   291→esp_err_t sr_set_mode(sr_mode_t mode) {
   292→  ESP_RETURN_ON_FALSE(NULL != g_sr_data, ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE, "SR is not running");
   293→  switch (mode) {
   294→    case SR_MODE_OFF:
   295→      if (g_sr_data->mode == SR_MODE_WAKEWORD) {
   296→        g_sr_data->afe_handle->disable_wakenet(g_sr_data->afe_data);
   297→      }
   298→      break;
   299→    case SR_MODE_WAKEWORD:
   300→      if (g_sr_data->mode != SR_MODE_WAKEWORD) {
   301→        g_sr_data->afe_handle->enable_wakenet(g_sr_data->afe_data);
   302→      }
   303→      break;
   304→    case SR_MODE_COMMAND:
   305→      if (g_sr_data->mode == SR_MODE_WAKEWORD) {
   306→        g_sr_data->afe_handle->disable_wakenet(g_sr_data->afe_data);
   307→      }
   308→      break;
   309→    default: return ESP_FAIL;
   310→  }
   311→  g_sr_data->mode = mode;
   312→  return ESP_OK;
   313→}
   314→
   315→esp_err_t sr_start(
   316→  sr_fill_cb fill_cb, void *fill_cb_arg, sr_channels_t rx_chan, sr_mode_t mode, const char *input_format, const sr_cmd_t sr_commands[], size_t cmd_number,
   317→  sr_event_cb cb, void *cb_arg
   318→) {
   319→  esp_err_t ret = ESP_OK;
   320→  ESP_RETURN_ON_FALSE(NULL == g_sr_data, ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE, "SR already running");
   321→
   322→  g_sr_data = heap_caps_calloc(1, sizeof(sr_data_t), MALLOC_CAP_INTERNAL | MALLOC_CAP_8BIT);
   323→  ESP_RETURN_ON_FALSE(NULL != g_sr_data, ESP_ERR_NO_MEM, "Failed create sr data");
   324→
   325→  g_sr_data->result_que = xQueueCreate(3, sizeof(sr_result_t));
   326→  ESP_GOTO_ON_FALSE(NULL != g_sr_data->result_que, ESP_ERR_NO_MEM, err, "Failed create result queue");
   327→
   328→  g_sr_data->event_group = xEventGroupCreate();
   329→  ESP_GOTO_ON_FALSE(NULL != g_sr_data->event_group, ESP_ERR_NO_MEM, err, "Failed create event_group");
   330→
   331→  BaseType_t ret_val;
   332→  g_sr_data->user_cb = cb;
   333→  g_sr_data->user_cb_arg = cb_arg;
   334→  g_sr_data->fill_cb = fill_cb;
   335→  g_sr_data->fill_cb_arg = fill_cb_arg;
   336→  g_sr_data->i2s_rx_chan_num = rx_chan + 1;
   337→  g_sr_data->mode = mode;
   338→
   339→  // Init Model
   340→  log_d("init model");
   341→  models = esp_srmodel_init("model");
   342→
   343→  // Load WakeWord Detection
   344→  afe_config_t *afe_config = afe_config_init(input_format, models, AFE_TYPE_SR, AFE_MODE_LOW_COST);
   345→  g_sr_data->afe_handle = esp_afe_handle_from_config(afe_config);
   346→  log_d("load wakenet '%s'", afe_config->wakenet_model_name);
   347→  g_sr_data->afe_data = g_sr_data->afe_handle->create_from_config(afe_config);
   348→  afe_config_free(afe_config);
   349→
   350→  // Load Custom Command Detection
   351→  char *mn_name = esp_srmodel_filter(models, ESP_MN_PREFIX, ESP_MN_ENGLISH);
   352→  log_d("load multinet '%s'", mn_name);
   353→  g_sr_data->multinet = esp_mn_handle_from_name(mn_name);
   354→  log_d("load model_data '%s'", mn_name);
   355→  g_sr_data->model_data = g_sr_data->multinet->create(mn_name, 5760);
   356→
   357→  // Add commands
   358→  esp_mn_commands_alloc((esp_mn_iface_t *)g_sr_data->multinet, (model_iface_data_t *)g_sr_data->model_data);
   359→  log_i("add %d commands", cmd_number);
   360→  for (size_t i = 0; i < cmd_number; i++) {
   361→    esp_mn_commands_add(sr_commands[i].command_id, (char *)(sr_commands[i].phoneme));
   362→    log_i("  cmd[%d] phrase[%d]:'%s'", sr_commands[i].command_id, i, sr_commands[i].str);
   363→  }
   364→
   365→  // Load commands
   366→  esp_mn_error_t *err_id = esp_mn_commands_update();
   367→  if (err_id) {
   368→    for (int i = 0; i < err_id->num; i++) {
   369→      log_e("err cmd id:%d", err_id->phrases[i]->command_id);
   370→    }
   371→  }
   372→
   373→  //Start tasks
   374→  log_d("start tasks");
   375→  ret_val = xTaskCreatePinnedToCore(&audio_feed_task, "SR Feed Task", 4 * 1024, NULL, 5, &g_sr_data->feed_task, 0);
   376→  ESP_GOTO_ON_FALSE(pdPASS == ret_val, ESP_FAIL, err, "Failed create audio feed task");
   377→  vTaskDelay(10);
   378→  ret_val = xTaskCreatePinnedToCore(&audio_detect_task, "SR Detect Task", 8 * 1024, NULL, 5, &g_sr_data->detect_task, 1);
   379→  ESP_GOTO_ON_FALSE(pdPASS == ret_val, ESP_FAIL, err, "Failed create audio detect task");
   380→  ret_val = xTaskCreatePinnedToCore(&sr_handler_task, "SR Handler Task", 6 * 1024, NULL, configMAX_PRIORITIES - 1, &g_sr_data->handle_task, 1);
   381→  //ret_val = xTaskCreatePinnedToCore(&sr_handler_task, "SR Handler Task", 6 * 1024, NULL, configMAX_PRIORITIES - 1, &g_sr_data->handle_task, 0);
   382→  ESP_GOTO_ON_FALSE(pdPASS == ret_val, ESP_FAIL, err, "Failed create audio handler task");
   383→
   384→  return ESP_OK;
   385→err:
   386→  sr_stop();
   387→  return ret;
   388→}
   389→
   390→esp_err_t sr_stop(void) {
   391→  ESP_RETURN_ON_FALSE(NULL != g_sr_data, ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE, "SR is not running");
   392→
   393→  /**
   394→     * Waiting for all task stopped
   395→     * TODO: A task creation failure cannot be handled correctly now
   396→     * */
   397→  vTaskDelete(g_sr_data->handle_task);
   398→  xEventGroupSetBits(g_sr_data->event_group, NEED_DELETE);
   399→  xEventGroupWaitBits(g_sr_data->event_group, NEED_DELETE | FEED_DELETED | DETECT_DELETED, 1, 1, portMAX_DELAY);
   400→
   401→  if (g_sr_data->result_que) {
   402→    vQueueDelete(g_sr_data->result_que);
   403→    g_sr_data->result_que = NULL;
   404→  }
   405→
   406→  if (g_sr_data->event_group) {
   407→    vEventGroupDelete(g_sr_data->event_group);
   408→    g_sr_data->event_group = NULL;
   409→  }
   410→
   411→  if (g_sr_data->model_data) {
   412→    g_sr_data->multinet->destroy(g_sr_data->model_data);
   413→  }
   414→
   415→  if (g_sr_data->afe_data) {
   416→    g_sr_data->afe_handle->destroy(g_sr_data->afe_data);
   417→  }
   418→
   419→  if (g_sr_data->afe_in_buffer) {
   420→    heap_caps_free(g_sr_data->afe_in_buffer);
   421→  }
   422→
   423→  heap_caps_free(g_sr_data);
   424→  g_sr_data = NULL;
   425→  return ESP_OK;
   426→}
   427→
   428→esp_err_t sr_pause(void) {
   429→  ESP_RETURN_ON_FALSE(NULL != g_sr_data, ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE, "SR is not running");
   430→  xEventGroupSetBits(g_sr_data->event_group, PAUSE_FEED | PAUSE_DETECT);
   431→  return ESP_OK;
   432→}
   433→
   434→esp_err_t sr_resume(void) {
   435→  ESP_RETURN_ON_FALSE(NULL != g_sr_data, ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE, "SR is not running");
   436→  xEventGroupSetBits(g_sr_data->event_group, RESUME_FEED | RESUME_DETECT);
   437→  return ESP_OK;
   438→}

# ESP_SR Library Setup Guide for Arduino ESP32

## Partition Scheme Requirements

The ESP_SR library requires a **special "SR" partition table** to function properly. This is a critical setup step that must be configured before uploading sketches. Without this partition scheme, you'll encounter errors in the serial monitor.

## I2S Configuration

Based on the issue discussion, the working configuration for a single mono microphone (INMP441) is:

```cpp
i2s.begin(I2S_MODE_STD, 16000, I2S_DATA_BIT_WIDTH_16BIT, I2S_SLOT_MODE_MONO);
ESP_SR.begin(i2s, sr_commands, sizeof(sr_commands) / sizeof(sr_cmd_t), 
             SR_CHANNELS_MONO, SR_MODE_WAKEWORD);
```

**Key differences from stereo setup:**
- Use `I2S_SLOT_MODE_MONO` instead of stereo
- Use `SR_CHANNELS_MONO` in ESP_SR initialization
- Sample rate: 16000 Hz

## Wake Word

The default wake word is **"Hi ESP"**. This triggers the speech recognition system.

## Known Issues & Solutions

**Problem:** Sketch compiles but ESP_SR fails silently even with verbose debug output enabled.

**Solution:** Ensure the I2S configuration matches your microphone setup (mono vs. stereo). Reference the [esp-skainet examples](https://github.com/espressif/esp-skainet/tree/master/examples/en_speech_commands_recognition) for working configurations.

## Storage Requirements

The library requires substantial flash memory. Users with limited storage should consult alternative examples rather than the full Basic.ino sketch.

```ino
/*
 * ESP-SR Native Wakeword Test
 *
 * Tests "Hi ESP" wake word detection using Espressif's native speech recognition.
 * Requires: esp_sr_16 partition scheme + model flashed to partition.
 *
 * Wake word: "Hi ESP"
 * LED lights up on detection, then listens for commands.
 */

#include "ESP_I2S.h"
#include "ESP_SR.h"

// INMP441 Microphone Pins
#define I2S_PIN_BCK  2
#define I2S_PIN_WS   4
#define I2S_PIN_DIN  18

// LED for feedback
#define LED_PIN  1

// Input format: M = microphone channel, N = null/unused
#define SR_INPUT_FORMAT "MN"

I2SClass i2s;

// Voice commands (after wake word detected)
enum {
  SR_CMD_LIGHT_ON,
  SR_CMD_LIGHT_OFF,
};

static const sr_cmd_t sr_commands[] = {
  {SR_CMD_LIGHT_ON,  "Turn on the light", "TkN nN jc LiT"},
  {SR_CMD_LIGHT_OFF, "Turn off the light", "TkN eF jc LiT"},
};

void onSrEvent(sr_event_t event, int command_id, int phrase_id) {
  switch (event) {
    case SR_EVENT_WAKEWORD:
      Serial.println("\n>>> WAKEWORD DETECTED: Hi ESP <<<");
      digitalWrite(LED_PIN, HIGH);
      break;

    case SR_EVENT_WAKEWORD_CHANNEL:
      Serial.printf("Wake channel %d verified\n", command_id);
      ESP_SR.setMode(SR_MODE_COMMAND);
      break;

    case SR_EVENT_TIMEOUT:
      Serial.println("Command timeout - listening for wakeword...");
      digitalWrite(LED_PIN, LOW);
      ESP_SR.setMode(SR_MODE_WAKEWORD);
      break;

    case SR_EVENT_COMMAND:
      Serial.printf("COMMAND: %s\n", sr_commands[phrase_id].str);
      if (command_id == SR_CMD_LIGHT_ON) {
        Serial.println("-> Light ON");
      } else if (command_id == SR_CMD_LIGHT_OFF) {
        Serial.println("-> Light OFF");
        digitalWrite(LED_PIN, LOW);
      }
      ESP_SR.setMode(SR_MODE_COMMAND);  // Continue listening for commands
      break;

    default:
      Serial.printf("Unknown event: %d\n", event);
      break;
  }
}

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(115200);
  delay(1000);

  pinMode(LED_PIN, OUTPUT);
  digitalWrite(LED_PIN, LOW);

  Serial.println("\n=== ESP-SR Wakeword Test ===");
  Serial.println("Wake word: \"Hi ESP\"");
  Serial.println("Commands: \"Turn on the light\", \"Turn off the light\"\n");

  // Initialize I2S for mono INMP441 microphone
  i2s.setPins(I2S_PIN_BCK, I2S_PIN_WS, -1, I2S_PIN_DIN);
  i2s.setTimeout(1000);

  if (!i2s.begin(I2S_MODE_STD, 16000, I2S_DATA_BIT_WIDTH_16BIT, I2S_SLOT_MODE_MONO)) {
    Serial.println("ERROR: I2S init failed");
    errorBlink();
  }
  Serial.println("I2S: OK (16kHz mono)");

  // Initialize speech recognition
  ESP_SR.onEvent(onSrEvent);
  if (!ESP_SR.begin(i2s, sr_commands, sizeof(sr_commands) / sizeof(sr_cmd_t),
                    SR_CHANNELS_MONO, SR_MODE_WAKEWORD, SR_INPUT_FORMAT)) {
    Serial.println("ERROR: ESP_SR init failed");
    Serial.println("Check: Partition scheme = esp_sr_16");
    errorBlink();
  }
  Serial.println("ESP_SR: OK");

  Serial.println("\nListening for \"Hi ESP\"...");
  Serial.println("================================\n");
}

void loop() {
  delay(100);
}

void errorBlink() {
  while (1) {
    digitalWrite(LED_PIN, !digitalRead(LED_PIN));
    delay(200);
  }
}

```

```md
# ESP-SR Native Wakeword Test

Tests wake word detection using Espressif's native ESP-SR library.
Wake word: **"Hi ESP"** (built-in, optimized for ESP32-S3)

## Setup (IMPORTANT)

### 1. Select ESP_SR Partition Scheme

In Arduino IDE:
1. Go to **Tools > Partition Scheme**
2. Select: **"ESP SR 16M (3MB APP / 7MB SPIFFS / 2.9MB Model)"**

This partition includes a dedicated `model` partition for speech recognition models.

### 2. Flash the Speech Recognition Model

The model file is pre-installed with Arduino ESP32:
\```
~/.arduino15/packages/esp32/tools/esp32-arduino-libs/idf-release_v5.5-07e9bf49-v1/esp32s3/esp_sr/srmodels.bin
\```

Flash it to the model partition (offset 0xD10000):
\```bash
esptool.py --chip esp32s3 --port /dev/ttyACM0 --baud 921600 \
  write_flash 0xD10000 \
  ~/.arduino15/packages/esp32/tools/esp32-arduino-libs/idf-release_v5.5-07e9bf49-v1/esp32s3/esp_sr/srmodels.bin
\```

### 3. Upload Sketch

Upload the sketch via Arduino IDE. Ensure partition scheme is correct.

## Usage

1. Open Serial Monitor (115200 baud)
2. Say **"Hi ESP"** clearly
3. LED turns ON when wake word detected
4. After wake word, say a command:
   - "Turn on the light"
   - "Turn off the light"
5. After timeout (no command), returns to wake word listening

## Expected Output

\```
=== ESP-SR Wakeword Test ===
Wake word: "Hi ESP"
Commands: "Turn on the light", "Turn off the light"

I2S: OK (16kHz mono)
ESP_SR: OK

Listening for "Hi ESP"...
================================

>>> WAKEWORD DETECTED: Hi ESP <<<
Wake channel 0 verified
COMMAND: Turn on the light
-> Light ON
Command timeout - listening for wakeword...
\```

## LED Feedback

- **OFF** - Listening for wake word
- **ON** - Wake word detected, listening for commands
- **Blinking** - Error during initialization

## Troubleshooting

### "ESP_SR init failed"
- Wrong partition scheme selected
- Model not flashed to partition
- Check serial output for specific error

### No wake word detection
- Speak clearly, closer to microphone
- Check I2S pins match your hardware
- Verify microphone is working (test with mic_test sketch)

### "model partition not found"
- Re-select esp_sr_16 partition scheme
- Verify model was flashed to correct offset (0xD10000)

## Hardware

- **Microphone**: INMP441 (GPIO 2=BCK, 4=WS, 18=DIN)
- **LED**: GPIO 1
- **Sample rate**: 16kHz mono

## Technical Details

- Uses Espressif's WakeNet neural network model
- Model size: ~2.4MB (pre-trained "Hi ESP")
- Includes MultiNet for command recognition
- Runs on ESP32-S3's neural network accelerator

## Sources

- [ESP-SR Documentation](https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-sr/en/latest/esp32s3/getting_started/readme.html)
- [Arduino ESP32 Issue #9820](https://github.com/espressif/arduino-esp32/issues/9820)

#!/bin/bash
# Flash ESP-SR model to ESP32-S3
# Run this ONCE before uploading the sketch

MODEL_PATH="$HOME/.arduino15/packages/esp32/tools/esp32-arduino-libs/idf-release_v5.5-07e9bf49-v1/esp32s3/esp_sr/srmodels.bin"
PORT="${1:-/dev/ttyACM0}"
OFFSET="0xD10000"

if [ ! -f "$MODEL_PATH" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: Model file not found: $MODEL_PATH"
    echo "Make sure Arduino ESP32 3.x is installed"
    exit 1
fi

echo "Flashing ESP-SR model (2.4MB)..."
echo "  Model: $MODEL_PATH"
echo "  Port:  $PORT"
echo "  Offset: $OFFSET"
echo ""

esptool.py --chip esp32s3 --port "$PORT" --baud 921600 \
    write_flash "$OFFSET" "$MODEL_PATH"

echo ""
echo "Done! Now upload the sketch with esp_sr_16 partition scheme."

```

## Summary

I researched the options you mentioned and created a new test sketch using Espressif's native ESP-SR library.

### Research Findings

**klumw/wakeword repo**: Uses ESP-IDF (not Arduino) + Edge Impulse for "computer" wake word. Not suitable since you need Arduino framework.

**Native ESP-SR** (recommended): Already included in Arduino ESP32 3.3.2 with:
- Built-in "Hi ESP" wake word (optimized for ESP32-S3)
- 2.4MB pre-trained model (`srmodels.bin`)
- Simple Arduino API
- Runs on ESP32-S3's neural network accelerator

### Created Files

**`workbench/tests/wakeword_esp_sr_test/`**:
- `wakeword_esp_sr_test.ino` - Test sketch using mono INMP441 config
- `README.md` - Setup instructions
- `flash_model.sh` - Helper script to flash model

### Setup Steps

1. **Select partition**: Tools > Partition Scheme > **"ESP SR 16M"**

2. **Flash the model** (once):
   ```bash
   ./flash_model.sh /dev/ttyACM0
   ```
   This flashes the 2.4MB `srmodels.bin` to offset 0xD10000

3. **Upload sketch** via Arduino IDE

4. **Test**: Say "Hi ESP" - LED should turn on

### Key Differences from Previous Test

| Previous (micro_speech) | New (ESP-SR) |
|------------------------|--------------|
| TFLite yes/no classifier | Native wake word detector |
| Simplified spectrogram | Full AFE preprocessing |
| ~18KB model | ~2.4MB optimized model |
| Buggy detection | Espressif-optimized |

The ESP-SR approach uses Espressif's production-grade speech recognition with proper noise cancellation and audio front-end processing, which should be much more reliable than the buggy yes/no classifier.

Sources:
- [ESP-SR Documentation](https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-sr/en/latest/esp32s3/getting_started/readme.html)
- [Arduino ESP32 Issue #9820](https://github.com/espressif/arduino-esp32/issues/9820)

     1→![microWakeWord logo](etc/logo.png)
     2→
     3→microWakeWord is an open-source wakeword library for detecting custom wake words on low power devices. It produces models that are suitable for using [TensorFlow Lite for Microcontrollers](https://www.tensorflow.org/lite/microcontrollers). The models are suitable for real-world usage with low false accept and false reject rates.
     4→
     5→[![A library from the Open Home Foundation](https://www.openhomefoundation.org/badges/ohf-library.png)](https://www.openhomefoundation.org/)
     6→
     7→**microWakeword is currently available as an early release. Training new models is intended for advanced users. Training a model that works well is still very difficult, as it typically requires experimentation with hyperparameters and sample generation settings. Please share any insights you find for training a good model!**
     8→
     9→## Detection Process
    10→
    11→We detect the wake word in two stages. Raw audio data is processed into 40 spectrogram features every 10 ms. The streaming inference model uses the newest slice of feature data as input and returns a probability that the wake word is said. If the model consistently predicts the wake word over multiple windows, then we predict that the wake word has been said.
    12→
    13→The first stage processes the raw monochannel audio data at a sample rate of 16 kHz via the [micro_speech preprocessor](https://github.com/tensorflow/tflite-micro/tree/main/tensorflow/lite/micro/examples/micro_speech). The preprocessor generates 40 features over 30 ms (the window duration) of audio data. The preprocessor generates these features every 10 ms (the stride duration), so the first 20 ms of audio data is part of the previous window. This process is similar to calculating a Mel spectrogram for the audio data, but it includes noise supression and automatic gain control. This makes it suitable for devices with limited processing power. See the linked TFLite Micro example for full details on how the audio is processed.
    14→
    15→The streaming model performs inferences every 30 ms, where the initial convolution layer strides over three 10 ms slices of audio. The model is a neural network using [MixConv](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.09595) mixed depthwise convolutions suitable for streaming. Streaming and training the model uses heavily modified open-sourced code from [Google Research](https://github.com/google-research/google-research/tree/master/kws_streaming) found in the paper [Streaming Keyword Spotting on Mobile Devices](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2005.06720.pdf) by Rykabov, Kononenko, Subrahmanya, Visontai, and Laurenzo.
    16→
    17→### Training Process
    18→- We augment the spectrograms in several possible ways during training:
    19→    - [SpecAugment](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1904.08779.pdf) masks time and frequency features
    20→- The best weights are chosen as a two-step process:
    21→    1. The top priority is minimizing a specific metric like the false accepts per hour on ambient background noise first.
    22→    2. If the specified minimization target metric is met, then we maximize a different specified metric like accuracy.
    23→- Validation and test sets are split into two portions:
    24→    1. The ``validation`` and ``testing`` sets include the positive and negative generated samples.
    25→    2. The ``validation_ambient`` and ``testing_ambient`` sets are all negative samples representing real-world background sounds; e.g., music, random household noises, and general speech/conversations.
    26→- Generated spectrograms are stored as [Ragged Mmap](https://github.com/hristo-vrigazov/mmap.ninja/tree/master) folders for quick loading from the disk while training.
    27→- Each feature set is configured with a ``sampling_weight`` and ``penalty_weight``. The ``sampling_weight`` parameter controls oversampling and ``penalty_weight`` controls the weight of incorrect predictions.
    28→- Class weights are also adjustable with the ``positive_class_weight`` and ``negative_class_weight`` parameters. It is useful to increase the ``negative_class_weight`` to reduce the amount of false acceptances.
    29→- We train the model in a non-streaming mode; i.e., it trains on the entire spectrogram. When finished, this is converted to a streaming model that updates on only the newest spectrogram features.
    30→    - Not padding the convolutions ensures the non-streaming and streaming models have nearly identical prediction behaviors.
    31→    - We estimate the false accepts per hour metric during training by splitting long-duration ambient clips into appropriate-sized spectrograms with a 100 ms stride to simulate the streaming model. This is not a perfect estimate of the streaming model's real-world false accepts per hour, but it is sufficient for determining the best weights.
    32→- We should generate spectrogram features over a longer time period than needed for training the model. The preprocessor model applies PCAN and noise reduction, and generating features over a longer time period results in models that are better to generalize.
    33→- We quantize the streaming models to increase performance on low-power devices. This has a small performance penalty that varies from model to model, but there is typically no reduction in accuracy.
    34→
    35→
    36→## Model Training Process
    37→
    38→We generate samples using [Piper sample generator](https://github.com/rhasspy/piper-sample-generator).
    39→
    40→The generated samples are augmented before or during training to increase variability. There are pre-generated spectrogram features for various negative datasets available on [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/kahrendt/microwakeword).
    41→
    42→Please see the ``basic_training_notebook.ipynb`` notebook to see how a model is trained. This notebook will produce a model, but it will most likely not be usable! Training a usable model requires a lot of experimentation, and that notebook is meant to serve only as a starting point for advanced users.
    43→
    44→## Models
    45→
    46→See https://github.com/esphome/micro-wake-word-models to download the currently available models.
    47→
    48→## Acknowledgements
    49→
    50→I am very thankful for many people's support to help improve this! Thank you, in particular, to the following individuals and organizations for providing feedback, collaboration, and developmental support:
    51→

    54→  - [jesserockz](https://github.com/jesserockz)

    58→  - [Nabu Casa](https://github.com/NabuCasa)
    59→  - [Open Home Foundation](https://www.openhomefoundation.org/)
    60→

    20→import numpy as np
    21→import tensorflow as tf
    22→from microwakeword.audio.audio_utils import generate_features_for_clip
    23→
    24→
    25→class Model:
    26→    """
    27→    Class for loading and running tflite microwakeword models
    28→
    29→    Args:
    30→        tflite_model_path (str): Path to tflite model file.
    31→        stride (int | None, optional): Time dimension's stride. If None, then the stride is the input tensor's time dimension. Defaults to None.
    32→    """
    33→
    34→    def __init__(self, tflite_model_path: str, stride: int | None = None):
    35→        # Load tflite model
    36→        interpreter = tf.lite.Interpreter(
    37→            model_path=tflite_model_path,
    38→        )
    39→        interpreter.allocate_tensors()
    40→
    41→        self.input_details = interpreter.get_input_details()
    42→        self.output_details = interpreter.get_output_details()
    43→
    44→        self.is_quantized_model = self.input_details[0]["dtype"] == np.int8
    45→        self.input_feature_slices = self.input_details[0]["shape"][1]
    46→
    47→        if stride is None:
    48→            self.stride = self.input_feature_slices
    49→        else:
    50→            self.stride = stride
    51→
    52→        for s in range(len(self.input_details)):
    53→            if self.is_quantized_model:
    54→                interpreter.set_tensor(
    55→                    self.input_details[s]["index"],
    56→                    np.zeros(self.input_details[s]["shape"], dtype=np.int8),
    57→                )
    58→            else:
    59→                interpreter.set_tensor(
    60→                    self.input_details[s]["index"],
    61→                    np.zeros(self.input_details[s]["shape"], dtype=np.float32),
    62→                )
    63→
    64→        self.model = interpreter

    66→    def predict_clip(self, data: np.ndarray, step_ms: int = 20):
    67→        """Run the model on a single clip of audio data
    68→
    69→        Args:
    70→            data (numpy.ndarray): input data for the model (16 khz, 16-bit PCM audio data)
    71→            step_ms (int): The window step sized used for generating the spectrogram in ms. Defaults to 20.
    72→
    73→        Returns:
    74→            list: model predictions for the input audio data
    75→        """
    76→
    77→        # Get the spectrogram
    78→        spectrogram = generate_features_for_clip(data, step_ms=step_ms)
    79→
    80→        return self.predict_spectrogram(spectrogram)

    82→    def predict_spectrogram(self, spectrogram: np.ndarray):

    84→
    85→        Args:

    87→

   102→        ):

   104→            if len(chunk) == self.input_feature_slices:
   105→                chunks.append(chunk)

   117→            self.model.invoke()
   118→
   119→            output = self.model.get_tensor(self.output_details[0]["index"])[0][0]
   120→            if self.is_quantized_model:
   121→                output = self.dequantize_output_data(output, self.output_details[0])
   122→
   123→            predictions.append(output)
   124→
   125→        return predictions
   126→
   127→    def quantize_input_data(self, data: np.ndarray, input_details: dict) -> np.ndarray:
   128→        """quantize the input data using scale and zero point
   129→
   130→        Args:
   131→            data (numpy.array in float): input data for the interpreter
   132→            input_details (dict): output of get_input_details from the tflm interpreter.
   133→
   134→        Returns:
   135→          numpy.ndarray: quantized data as int8 dtype
   136→        """
   137→        # Get input quantization parameters
   138→        data_type = input_details["dtype"]
   139→
   140→        input_quantization_parameters = input_details["quantization_parameters"]
   141→        input_scale, input_zero_point = (
   142→            input_quantization_parameters["scales"][0],
   143→            input_quantization_parameters["zero_points"][0],
   144→        )
   145→        # quantize the input data
   146→        data = data / input_scale + input_zero_point
   147→        return data.astype(data_type)
   148→
   149→    def dequantize_output_data(
   150→        self, data: np.ndarray, output_details: dict
   151→    ) -> np.ndarray:
   152→        """Dequantize the model output
   153→
   154→        Args:
   155→            data (numpy.ndarray): integer data to be dequantized
   156→            output_details (dict): TFLM interpreter model output details
   157→
   158→        Returns:
   159→            numpy.ndarray: dequantized data as float32 dtype
   160→        """
   161→        output_quantization_parameters = output_details["quantization_parameters"]
   162→        output_scale = 255.0  # assume (u)int8 quantization
   163→        output_zero_point = output_quantization_parameters["zero_points"][0]
   164→        # Caveat: tflm_output_quant need to be converted to float to avoid integer
   165→        # overflow during dequantization
   166→        # e.g., (tflm_output_quant -output_zero_point) and
   167→        # (tflm_output_quant + (-output_zero_point))
   168→        # can produce different results (int8 calculation)
   169→        # return output_scale * (data.astype(np.float32) - output_zero_point)
   170→        return 1 / output_scale * (data.astype(np.float32) - output_zero_point)
   171→

    23→class SpectrogramGeneration:
    24→    """A class that handles generating spectrogram features for audio clips. Spectrograms can optionally be split into nonoverlapping segments for faster file loading or they can optionally be strided by dropping the last feature windows to simulate a streaming model's sequential inputs.
    25→
    26→    Args:
    27→        clips (Clips): Object that retrieves audio clips.
    28→        augmenter (Augmentation | None, optional): Object that augments audio clips. If None, no augmentations are applied. Defaults to None.
    29→        step_ms (int, optional): The window step size in ms for the spectrogram features. Defaults to 20.
    30→        split_spectrogram_duration_s (float | None, optional): Splits generated spectrograms to yield nonoverlapping spectrograms with this duration. If None, the entire spectrogram is yielded. Defaults to None.
    31→        slide_frames (int | None, optional): Strides the generated spectrograms to yield `slide_frames` overlapping spectrogram by removing features at the end of the spectrogram. If None, the entire spectrogram is yielded. Defaults to None.
    32→    """
    33→
    34→    def __init__(
    35→        self,
    36→        clips: Clips,
    37→        augmenter: Augmentation | None = None,
    38→        step_ms: int = 20,
    39→        split_spectrogram_duration_s: float | None = None,
    40→        slide_frames: int | None = None,
    41→    ):
    42→
    43→        self.clips = clips
    44→        self.augmenter = augmenter
    45→        self.step_ms = step_ms
    46→        self.split_spectrogram_duration_s = split_spectrogram_duration_s
    47→        self.slide_frames = slide_frames
    48→
    49→    def get_random_spectrogram(self):
    50→        """Retrieves a random audio clip's spectrogram that is optionally augmented.
    51→
    52→        Returns:
    53→            numpy.ndarry: 2D spectrogram array for the random (augmented) audio clip.
    54→        """
    55→        clip = self.clips.get_random_clip()
    56→        if self.augmenter is not None:
    57→            clip = self.augmenter.augment_clip(clip)
    58→
    59→        return generate_features_for_clip(clip, self.step_ms)
    60→
    61→    def spectrogram_generator(self, random=False, max_clips=None, **kwargs):
    62→        """A Python generator that retrieves (augmented) spectrograms.
    63→
    64→        Args:
    65→            random (bool, optional): Specifies if the source audio clips should be chosen randomly. Defaults to False.
    66→            kwargs: Parameters to pass to the clips audio generator.
    67→
    68→        Yields:
    69→            numpy.ndarry: 2D spectrogram array for the random (augmented) audio clip.
    70→        """
    71→        if random:
    72→            if max_clips is not None:
    73→                clip_generator = self.clips.random_audio_generator(max_clips=max_clips)
    74→            else:
    75→                clip_generator = self.clips.random_audio_generator()
    76→        else:
    77→            clip_generator = self.clips.audio_generator(**kwargs)
    78→
    79→        if self.augmenter is not None:
    80→            augmented_generator = self.augmenter.augment_generator(clip_generator)
    81→        else:
    82→            augmented_generator = clip_generator
    83→
    84→        for augmented_clip in augmented_generator:
    85→            spectrogram = generate_features_for_clip(augmented_clip, self.step_ms)
    86→
    87→            if self.split_spectrogram_duration_s is not None:
    88→                # Splits the resulting spectrogram into non-overlapping spectrograms. The features from the first 20 feature windows are dropped.
    89→                desired_spectrogram_length = int(
    90→                    self.split_spectrogram_duration_s / (self.step_ms / 1000)
    91→                )
    92→
    93→                if spectrogram.shape[0] > desired_spectrogram_length + 20:
    94→                    slided_spectrograms = np.lib.stride_tricks.sliding_window_view(
    95→                        spectrogram,
    96→                        window_shape=(desired_spectrogram_length, spectrogram.shape[1]),
    97→                    )[20::desired_spectrogram_length, ...]
    98→
    99→                    for i in range(slided_spectrograms.shape[0]):
   100→                        yield np.squeeze(slided_spectrograms[i])
   101→                else:
   102→                    yield spectrogram
   103→            elif self.slide_frames is not None:
   104→                # Generates self.slide_frames spectrograms by shifting over the already generated spectrogram
   105→                spectrogram_length = spectrogram.shape[0] - self.slide_frames + 1

   108→                    spectrogram, window_shape=(spectrogram_length, spectrogram.shape[1])
   109→                )
   110→                for i in range(self.slide_frames):
   111→                    yield np.squeeze(slided_spectrograms[i])
   112→            else:

    23→from scipy.io import wavfile

    25→from pymicro_features import MicroFrontend

    27→
    28→def generate_features_for_clip(
    29→    audio_samples: np.ndarray, step_ms: int = 20, use_c: bool = True
    30→):
    31→    """Generates spectrogram features for the given audio data.
    32→
    33→    Args:
    34→        audio_samples (numpy.ndarray): The clip's audio samples.
    35→        step_ms (int, optional): The window step size in ms. Defaults to 20.
    36→        use_c (bool, optional): Whether to use the C implementation of the microfrontend via pymicro-features. Defaults to True.
    37→
    38→    Raises:
    39→        ValueError: If the provided audio data is not a 16-bit integer array.
    40→
    41→
    42→    Returns:
    43→        numpy.ndarray: The spectrogram features for the provided audio clip.
    44→    """
    45→
    46→    # Convert any float formatted audio data to an int16 array
    47→    if audio_samples.dtype in (np.float32, np.float64):
    48→        audio_samples = np.clip((audio_samples * 32768), -32768, 32767).astype(np.int16)
    49→
    50→    if use_c:
    51→        audio_samples = audio_samples.tobytes()
    52→        micro_frontend = MicroFrontend()
    53→        features = []
    54→        audio_idx = 0
    55→        num_audio_bytes = len(audio_samples)
    56→        while audio_idx + 160 * 2 < num_audio_bytes:
    57→            frontend_result = micro_frontend.ProcessSamples(
    58→                audio_samples[audio_idx : audio_idx + 160 * 2]
    59→            )
    60→            audio_idx += frontend_result.samples_read * 2
    61→            if frontend_result.features:
    62→                features.append(frontend_result.features)
    63→
    64→        return np.array(features).astype(np.float32)
    65→
    66→    with tf.device("/cpu:0"):
    67→        # The default settings match the TFLM preprocessor settings.
    68→        # Preproccesor model is available from the tflite-micro repository, accessed December 2023.
    69→        micro_frontend = frontend_op.audio_microfrontend(
    70→            tf.convert_to_tensor(audio_samples),
    71→            sample_rate=16000,
    72→            window_size=30,
    73→            window_step=step_ms,
    74→            num_channels=40,
    75→            upper_band_limit=7500,
    76→            lower_band_limit=125,
    77→            enable_pcan=True,
    78→            min_signal_remaining=0.05,
    79→            out_scale=1,
    80→            out_type=tf.uint16,
    81→        )
    82→
    83→        spectrogram = micro_frontend.numpy()
    84→        return spectrogram

    87→def save_clip(audio_samples: np.ndarray, output_file: str) -> None:
    88→    """Saves an audio clip's sample as a wave file.
    89→
    90→    Args:
    91→        audio_samples (numpy.ndarray): The clip's audio samples.
    92→        output_file (str): Path to the desired output file.
    93→    """
    94→    if audio_samples.dtype in (np.float32, np.float64):
    95→        audio_samples = (audio_samples * 32767).astype(np.int16)
    96→    wavfile.write(output_file, 16000, audio_samples)
    97→
    98→
    99→def remove_silence_webrtc(
   100→    audio_data: np.ndarray,
   101→    frame_duration: float = 0.030,
   102→    sample_rate: int = 16000,
   103→    min_start: int = 2000,
   104→) -> np.ndarray:
   105→    """Uses webrtc voice activity detection to remove silence from the clips
   106→
   107→    Args:
   108→        audio_data (numpy.ndarray): The input clip's audio samples.
   109→        frame_duration (float): The frame_duration for webrtcvad. Defaults to 0.03.
   110→        sample_rate (int): The audio's sample rate. Defaults to 16000.
   111→        min_start: (int): The number of audio samples from the start of the clip to always include. Defaults to 2000.
   112→
   113→    Returns:
   114→        numpy.ndarray: Array with the trimmed audio clip's samples.
   115→    """
   116→    vad = webrtcvad.Vad(0)
   117→
   118→    # webrtcvad expects int16 arrays as input, so convert if audio_data is a float
   119→    float_type = audio_data.dtype in (np.float32, np.float64)
   120→    if float_type:
   121→        audio_data = (audio_data * 32767).astype(np.int16)
   122→
   123→    filtered_audio = audio_data[0:min_start].tolist()
   124→
   125→    step_size = int(sample_rate * frame_duration)
   126→
   127→    for i in range(min_start, audio_data.shape[0] - step_size, step_size):
   128→        vad_detected = vad.is_speech(
   129→            audio_data[i : i + step_size].tobytes(), sample_rate
   130→        )
   131→        if vad_detected:
   132→            # If voice activity is detected, add it to filtered_audio
   133→            filtered_audio.extend(audio_data[i : i + step_size].tolist())
   134→
   135→    # If the original audio data was a float array, convert back
   136→    if float_type:
   137→        trimmed_audio = np.array(filtered_audio)
   138→        return np.array(trimmed_audio / 32767).astype(np.float32)
   139→
   140→    return np.array(filtered_audio).astype(np.int16)
   141→

## Overview

This component implements wake word detection on the ESPHome device itself.(no content)Wake word detection is done entirely with TensorFlow Lite Micro.

## Audio Preprocessing Details

The preprocessor generates 40 features over 30 ms (the window duration) of audio data. The preprocessor generates these features every 20 ms (the stride duration), so the first 10 ms of audio data is part of the previous window.(no content)This process is similar to calculating a Mel spectrogram for the audio data, but it is lightweight for devices with limited processing power. See the linked TFLite Micro example for full details on how the audio is processed.

## Model Architecture & Performance

The streaming model performs inferences every 20 ms on the newest audio stride. The model is based on an inception neural network converted for streaming. It executes an inference in under 10 ms on an ESP32-S3, much faster than the 20 ms stride length.(no content)Streaming and training the model uses modified open-sourced code from Google Research found in the paper "Streaming Keyword Spotting on Mobile Devices" by Rykabov, Kononenko, Subrahmanya, Visontai, and Laurenzo.

## 2024.7 Updates

These models require a new version of the micro_wake_word component in ESPHome as they use a 10 ms step size instead of the original 20 ms. It should be available in the ESPHome's 2024.7 release.(no content)These models are faster and more accurate. Up to 3 models can run on a regular ESP32 at the same time (e.g., VAD, "okay nabu", and "hey mycroft"). ESP32-S3 supports running all 4 concurrently.

## Target Hardware

The target devices are ESP32-S3 based with external PSRAM. It may run on a regular ESP32 but may not perform as well.

## Development Background

Kevin Ahrendt has written microWakeWord to develop streaming wake word models suitable for ESP32-S3 devices. He heavily adapted the project from Google Research's code. It currently uses an Inception based model.

The key repositories for the C++ implementation are:
- **GitHub**: kahrendt/esphome-on-device-wake-word
- **GitHub**: OHF-Voice/micro-wake-word (for training framework)

# C++ Implementation for Wake Word Detection on ESP32-S3

Based on the repository documentation, here's what the implementation involves:

## Audio Preprocessing

The system uses the **TensorFlow Lite Micro speech preprocessor**, which processes audio at **16 kHz sample rate** and generates **40 features every 20 ms**. According to the README: "The preprocessor generates 40 features over 30 ms (the window duration) of audio data. The preprocessor generates these features every 20 ms (the stride duration)."

This approach mimics Mel spectrogram calculation but remains lightweight for resource-constrained devices.

## Core Libraries

- **TensorFlow Lite Micro** - primary inference engine for wake word detection
- **Espressif ESP-TFLite-Micro** - ESP32-optimized implementation
- Google Research's **KWS Streaming framework** - based on their "Streaming Keyword Spotting on Mobile Devices" paper

## Model Architecture

The system employs a "streaming inference model" based on an inception neural network adapted for streaming. The model executes inferences under 10 milliseconds on ESP32-S3, substantially faster than the 20 ms stride.

## Integration Pattern

The component detects the wake word in two stages: feature extraction, then streaming model inference. When the model consistently predicts the target phrase across multiple windows, the assist pipeline activates.

**Note:** The repository is archived; active development continues in the [microWakeWord repository](https://github.com/kahrendt/microWakeWord) and ESPHome 2024.2+.

# Micro Wake Word Technical Implementation

## Model Architecture
The system uses **TFLite (TensorFlow Lite)** trained models for wake word detection. As stated in the documentation, models are specified as `"stream_state_internal_quant.tflite"` files, indicating quantized neural networks optimized for embedded systems.

## Feature Generation Parameters
Key audio processing specifications include:

- **Feature Step Size**: 10 milliseconds (spectrogram generation stride)
- **Tensor Arena Size**: Minimum 22,860 bytes for model inference memory
- **Audio Input**: Configurable microphone source with adjustable gain factor

## Detection Thresholds & Sliding Window

The detection mechanism employs probability-based filtering:

- **Probability Cutoff**: Default 0.97 (97%) - wake words below this confidence are rejected
- **Sliding Window Size**: Default value of 5 - "Wake words average all probabilities in the sliding window"
- **VAD (Voice Activity Detection)**: Uses maximum probability across the window, reducing false positives from non-speech sounds

## Configuration Example

```yaml
micro_wake_word:
  microphone:
    channels: 0
    gain_factor: 4
  models:
    - model: okay_nabu
      probability_cutoff: 0.97
      sliding_window_size: 5
  vad:
    probability_cutoff: 0.5
```

## Process Flow

Detection operates as: audio input → spectrogram features (10ms steps) → TFLite inference → probability averaging (5-frame window) → threshold comparison → wake word trigger.
```

<cell id="cell-0"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type># Training a microWakeWord Model

This notebook steps you through training a basic microWakeWord model. It is intended as a **starting point** for advanced users. You should use Python 3.10.

**The model generated will most likely not be usable for everyday use; it may be difficult to trigger or falsely activates too frequently. You will most likely have to experiment with many different settings to obtain a decent model!**

In the comment at the start of certain blocks, I note some specific settings to consider modifying.

This runs on Google Colab, but is extremely slow compared to training on a local GPU. If you must use Colab, be sure to Change the runtime type to a GPU. Even then, it still slow!

At the end of this notebook, you will be able to download a tflite file. To use this in ESPHome, you need to write a model manifest JSON file. See the [ESPHome documentation](https://esphome.io/components/micro_wake_word) for the details and the [model repo](https://github.com/esphome/micro-wake-word-models/tree/main/models/v2) for examples.</cell id="cell-0">
