<cell id="cell-4"># Downloads audio data for augmentation. This can be slow!
# Borrowed from openWakeWord's automatic_model_training.ipynb, accessed March 4, 2024
#
# **Important note!** The data downloaded here has a mixture of difference
# licenses and usage restrictions. As such, any custom models trained with this
# data should be considered as appropriate for **non-commercial** personal use only.


import datasets
import scipy
import os

import numpy as np

from pathlib import Path
from tqdm import tqdm

## Download MIR RIR data

output_dir = "./mit_rirs"
if not os.path.exists(output_dir):
    os.mkdir(output_dir)
    rir_dataset = datasets.load_dataset("davidscripka/MIT_environmental_impulse_responses", split="train", streaming=True)
    # Save clips to 16-bit PCM wav files
    for row in tqdm(rir_dataset):
        name = row['audio']['path'].split('/')[-1]
        scipy.io.wavfile.write(os.path.join(output_dir, name), 16000, (row['audio']['array']*32767).astype(np.int16))

## Download noise and background audio

# Audioset Dataset (https://research.google.com/audioset/dataset/index.html)
# Download one part of the audioset .tar files, extract, and convert to 16khz
# For full-scale training, it's recommended to download the entire dataset from
# https://huggingface.co/datasets/agkphysics/AudioSet, and
# even potentially combine it with other background noise datasets (e.g., FSD50k, Freesound, etc.)

if not os.path.exists("audioset"):
    os.mkdir("audioset")

    fname = "bal_train09.tar"
    out_dir = f"audioset/{fname}"
    link = "https://huggingface.co/datasets/agkphysics/AudioSet/resolve/main/data/" + fname
    !wget -O {out_dir} {link}
    !cd audioset && tar -xf bal_train09.tar

    output_dir = "./audioset_16k"
    if not os.path.exists(output_dir):
        os.mkdir(output_dir)

    # Save clips to 16-bit PCM wav files
    audioset_dataset = datasets.Dataset.from_dict({"audio": [str(i) for i in Path("audioset/audio").glob("**/*.flac")]})
    audioset_dataset = audioset_dataset.cast_column("audio", datasets.Audio(sampling_rate=16000))
    for row in tqdm(audioset_dataset):
        name = row['audio']['path'].split('/')[-1].replace(".flac", ".wav")
        scipy.io.wavfile.write(os.path.join(output_dir, name), 16000, (row['audio']['array']*32767).astype(np.int16))

# Free Music Archive dataset
# https://github.com/mdeff/fma
# (Third-party mchl914 extra small set)

output_dir = "./fma"
if not os.path.exists(output_dir):
    os.mkdir(output_dir)
    fname = "fma_xs.zip"
    link = "https://huggingface.co/datasets/mchl914/fma_xsmall/resolve/main/" + fname
    out_dir = f"fma/{fname}"
    !wget -O {out_dir} {link}
    !cd {output_dir} && unzip -q {fname}

    output_dir = "./fma_16k"
    if not os.path.exists(output_dir):
        os.mkdir(output_dir)

    # Save clips to 16-bit PCM wav files
    fma_dataset = datasets.Dataset.from_dict({"audio": [str(i) for i in Path("fma/fma_small").glob("**/*.mp3")]})
    fma_dataset = fma_dataset.cast_column("audio", datasets.Audio(sampling_rate=16000))
    for row in tqdm(fma_dataset):
        name = row['audio']['path'].split('/')[-1].replace(".mp3", ".wav")
        scipy.io.wavfile.write(os.path.join(output_dir, name), 16000, (row['audio']['array']*32767).astype(np.int16))
</cell id="cell-4">
<cell id="cell-5"># Sets up the augmentations.
# To improve your model, experiment with these settings and use more sources of
# background clips.

from microwakeword.audio.augmentation import Augmentation
from microwakeword.audio.clips import Clips
from microwakeword.audio.spectrograms import SpectrogramGeneration

clips = Clips(input_directory='generated_samples',
              file_pattern='*.wav',
              max_clip_duration_s=None,
              remove_silence=False,
              random_split_seed=10,
              split_count=0.1,
              )
augmenter = Augmentation(augmentation_duration_s=3.2,
                         augmentation_probabilities = {
                                "SevenBandParametricEQ": 0.1,
                                "TanhDistortion": 0.1,
                                "PitchShift": 0.1,
                                "BandStopFilter": 0.1,
                                "AddColorNoise": 0.1,
                                "AddBackgroundNoise": 0.75,
                                "Gain": 1.0,
                                "RIR": 0.5,
                            },
                         impulse_paths = ['mit_rirs'],
                         background_paths = ['fma_16k', 'audioset_16k'],
                         background_min_snr_db = -5,
                         background_max_snr_db = 10,
                         min_jitter_s = 0.195,
                         max_jitter_s = 0.205,
                         )
</cell id="cell-5">
<cell id="cell-6"># Augment a random clip and play it back to verify it works well

from IPython.display import Audio
from microwakeword.audio.audio_utils import save_clip

random_clip = clips.get_random_clip()
augmented_clip = augmenter.augment_clip(random_clip)
save_clip(augmented_clip, 'augmented_clip.wav')

Audio("augmented_clip.wav", autoplay=True)</cell id="cell-6">
<cell id="cell-7"># Augment samples and save the training, validation, and testing sets.
# Validating and testing samples generated the same way can make the model
# benchmark better than it performs in real-word use. Use real samples or TTS
# samples generated with a different TTS engine to potentially get more accurate
# benchmarks.

import os
from mmap_ninja.ragged import RaggedMmap

output_dir = 'generated_augmented_features'

if not os.path.exists(output_dir):
    os.mkdir(output_dir)

splits = ["training", "validation", "testing"]
for split in splits:
  out_dir = os.path.join(output_dir, split)
  if not os.path.exists(out_dir):
      os.mkdir(out_dir)


  split_name = "train"
  repetition = 2

  spectrograms = SpectrogramGeneration(clips=clips,
                                     augmenter=augmenter,
                                     slide_frames=10,    # Uses the same spectrogram repeatedly, just shifted over by one frame. This simulates the streaming inferences while training/validating in nonstreaming mode.
                                     step_ms=10,
                                     )
  if split == "validation":
    split_name = "validation"
    repetition = 1
  elif split == "testing":
    split_name = "test"
    repetition = 1
    spectrograms = SpectrogramGeneration(clips=clips,
                                     augmenter=augmenter,
                                     slide_frames=1,    # The testing set uses the streaming version of the model, so no artificial repetition is necessary
                                     step_ms=10,
                                     )

  RaggedMmap.from_generator(
      out_dir=os.path.join(out_dir, 'wakeword_mmap'),
      sample_generator=spectrograms.spectrogram_generator(split=split_name, repeat=repetition),
      batch_size=100,
      verbose=True,
  )</cell id="cell-7">

    filenames = ['dinner_party.zip', 'dinner_party_eval.zip', 'no_speech.zip', 'speech.zip']
    for fname in filenames:
        link = link_root + fname

        zip_path = f"negative_datasets/{fname}"
        !wget -O {zip_path} {link}
        !unzip -q {zip_path} -d {output_dir}</cell id="cell-8">

#  validation/
#    ragged_mmap_folders_ending_in_mmap
#  validation_ambient/
#    ragged_mmap_folders_ending_in_mmap
#
#  sampling_weight: Weight for choosing a spectrogram from this set in the batch
#  penalty_weight: Penalizing weight for incorrect predictions from this set
#  truth: Boolean whether this set has positive samples or negative samples
#  truncation_strategy = If spectrograms in the set are longer than necessary for training, how are they truncated
#       - random: choose a random portion of the entire spectrogram - useful for long negative samples
#       - truncate_start: remove the start of the spectrogram
#       - truncate_end: remove the end of the spectrogram
#       - split: Split the longer spectrogram into separate spectrograms offset by 100 ms. Only for ambient sets

config["features"] = [
    {
        "features_dir": "generated_augmented_features",
        "sampling_weight": 2.0,
        "penalty_weight": 1.0,
        "truth": True,
        "truncation_strategy": "truncate_start",
        "type": "mmap",
    },
    {
        "features_dir": "negative_datasets/speech",
        "sampling_weight": 10.0,
        "penalty_weight": 1.0,
        "truth": False,
        "truncation_strategy": "random",
        "type": "mmap",
    },
    {
        "features_dir": "negative_datasets/dinner_party",
        "sampling_weight": 10.0,
        "penalty_weight": 1.0,
        "truth": False,
        "truncation_strategy": "random",
        "type": "mmap",
    },
    {
        "features_dir": "negative_datasets/no_speech",
        "sampling_weight": 5.0,
        "penalty_weight": 1.0,
        "truth": False,
        "truncation_strategy": "random",
        "type": "mmap",
    },
    { # Only used for validation and testing
        "features_dir": "negative_datasets/dinner_party_eval",
        "sampling_weight": 0.0,
        "penalty_weight": 1.0,
        "truth": False,
        "truncation_strategy": "split",
        "type": "mmap",
    },
]

# Number of training steps in each iteration - various other settings are configured as lists that corresponds to different steps
config["training_steps"] = [10000]

# Penalizing weight for incorrect class predictions - lists that correspond to training steps
config["positive_class_weight"] = [1]
config["negative_class_weight"] = [20]

config["learning_rates"] = [
    0.001,
]  # Learning rates for Adam optimizer - list that corresponds to training steps
config["batch_size"] = 128

config["time_mask_max_size"] = [
    0
]  # SpecAugment - list that corresponds to training steps
config["time_mask_count"] = [0]  # SpecAugment - list that corresponds to training steps
config["freq_mask_max_size"] = [
    0
]  # SpecAugment - list that corresponds to training steps
config["freq_mask_count"] = [0]  # SpecAugment - list that corresponds to training steps

config["eval_step_interval"] = (
    500  # Test the validation sets after every this many steps
)
config["clip_duration_ms"] = (
    1500  # Maximum length of wake word that the streaming model will accept
)

# The best model weights are chosen first by minimizing the specified minimization metric below the specified target_minimization
# Once the target has been met, it chooses the maximum of the maximization metric. Set 'minimization_metric' to None to only maximize
# Available metrics:
#   - "loss" - cross entropy error on validation set
#   - "accuracy" - accuracy of validation set
#   - "recall" - recall of validation set
#   - "precision" - precision of validation set
#   - "false_positive_rate" - false positive rate of validation set
#   - "false_negative_rate" - false negative rate of validation set
#   - "ambient_false_positives" - count of false positives from the split validation_ambient set
#   - "ambient_false_positives_per_hour" - estimated number of false positives per hour on the split validation_ambient set
config["target_minimization"] = 0.9
config["minimization_metric"] = None  # Set to None to disable

config["maximization_metric"] = "average_viable_recall"

with open(os.path.join("training_parameters.yaml"), "w") as file:
    documents = yaml.dump(config, file)</cell id="cell-9">
<cell id="cell-10"># Trains a model. When finished, it will quantize and convert the model to a
# streaming version suitable for on-device detection.
# It will resume if stopped, but it will start over at the configured training
# steps in the yaml file.
# Change --train 0 to only convert and test the best-weighted model.
# On Google colab, it doesn't print the mini-batch results, so it may appear
# stuck for several minutes! Additionally, it is very slow compared to training
# on a local GPU.

!python -m microwakeword.model_train_eval \
--training_config='training_parameters.yaml' \
--train 1 \
--restore_checkpoint 1 \
--test_tf_nonstreaming 0 \
--test_tflite_nonstreaming 0 \
--test_tflite_nonstreaming_quantized 0 \
--test_tflite_streaming 0 \
--test_tflite_streaming_quantized 1 \
--use_weights "best_weights" \
mixednet \
--pointwise_filters "64,64,64,64" \
--repeat_in_block  "1, 1, 1, 1" \
--mixconv_kernel_sizes '[5], [7,11], [9,15], [23]' \
--residual_connection "0,0,0,0" \
--first_conv_filters 32 \
--first_conv_kernel_size 5 \
--stride 3</cell id="cell-10">
<cell id="cell-11"># Downloads the tflite model file. To use on the device, you need to write a

# examples. Adjust the probability threshold based on the test results obtained
# after training is finished. You may also need to increase the Tensor arena
# model size if the model fails to load.

from google.colab import files

files.download(f"trained_models/wakeword/tflite_stream_state_internal_quant/stream_state_internal_quant.tflite")</cell id="cell-11">

**Training Pipeline** (what micro-wake-word does):1. Generate samples using Piper TTS
2. Augment samples with background noise, RIR, effects
3. Generate spectrogram features using microfrontend (40 bins, 10ms step)
4. Train model using those spectrograms
5. Convert to streaming TFLite model

**Inference Pipeline** (what we need on ESP32):
1. Capture audio at 16kHz, 16-bit PCM
2. Process audio through microfrontend (40 features, 10ms step)
3. Feed features to TFLite model
4. Apply sliding window over probabilities5. Trigger when threshold exceeded

## Key Resources Found

### Official Espressif Repository
The esp-tflite-micro repository has the esp-tflite-micro component and examples needed to use TensorFlow Lite Micro on Espressif Chipsets (e.g., ESP32-P4) using the ESP-IDF platform.(no content)Currently ESP-IDF versions release/v4.4 and above are supported by this project.

### Micro Speech Example
The micro_speech sample has been tested on ESP-IDF version `release/v4.2` and `release/v4.4` with devices including ESP32-DevKitC, ESP32-S3-DevKitC, and ESP-EYE.

### Audio Preprocessing Challenges
Developers have been trying to identify sounds (like cat sounds) on the esp32-s3-eye using TFLM, where the first step is to create the preprocessor model.(no content)The audio_preprocessor.py script appears to use custom operations (like SignalWindow) which prevents using the model in TFLM.

### Microfrontend Resources
The google-research/kws_streaming repository has a framework that allows model creation specifically for the tflite4micro frontend, and there's also the TensorFlow microfrontend at tensorflow/lite/experimental/microfrontend.

### Sound Classification Projects
Developers have been using the tflite-micro-esp-examples repo to classify sound events on ESP32-S3, which works fine and compiles on IDF master while also using AI acceleration of the ESP32-S3.

### Arduino Integration
For Arduino projects, you can convert TFLite models into C source files using the xxd command to include in your Arduino project folder.

**Note:** Most of the official esp-tflite-micro examples use ESP-IDF rather than Arduino directly. For Arduino usage, you may need to use community libraries or adapt the ESP-IDF examples.

    45→  // figure out which audio data we need to fetch.

    47→  const int current_step = (time_in_ms / kFeatureSliceStrideMs);
    48→
    49→  int slices_needed = current_step - last_step;

    51→  if (is_first_run_) {

    53→    if (init_status != kTfLiteOk) {

    55→    }
    56→    is_first_run_ = false;

    58→  }

    60→    slices_needed = kFeatureSliceCount;
    61→  }
    62→  *how_many_new_slices = slices_needed;
    63→
    64→  const int slices_to_keep = kFeatureSliceCount - slices_needed;
    65→  const int slices_to_drop = kFeatureSliceCount - slices_to_keep;

    67→  // up in the spectrogram, to perform something like this:
    68→  // last time = 80ms          current time = 120ms
    69→  // +-----------+             +-----------+
    70→  // | data@20ms |         --> | data@60ms |
    71→  // +-----------+       --    +-----------+
    72→  // | data@40ms |     --  --> | data@80ms |
    73→  // +-----------+   --  --    +-----------+
    74→  // | data@60ms | --  --      |  <empty>  |

    46→  config.noise_reduction.min_signal_remaining = 0.05;
    47→  config.pcan_gain_control.enable_pcan = 1;
    48→  config.pcan_gain_control.strength = 0.95;
    49→  config.pcan_gain_control.offset = 80.0;
    50→  config.pcan_gain_control.gain_bits = 21;
    51→  config.log_scale.enable_log = 1;
    52→  config.log_scale.scale_shift = 6;
    53→  if (!FrontendPopulateState(&config, &g_micro_features_state,
    54→                             kAudioSampleFrequency)) {
    55→    TF_LITE_REPORT_ERROR(error_reporter, "FrontendPopulateState() failed");
    56→    return kTfLiteError;

    71→                                   const int16_t* input, int input_size,
    72→                                   int output_size, int8_t* output,
    73→                                   size_t* num_samples_read) {
    74→  const int16_t* frontend_input;
    75→  if (g_is_first_time) {

    78→  } else {

    88→    // range. In training, these are then arbitrarily divided by 25.6 to get
    89→    // float values in the rough range of 0.0 to 26.0. This scaling is performed
    90→    // for historical reasons, to match up with the output of other feature
    91→    // generators.
    92→    // The process is then further complicated when we quantize the model. This
    93→    // means we have to scale the 0.0 to 26.0 real values to the -128 to 127
    94→    // signed integer numbers.
    95→    // All this means that to get matching values from our integer feature
    96→    // output into the tensor input, we have to perform:
    97→    // input = (((feature / 25.6) / 26.0) * 256) - 128
    98→    // To simplify this and perform it in 32-bit integer math, we rearrange to:

   108→    }

 * microWakeWord Pretrained Test
 *
 * Tests "Hey Jarvis" wake word detection using microWakeWord TFLite model.
 * Uses the TensorFlowLite_ESP32 microfrontend for audio preprocessing.
 *
 * Based on: https://github.com/kahrendt/microWakeWord
 * Model: hey_jarvis.tflite (v2)
 *
 * Audio: 16kHz, 16-bit mono
 * Features: 40 bins, 30ms window, 10ms stride
 * Detection: Sliding window probability averaging
 */

#include <TensorFlowLite_ESP32.h>
#include <driver/i2s.h>

#include "tensorflow/lite/micro/micro_interpreter.h"
#include "tensorflow/lite/micro/micro_mutable_op_resolver.h"
#include "tensorflow/lite/schema/schema_generated.h"
#include "tensorflow/lite/experimental/microfrontend/lib/frontend.h"
#include "tensorflow/lite/experimental/microfrontend/lib/frontend_util.h"

// Include model (convert tflite to C array with xxd -i)
#include "hey_jarvis_model.h"

// Pins (INMP441 microphone)
#define MIC_BCK  2
#define MIC_WS   4
#define MIC_DIN  18
#define LED_PIN  1

// Audio config
#define SAMPLE_RATE     16000
#define AUDIO_CHUNK_MS  10          // Process 10ms chunks (160 samples)
#define AUDIO_CHUNK_SAMPLES (SAMPLE_RATE * AUDIO_CHUNK_MS / 1000)

// Feature config (matches microWakeWord training)
#define FEATURE_WINDOW_MS   30      // 30ms window
#define FEATURE_STRIDE_MS   10      // 10ms stride (v2 models)
#define FEATURE_BINS        40      // Frequency bins
#define FEATURE_WINDOW_SAMPLES (SAMPLE_RATE * FEATURE_WINDOW_MS / 1000)

// Detection config (from hey_jarvis.json)
#define PROBABILITY_CUTOFF  0.97f   // 97% confidence threshold
#define SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE 5       // Average over 5 inferences
#define TENSOR_ARENA_SIZE   30000   // ~26KB needed, allocate 30KB

// Globals
static uint8_t tensor_arena[TENSOR_ARENA_SIZE];
static tflite::MicroInterpreter* interpreter = nullptr;
static TfLiteTensor* input_tensor = nullptr;
static TfLiteTensor* output_tensor = nullptr;
static FrontendState frontend_state;

// Audio buffers
static int32_t i2s_buffer[512];
static int16_t audio_buffer[FEATURE_WINDOW_SAMPLES];
static int audio_buffer_pos = 0;

// Sliding window for probability averaging
static float probability_window[SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE];
static int window_pos = 0;
static bool window_filled = false;

// Forward declarations
bool initMicrophone();
bool initFrontend();
bool initInterpreter();
bool captureAudio();
float runInference();
bool detectWakeword(float probability);
void errorBlink();

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(115200);
  delay(1000);

  pinMode(LED_PIN, OUTPUT);
  digitalWrite(LED_PIN, LOW);

  Serial.println("\n=== microWakeWord Test ===");
  Serial.println("Wake word: \"Hey Jarvis\"");
  Serial.println("Model: hey_jarvis.tflite v2\n");

  // Initialize microphone
  if (!initMicrophone()) {
    Serial.println("ERROR: Microphone init failed");
    errorBlink();
  }
  Serial.println("Microphone: OK");

  // Initialize microfrontend
  if (!initFrontend()) {
    Serial.println("ERROR: Frontend init failed");
    errorBlink();
  }
  Serial.println("Frontend: OK");

  // Initialize TFLite interpreter
  if (!initInterpreter()) {
    Serial.println("ERROR: TFLite init failed");
    errorBlink();
  }
  Serial.println("TFLite: OK");
  Serial.printf("  Input shape: [%d, %d]\n",
                input_tensor->dims->data[1],
                input_tensor->dims->data[2]);
  Serial.printf("  Arena used: %d bytes\n", interpreter->arena_used_bytes());

  // Initialize probability window
  for (int i = 0; i < SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE; i++) {
    probability_window[i] = 0.0f;
  }

  Serial.println("\nListening for \"Hey Jarvis\"...");
  Serial.println("================================\n");
}

void loop() {
  // Capture audio and accumulate in buffer
  if (!captureAudio()) {
    return;
  }

  // Once we have enough audio, run inference
  if (audio_buffer_pos >= FEATURE_WINDOW_SAMPLES) {
    // Run inference
    float prob = runInference();

    // Check detection with sliding window
    if (detectWakeword(prob)) {
      Serial.println("\n>>> HEY JARVIS DETECTED! <<<\n");
      digitalWrite(LED_PIN, HIGH);
      delay(500);
      digitalWrite(LED_PIN, LOW);

      // Reset window after detection
      for (int i = 0; i < SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE; i++) {
        probability_window[i] = 0.0f;
      }
      window_filled = false;
    }

    // Shift audio buffer by stride (keep overlap)
    int stride_samples = SAMPLE_RATE * FEATURE_STRIDE_MS / 1000;
    int overlap = FEATURE_WINDOW_SAMPLES - stride_samples;
    memmove(audio_buffer, audio_buffer + stride_samples, overlap * sizeof(int16_t));
    audio_buffer_pos = overlap;
  }
}

bool initMicrophone() {
  i2s_config_t config = {
    .mode = (i2s_mode_t)(I2S_MODE_MASTER | I2S_MODE_RX),
    .sample_rate = SAMPLE_RATE,
    .bits_per_sample = I2S_BITS_PER_SAMPLE_32BIT,
    .channel_format = I2S_CHANNEL_FMT_ONLY_LEFT,
    .communication_format = I2S_COMM_FORMAT_STAND_I2S,
    .intr_alloc_flags = ESP_INTR_FLAG_LEVEL1,
    .dma_buf_count = 4,
    .dma_buf_len = 256,
    .use_apll = false
  };

  i2s_pin_config_t pins = {
    .bck_io_num = MIC_BCK,
    .ws_io_num = MIC_WS,
    .data_out_num = I2S_PIN_NO_CHANGE,
    .data_in_num = MIC_DIN
  };

  return (i2s_driver_install(I2S_NUM_0, &config, 0, NULL) == ESP_OK &&
          i2s_set_pin(I2S_NUM_0, &pins) == ESP_OK);
}

bool initFrontend() {
  FrontendConfig config;
  config.window.size_ms = FEATURE_WINDOW_MS;
  config.window.step_size_ms = FEATURE_STRIDE_MS;
  config.filterbank.num_channels = FEATURE_BINS;
  config.filterbank.lower_band_limit = 125.0f;
  config.filterbank.upper_band_limit = 7500.0f;
  config.noise_reduction.smoothing_bits = 10;
  config.noise_reduction.even_smoothing = 0.025f;
  config.noise_reduction.odd_smoothing = 0.06f;
  config.noise_reduction.min_signal_remaining = 0.05f;
  config.pcan_gain_control.enable_pcan = 1;
  config.pcan_gain_control.strength = 0.95f;
  config.pcan_gain_control.offset = 80.0f;
  config.pcan_gain_control.gain_bits = 21;
  config.log_scale.enable_log = 1;
  config.log_scale.scale_shift = 6;

  return FrontendPopulateState(&config, &frontend_state, SAMPLE_RATE);
}

bool initInterpreter() {
  const tflite::Model* model = tflite::GetModel(hey_jarvis_model);
  if (model->version() != TFLITE_SCHEMA_VERSION) {
    Serial.printf("Model version mismatch: %d vs %d\n",
                  model->version(), TFLITE_SCHEMA_VERSION);
    return false;
  }

  // Add ops needed by microWakeWord models
  static tflite::MicroMutableOpResolver<10> resolver;
  resolver.AddConv2D();
  resolver.AddDepthwiseConv2D();
  resolver.AddFullyConnected();
  resolver.AddReshape();
  resolver.AddSoftmax();
  resolver.AddMul();
  resolver.AddAdd();
  resolver.AddMean();
  resolver.AddPad();
  resolver.AddQuantize();

  static tflite::MicroInterpreter static_interpreter(
      model, resolver, tensor_arena, TENSOR_ARENA_SIZE);
  interpreter = &static_interpreter;

  if (interpreter->AllocateTensors() != kTfLiteOk) {
    Serial.println("AllocateTensors failed");
    return false;
  }

  input_tensor = interpreter->input(0);
  output_tensor = interpreter->output(0);

  return true;
}

bool captureAudio() {
  size_t bytes_read;
  if (i2s_read(I2S_NUM_0, i2s_buffer, sizeof(i2s_buffer), &bytes_read, 10) != ESP_OK) {
    return false;
  }

  int samples = bytes_read / 4;
  for (int i = 0; i < samples && audio_buffer_pos < FEATURE_WINDOW_SAMPLES; i++) {
    // Convert 32-bit I2S to 16-bit with gain
    int32_t sample = i2s_buffer[i] >> 14;
    audio_buffer[audio_buffer_pos++] = constrain(sample, -32768, 32767);
  }

  return true;
}

float runInference() {
  // Generate features using microfrontend
  size_t num_samples_read;
  FrontendOutput frontend_output = FrontendProcessSamples(
      &frontend_state, audio_buffer, FEATURE_WINDOW_SAMPLES, &num_samples_read);

  if (frontend_output.size != FEATURE_BINS) {
    return 0.0f;
  }

  // Copy features to input tensor with quantization
  int8_t* input_data = input_tensor->data.int8;
  float input_scale = input_tensor->params.scale;
  int input_zero_point = input_tensor->params.zero_point;

  for (size_t i = 0; i < frontend_output.size; i++) {
    // Scale microfrontend output (uint16) to model input range
    float value = frontend_output.values[i] * 0.0390625f;  // /25.6
    int32_t quantized = (int32_t)(value / input_scale) + input_zero_point;
    input_data[i] = constrain(quantized, -128, 127);
  }

  // Run inference
  if (interpreter->Invoke() != kTfLiteOk) {
    Serial.println("Invoke failed");
    return 0.0f;
  }

  // Get output probability (dequantize if needed)
  float probability;
  if (output_tensor->type == kTfLiteInt8) {
    int8_t output_value = output_tensor->data.int8[0];
    probability = (output_value - output_tensor->params.zero_point) *
                  output_tensor->params.scale;
  } else {
    probability = output_tensor->data.f[0];
  }

  return probability;
}

bool detectWakeword(float probability) {
  // Add to sliding window
  probability_window[window_pos] = probability;
  window_pos = (window_pos + 1) % SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE;

  if (window_pos == 0) {
    window_filled = true;
  }

  // Don't trigger until window is filled
  if (!window_filled) {
    return false;
  }

  // Calculate average probability
  float avg = 0.0f;
  for (int i = 0; i < SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE; i++) {
    avg += probability_window[i];
  }
  avg /= SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE;

  // Debug output
  static int count = 0;
  if (++count >= 10) {
    Serial.printf("prob: %.3f, avg: %.3f\n", probability, avg);
    count = 0;
  }

  return avg >= PROBABILITY_CUTOFF;
}

void errorBlink() {
  while (1) {
    digitalWrite(LED_PIN, !digitalRead(LED_PIN));
    delay(200);
  }
}

# microWakeWord Pretrained Test

Tests wake word detection using pre-trained microWakeWord TFLite models.

**Wake word: "Hey Jarvis"**

## How It Works

1. **Audio capture**: INMP441 microphone at 16kHz, 16-bit mono
2. **Feature extraction**: TFLite microfrontend generates 40-bin spectrogram features
3. **Inference**: Streaming TFLite model processes features every 10ms
4. **Detection**: Sliding window averages probabilities, triggers at 97% threshold

## Setup

### 1. Convert Model to C Header

The model must be converted to a C array:

\```bash
# From this directory
xxd -i models/hey_jarvis.tflite > hey_jarvis_model.h

# Edit the header to rename the array:
# Change: unsigned char models_hey_jarvis_tflite[]
# To: const unsigned char hey_jarvis_model[] PROGMEM
\```

Or use the provided script:
\```bash
./convert_model.sh
\```

### 2. Copy Model File

Copy from the micro-wake-word-models repo:
\```bash
cp /path/to/_STASH_/micro-wake-word-models/models/v2/hey_jarvis.tflite models/
\```

### 3. Install TensorFlowLite_ESP32

Via Arduino Library Manager or from:
https://github.com/tanakamasayuki/TensorFlowLite_ESP32

### 4. Board Settings

- Board: ESP32S3 Dev Module
- PSRAM: OPI PSRAM
- Flash Size: 16MB
- Partition: Default or larger

### 5. Upload and Test

Say "Hey Jarvis" - LED lights up on detection.

## Expected Output

\```
=== microWakeWord Test ===
Wake word: "Hey Jarvis"
Model: hey_jarvis.tflite v2

Microphone: OK
Frontend: OK
TFLite: OK
  Input shape: [1, 40]
  Arena used: 23456 bytes

Listening for "Hey Jarvis"...
================================

prob: 0.012, avg: 0.008
prob: 0.003, avg: 0.005
prob: 0.891, avg: 0.234
prob: 0.967, avg: 0.612
prob: 0.989, avg: 0.823
prob: 0.994, avg: 0.971

>>> HEY JARVIS DETECTED! <<<
\```

## Model Parameters

From `hey_jarvis.json`:
- **probability_cutoff**: 0.97 (97% confidence)
- **feature_step_size**: 10ms
- **sliding_window_size**: 5 frames
- **tensor_arena_size**: ~23KB

## Troubleshooting

### "TFLite init failed"
- Model not converted correctly
- Check tensor arena size (increase if needed)
- Missing ops in resolver

### No detection / false positives
- Adjust PROBABILITY_CUTOFF (lower = more sensitive)
- Check microphone gain
- Try different sliding window size

### Memory issues
- Use PSRAM for large buffers
- Reduce tensor arena size

## Technical Details

### Audio Processing
- Sample rate: 16000 Hz
- Window: 30ms (480 samples)
- Stride: 10ms (160 samples)
- FFT size: 512

### Feature Extraction (microfrontend)
- 40 Mel-frequency bins
- 125 Hz - 7500 Hz range
- PCAN gain control enabled
- Noise reduction enabled
- Log scaling

### Model Architecture
- Streaming inception-based neural network
- Quantized INT8
- Single probability output [0.0 - 1.0]

## Available Models

From [micro-wake-word-models](https://github.com/esphome/micro-wake-word-models):

| Model | Wake Word | Size |
|-------|-----------|------|
| hey_jarvis.tflite | "Hey Jarvis" | ~50KB |
| okay_nabu.tflite | "Okay Nabu" | ~50KB |
| alexa.tflite | "Alexa" | ~50KB |

## Sources

- [microWakeWord](https://github.com/kahrendt/microWakeWord)
- [micro-wake-word-models](https://github.com/esphome/micro-wake-word-models)
- [ESPHome micro_wake_word](https://esphome.io/components/micro_wake_word/)
- [TensorFlowLite_ESP32](https://github.com/tanakamasayuki/TensorFlowLite_ESP32)

#!/bin/bash
# Convert TFLite model to C header for Arduino

MODEL_SRC="${1:-/home/alphons/project/OAISYS25/_STASH_/micro-wake-word-models/models/v2/hey_jarvis.tflite}"
MODEL_NAME="hey_jarvis_model"
OUTPUT="hey_jarvis_model.h"

if [ ! -f "$MODEL_SRC" ]; then
    echo "Model not found: $MODEL_SRC"
    echo "Usage: $0 [path/to/model.tflite]"
    exit 1
fi

# Copy model locally
mkdir -p models
cp "$MODEL_SRC" models/hey_jarvis.tflite

# Convert to C array
echo "Converting $MODEL_SRC to $OUTPUT..."

xxd -i models/hey_jarvis.tflite > temp_model.h

# Fix the header
sed -i "s/unsigned char models_hey_jarvis_tflite/const unsigned char ${MODEL_NAME}/" temp_model.h
sed -i "s/unsigned int models_hey_jarvis_tflite_len/const unsigned int ${MODEL_NAME}_len/" temp_model.h

# Add header guard and alignment
cat > "$OUTPUT" << 'EOF'
// Auto-generated from hey_jarvis.tflite
// Model: microWakeWord "Hey Jarvis" v2
// Source: https://github.com/esphome/micro-wake-word-models

#ifndef HEY_JARVIS_MODEL_H
#define HEY_JARVIS_MODEL_H

#include <stdint.h>

EOF

cat temp_model.h >> "$OUTPUT"

echo "" >> "$OUTPUT"
echo "#endif // HEY_JARVIS_MODEL_H" >> "$OUTPUT"

rm temp_model.h

SIZE=$(stat -c%s models/hey_jarvis.tflite 2>/dev/null || stat -f%z models/hey_jarvis.tflite)
echo "Done! Model size: $SIZE bytes"
echo "Header: $OUTPUT"

   124→  }

   127→  if (audio_buffer_pos >= FEATURE_WINDOW_SAMPLES) {

   142→      window_filled = false;
   143→    }

   145→    // Shift audio buffer by stride (keep overlap)
   146→    int stride_samples = SAMPLE_RATE * FEATURE_STRIDE_MS / 1000;
   147→    int overlap = FEATURE_WINDOW_SAMPLES - stride_samples;
   148→    memmove(audio_buffer, audio_buffer + stride_samples, overlap * sizeof(int16_t));
   149→    audio_buffer_pos = overlap;
   150→  }
   151→}

   234→bool captureAudio() {
   235→  size_t bytes_read;
   236→  if (i2s_read(I2S_NUM_0, i2s_buffer, sizeof(i2s_buffer), &bytes_read, 10) != ESP_OK) {
   237→    return false;
   238→  }
   239→
   240→  int samples = bytes_read / 4;
   241→  for (int i = 0; i < samples && audio_buffer_pos < FEATURE_WINDOW_SAMPLES; i++) {
   242→    // Convert 32-bit I2S to 16-bit with gain
   243→    int32_t sample = i2s_buffer[i] >> 14;
   244→    audio_buffer[audio_buffer_pos++] = constrain(sample, -32768, 32767);
   245→  }
   246→
   247→  return true;
   248→}
   249→
   250→float runInference() {
   251→  // Generate features using microfrontend
   252→  size_t num_samples_read;
   253→  FrontendOutput frontend_output = FrontendProcessSamples(
   254→      &frontend_state, audio_buffer, FEATURE_WINDOW_SAMPLES, &num_samples_read);
   255→
   256→  if (frontend_output.size != FEATURE_BINS) {
   257→    return 0.0f;
   258→  }
   259→
   260→  // Copy features to input tensor with quantization
   261→  int8_t* input_data = input_tensor->data.int8;
   262→  float input_scale = input_tensor->params.scale;
   263→  int input_zero_point = input_tensor->params.zero_point;
   264→
   265→  for (size_t i = 0; i < frontend_output.size; i++) {
   266→    // Scale microfrontend output (uint16) to model input range
   267→    float value = frontend_output.values[i] * 0.0390625f;  // /25.6
   268→    int32_t quantized = (int32_t)(value / input_scale) + input_zero_point;
   269→    input_data[i] = constrain(quantized, -128, 127);
   270→  }
   271→
   272→  // Run inference
   273→  if (interpreter->Invoke() != kTfLiteOk) {
   274→    Serial.println("Invoke failed");
   275→    return 0.0f;
   276→  }
   277→
   278→  // Get output probability (dequantize if needed)
   279→  float probability;
   280→  if (output_tensor->type == kTfLiteInt8) {
   281→    int8_t output_value = output_tensor->data.int8[0];
   282→    probability = (output_value - output_tensor->params.zero_point) *
   283→                  output_tensor->params.scale;
   284→  } else {
   285→    probability = output_tensor->data.f[0];
   286→  }
   287→
   288→  return probability;
   289→}
   290→
   291→bool detectWakeword(float probability) {
   292→  // Add to sliding window
   293→  probability_window[window_pos] = probability;
   294→  window_pos = (window_pos + 1) % SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE;
   295→
   296→  if (window_pos == 0) {
   297→    window_filled = true;
   298→  }
   299→
   300→  // Don't trigger until window is filled
   301→  if (!window_filled) {
   302→    return false;
   303→  }
   304→
   305→  // Calculate average probability
   306→  float avg = 0.0f;
   307→  for (int i = 0; i < SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE; i++) {
   308→    avg += probability_window[i];
   309→  }
   310→  avg /= SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE;
   311→
   312→  // Debug output
   313→  static int count = 0;
   314→  if (++count >= 10) {
   315→    Serial.printf("prob: %.3f, avg: %.3f\n", probability, avg);
   316→    count = 0;
   317→  }
   318→
   319→  return avg >= PROBABILITY_CUTOFF;
   320→}

   323→  while (1) {
   324→    digitalWrite(LED_PIN, !digitalRead(LED_PIN));
   325→    delay(200);
   326→  }
   327→}

The user is asking a very good question. They're right - you can absolutely load the TFLite model from an SD card instead of embedding it as a C header file. 

In fact, looking back at the earlier code I wrote for the `wakeword_pretrained_test`, I actually did load the model from SD card using `loadModelFromSD()`. That's a cleaner approach, especially for larger models or when you want to swap models without recompiling.

The two approaches are:

1. **Embedded in flash (C header)**: Model is compiled into the firmware. Good for small models, no SD card needed, faster startup.

2. **Load from SD card**: Model is read from SD at runtime into PSRAM. Good for larger models, easy to swap models, doesn't increase firmware size.

For microWakeWord models (~50KB), either approach works. But since the user already has SD card infrastructure in their project (they use it in other sketches), loading from SD is cleaner and more flexible.

# microWakeWord Pretrained Test

Tests wake word detection using pre-trained microWakeWord TFLite models.

**Wake word: "Hey Jarvis"**

## How It Works

1. **Audio capture**: INMP441 microphone at 16kHz, 16-bit mono
2. **Feature extraction**: TFLite microfrontend generates 40-bin spectrogram features
3. **Inference**: Streaming TFLite model processes features every 10ms
4. **Detection**: Sliding window averages probabilities, triggers at 97% threshold

## Setup

### 1. Copy Model to SD Card

Create this folder structure on your SD card:
\```
SD Card/
└── models/
    └── hey_jarvis.tflite
\```

Copy the model from:
\```
_STASH_/micro-wake-word-models/models/v2/hey_jarvis.tflite
\```

### 2. Install TensorFlowLite_ESP32

Via Arduino Library Manager or from:
https://github.com/tanakamasayuki/TensorFlowLite_ESP32

### 3. Board Settings

- Board: ESP32S3 Dev Module
- PSRAM: OPI PSRAM
- Flash Size: 16MB

### 4. Upload and Test

1. Insert SD card with model
2. Upload sketch
3. Open Serial Monitor (115200 baud)
4. Say "Hey Jarvis" - LED lights up on detection

## Expected Output

\```
=== microWakeWord Test ===
Wake word: "Hey Jarvis"
Model: /models/hey_jarvis.tflite

SD Card: OK
Model loaded: 51234 bytes
Microphone: OK
Frontend: OK
Model inputs: 1, outputs: 1
  Input[0]: dims=[1,3,40], type=9
  Output[0]: dims=[1,1], type=9
TFLite: OK
  Arena used: 23456 bytes

Listening for "Hey Jarvis"...
================================

prob: 0.012, avg: 0.008
prob: 0.967, avg: 0.612
prob: 0.994, avg: 0.971

>>> HEY JARVIS DETECTED! <<<
\```

## Model Parameters

From `hey_jarvis.json`:
- **probability_cutoff**: 0.97 (97% confidence)
- **feature_step_size**: 10ms
- **sliding_window_size**: 5 frames
- **tensor_arena_size**: ~23KB

## Troubleshooting

### "Model load failed"
- Check SD card has `/models/hey_jarvis.tflite`
- Try reformatting SD card as FAT32

### "TFLite init failed"
- Missing ops in resolver - check serial for details
- Increase TENSOR_ARENA_SIZE if needed

### No detection / false positives
- Adjust PROBABILITY_CUTOFF (lower = more sensitive)
- Check microphone gain
- Speak clearly, closer to microphone

## Available Models

From [micro-wake-word-models](https://github.com/esphome/micro-wake-word-models):

| Model | Wake Word |
|-------|-----------|
| hey_jarvis.tflite | "Hey Jarvis" |
| okay_nabu.tflite | "Okay Nabu" |
| alexa.tflite | "Alexa" |
| hey_mycroft.tflite | "Hey Mycroft" |

Just copy a different model to `/models/` on SD and update `MODEL_PATH` in the sketch.

## Sources

- [microWakeWord](https://github.com/kahrendt/microWakeWord)
- [micro-wake-word-models](https://github.com/esphome/micro-wake-word-models)
- [ESPHome micro_wake_word](https://esphome.io/components/micro_wake_word/)

Based on the search results, I found relevant information about the `stl_emulation.h` `count_` error in TensorFlowLite/flatbuffers on ESP32.

## The Problem

When compiling with newer GCC versions (like GCC 14.1.1), users get the error: `stl_emulation.h:549:12: error: assignment of read-only member 'flatbuffers::span<T, Extent>::count_'` with the line `count_ = other.count_;`. This was fixed in flatbuffers with google/flatbuffers#7227.(no content)It seems that the new GCC version somehow detects this error now as well.

## The Fix

The fix is to go to this line and remove the const qualifier from the `count_` variable in `stl_emulation.h`. This variable is no longer declared const on master in the flatbuffers repository.

Specifically, you need to find the `count_` member variable in the `span` class (around line 465 in older versions) and remove the `const` qualifier.

**Before:**
```cpp
const size_type count_;
```

**After:**
```cpp
size_type count_;
```

## Additional Solutions for ESP32 TensorFlowLite Issues

If you're also experiencing flatbuffers include path errors:

You can resolve the problem by adding `#include <TensorFlowLite_ESP32.h>` as the top-most header file.(no content)Another solution is using the TensorFlowLite_ESP32 library instead of Arduino_TensorFlowLite. You need to download this library and add the line `#include <TensorFlowLite_ESP32.h>`.

## References
- [BehaviorTree.CPP Issue #818](https://github.com/BehaviorTree/BehaviorTree.CPP/issues/818) - Documents the GCC 14 compilation error
- [xmos/lib_tflite_micro Issue #169](https://github.com/xmos/lib_tflite_micro/issues/169) - Provides the fix details
- [google/flatbuffers PR #7227](https://github.com/google/flatbuffers/pull/7227) - The upstream fix in flatbuffers

## Key Libraries Found

### 1. **MicroTFLite** (2024)
MicroTFLite is a TensorFlow Lite Micro library designed for Arduino, aimed at simplifying the process of using TensorFlow Lite Micro on Arduino boards.(no content)It provides an Arduino-style API, avoiding the use of pointers or other C++ syntax constructs, and can handle both quantized data and raw floating-point values, automatically detecting the appropriate processing method based on the model's metadata.

- GitHub: https://github.com/johnosbb/MicroTFLite
- This tutorial also applies to similar hardware platforms, such as ESP32 S3 AI devices.

### 2. **ArduTFLite**
ArduTFLite serves as a wrapper for the Chirale_TensorFlowLite library, which is a port of the official TensorFlow Lite Micro library for Arduino boards with ARM and ESP32 architecture. It is designed to enable experimentation with Tiny Machine Learning on Arduino boards with greater resources, such as Arduino Nano 33 BLE, Arduino Nano ESP32, Arduino Nicla, Arduino Portenta and Arduino Giga R1 WiFi.

- The library can be installed from the Arduino IDE Library Manager or can be installed as .zip file downloaded from GitHub.

# ESP32-S3 + TensorFlow Lite Micro: Implementation Guide

## Core Library & Setup

Use **TensorFlow Lite Micro (TFLM)** as the inference engine. The article states: "TensorFlow Lite Micro (TFLM) on ESP32-S3 to run real-time wake word detection."

## Model Preparation

1. **Quantize your model** to int8 format:
```python
converter = tf.lite.TFLiteConverter.from_saved_model("model_path")
converter.optimizations = [tf.lite.Optimize.DEFAULT]
converter.target_spec.supported_types = [tf.int8]
tflite_quant_model = converter.convert()
```

2. **Convert to C array**:
```bash
xxd -i model.tflite > model_data.cc
```

## Inference Code Structure

The basic inference loop:
```cpp
const tflite::Model* model = tflite::GetModel(model_data);
static tflite::MicroInterpreter interpreter(...);
interpreter.AllocateTensors();

while (true) {
    GetAudioFeature(input->data.int8);
    interpreter.Invoke();
    if (output->data.uint8[0] > 200) {
        printf("Wake word detected!\n");
    }
}
```

## Performance Expectations

- **Inference latency**: 50–60 ms
- **Model size**: ~240 KB (int8 quantized)
- **RAM usage**: ~350 KB
- **Throughput**: 15–20 FPS

## Audio Pipeline

Capture 16 kHz / 16-bit mono audio via I2S, extract MFCC features (2–3 ms per frame), then feed to the model.

## Top Working Alternatives

### 1. **MicroTFLite**
MicroTFLite is designed to enable experimentation with Tiny Machine Learning on Arduino boards with constrained resources, such as Arduino Nano 33 BLE, Arduino Nano ESP32, Arduino Nicla, Arduino Portenta, ESP32 based devices and Arduino Giga R1 WiFi.(no content)Usage is simple and straightforward and you don't need extensive TensorFlow expertise to code your sketches. MicroTFLite consists of an Arduino style abstraction called MicroTFLite and a port of TensorFlow Lite for Arduino type boards.

- GitHub: https://github.com/johnosbb/MicroTFLite

### 2. **EloquentTinyML**
Running TensorFlow on your ESP32 board can be as easy as 3 lines of code. You only have to install the EloquentTinyML Arduino library and follow the code examples. It works out of the box on ARM and ESP32 chips.(no content)Two lines are required: `sineNN.begin()` to init the TensorFlow Lite stuff and `sineNN.predict(input)` to get a prediction from the model. The same exact code works both for ESP32 boards and ARM boards.

### 3. **Espressif's Official Repository**
The https://github.com/espressif/tflite-micro-esp-examples repo is working fine and compiles on IDF master also using AI acceleration of the ESP32-S3.

### 4. **Chirale_TensorFlowLite**
It is similar to older and outdated Arduino_TensorFlowLite Micro example library, published in 2019 and referred by Arduino tutorials, but it has been regenerated from main TFLite Micro Library and is updated.

- GitHub: https://github.com/spaziochirale/Chirale_TensorFlowLite

### 5. **Arduino_TensorFlowLite_ESP32 (tanakamasayuki)**
This library runs TensorFlow machine learning models on microcontrollers, allowing you to build AI/ML applications powered by deep learning and neural networks.(no content)With the included examples, you can recognize speech, detect people using a camera, and recognise "magic wand" gestures using an accelerometer. The examples work best with the M5StickC(ESP32) board.

- GitHub: https://github.com/tanakamasayuki/Arduino_TensorFlowLite_ESP32

## Additional Notes
LiteRT for Microcontrollers (Google's rebranding) is written in C++ 17 and requires a 32-bit platform. It has been tested extensively with many processors based on the Arm Cortex-M Series architecture, and has been ported to other architectures including ESP32.

For the easiest getting-started experience, **MicroTFLite** or **EloquentTinyML** are recommended as they provide Arduino-friendly APIs that abstract away much of the complexity.

Here are the search results for ESPHome micro wake word TensorFlow Lite implementation on ESP32:

## Overview

ESPHome implements an on-device wake word detection framework from microWakeWord. This repository/library allows you to create a custom wake word for your ESPHome device.

## Technical Implementation

Wake word detection is done entirely with TensorFlow Lite Micro. Wake word models are trained without using Espressif's proprietary Skainet and can be customized without samples from different speakers.(no content)The target devices are ESP32-S3 based with external PSRAM. It may run on a regular ESP32 but may not perform as well.

### Audio Processing

The preprocessor generates 40 features over 30 ms (the window duration) of audio data. The preprocessor generates these features every 20 ms (the stride duration), so the first 10 ms of audio data is part of the previous window. This process is similar to calculating a Mel spectrogram for the audio data, but it is lightweight for devices with limited processing power.

### Model Architecture

The streaming model performs inferences every 20 ms on the newest audio stride. The model is based on an inception neural network converted for streaming. It executes an inference in under 10 ms on an ESP32-S3, much faster than the 20 ms stride length.

## Performance

It works well with comparable performance to openWakeWord. The detection latency is extremely low, nearly always faster than an ESP32 device using the openWakeWord pipeline.(no content)These models are faster and more accurate. Up to 3 models can run on a regular ESP32 at the same time (e.g., VAD, "okay nabu", and "hey mycroft"). ESP32-S3 supports running all 4 concurrently.

## Configuration Example

Models can be configured using shorthand names or GitHub URLs, such as `model: okay_nabu` or `model: github://esphome/micro-wake-word-models/models/v2/okay_nabu.json`.(no content)The `probability_cutoff` option sets the probability cutoff for wake word detection. If the probability of the wake word is below this value, the wake word is not detected. A larger value reduces the number of false accepts but increases the number of false rejections.

## Additional Features

VAD (Voice Activity Detection) model can be enabled to reduce false accepts from non-speech sounds.(no content)microWakeWord is an open-source wakeword library for detecting custom wake words on low power devices. It produces models that are suitable for using TensorFlow Lite for Microcontrollers. The models are suitable for real-world usage with low false accept and false reject rates.

## Key Resources

- **ESPHome Documentation**: https://esphome.io/components/micro_wake_word/
- **GitHub Repository**: https://github.com/kahrendt/esphome-on-device-wake-word
- **OHF-Voice micro-wake-word**: https://github.com/OHF-Voice/micro-wake-word/releases

This library allows you to run machine learning models locally on your ESP32 device. It runs TensorFlow machine learning models on microcontrollers, allowing you to build AI/ML applications powered by deep learning and neural networks.

### MicroTFLite
MicroTFLite is a TensorFlow Lite Micro library designed for Arduino, aimed at simplifying the process of using TensorFlow Lite Micro on Arduino boards. # MicroTFLite Installation and API Guide

## Installation

To install MicroTFLite, clone the GitHub repository into your Arduino libraries folder:

```
git clone https://github.com/johnosbb/MicroTFLite MicroTFLite
```

Update to the latest version by running:
```
cd MicroTFLite
git pull
```

Once installed, sample projects appear in the Arduino IDE under `File -> Examples -> MicroTFLite`.

## Core API Functions

The documentation states that MicroTFLite provides "APIs in the typical Arduino style" and avoids pointers and complex C++ constructs. The key functions for model deployment are:

- **`ModelInit()`** - initializes your trained model
- **`ModelSetInput()`** - inserts data into the model's input tensor
- **`ModelRunInference()`** - executes the inference operation
- **`ModelGetOutput()`** - retrieves results from the output tensor

## Basic Workflow Example

According to the development process outlined:

1. Include headers: `MicroTFLite.h` and your `model.h` file
2. Define a global `tensorArena` byte array for memory allocation
3. Call `ModelInit()` to load your model
4. Use `ModelSetInput()` to provide input data
5. Execute `ModelRunInference()` to process
6. Retrieve results via `ModelGetOutput()`

For complete API documentation and code examples, the documentation references an API guide at `./docs/API.md` and includes sample sketches within the library.
```

## Audio Processing Libraries for ESP32

1. **ESP8266Audio** (github.com/earlephilhower/ESP8266Audio)
   - Arduino library to play MOD, WAV, FLAC, MIDI, RTTTL, OGG/Opus, MP3, and AAC files on I2S DACs or with a software emulated delta-sigma DAC on the ESP8266 and ESP32 and Pico.
   - This library is compatible with the esp8266, esp32, rp2040 architectures.

2. **yummyDSP** (github.com/garygru/yummyDSP)
   - yummyDSP is an Arduino audio DSP library for the Espressif ESP32. Main focus is realtime processing of audio signals for e.g. a guitar stomp box.
   - The idea is to have modular blocks which are simply arranged in a processing tree to form the signal chain. These processing blocks are called Nodes inspired by Apple's Audio Unit framework.

3. **ESP32-A2DP** (github.com/pschatzmann/ESP32-A2DP)
   - You can use this library standalone, but it is part of my audio-tools project. So you can easily enhance this functionality with sound effects, use filters or an equilizer, use alternative audio sinks or audio sources, do FFT etc.

4. **arduino-audiokit** (github.com/pschatzmann/arduino-audiokit)
   - However I recommend to use my Arduino Audio Tools Library which implements an easy to use Stream API with additional functionality on top of this and it has plenty of examples.

## ESPMicroSpeechFeatures Library

ESPMicroSpeechFeatures is a fork of the TensorFlow Lite Micro's Microfrontend for microWakeWord. It is used to generate spectrogram features from audio samples. Using this library avoids having to use a TFLM interpreter for generating features, which increases performance.(no content)It's available as a PlatformIO component for TFLM spectrogram features from audio samples.

**Resources:**
- **GitHub Repository**: https://github.com/kahrendt/ESPMicroSpeechFeatures
- **PlatformIO Registry**: https://registry.platformio.org/libraries/kahrendt/ESPMicroSpeechFeatures

## Related Libraries & Resources

### TensorFlow Lite Micro Speech (Arduino)
The starting point for doing speech recognition on an Arduino based board is TensorFlow Lite For Microcontrollers with the example sketch called micro_speech. The MicroSpeech example from TensorFlow Lite has been adapted to follow the Arduino audio tools framework philosophy. The example uses a TensorFlow model which can recognize the words 'yes' and 'no'.

### Arduino_TensorFlowLite Library
The micro_speech example application is included as part of the official TensorFlow Lite Arduino library. To install it, open the Arduino library manager in Tools -> Manage Libraries... and search for Arduino_TensorFlowLite. Once the library has been added, go to File -> Examples. You should see an example near the bottom of the list named TensorFlowLite:micro_speech. Select it and click micro_speech to load the example.

### uSpeech Library
The uSpeech library provides an interface for voice recognition using the Arduino. It currently produces phonemes, though the library may produce some junk phonemes.

# Frontend Audio Processing API

Based on the header file, the main API consists of two functions:

## Primary Functions

**`FrontendProcessSamples()`** - The core processing function that accepts audio samples and generates feature output. According to the documentation, it "Updates num_samples_read to contain the number of samples that have been consumed from the input array" and produces spectrogram features. If insufficient data exists for a complete feature vector, it returns a null pointer with size 0.

**`FrontendReset()`** - Resets the frontend state, allowing you to restart processing.

## Data Structures

The API uses two main structures:

- **`FrontendState`** - Maintains internal state across six processing stages: windowing, FFT computation, filterbank analysis, noise reduction, PCAN gain control, and logarithmic scaling
- **`FrontendOutput`** - Contains the resulting feature values (16-bit unsigned integers) and their count

The design emphasizes that output pointers become invalid after the next processing call, so callers must copy results if they need persistent access.

# FrontendProcessSamples Implementation Analysis

## Function Implementation

The `FrontendProcessSamples` function processes audio samples through a signal processing pipeline:

1. **Window Processing**: Applies windowing to input samples via `WindowProcessSamples`
2. **FFT Transform**: Computes FFT with dynamic scaling based on signal magnitude
3. **Energy Conversion**: Converts FFT output to energy values using `FilterbankConvertFftComplexToEnergy`
4. **Channel Accumulation**: Aggregates filterbank channels
5. **Normalization**: Applies square root scaling via `FilterbankSqrt`
6. **Noise Reduction**: Reduces noise through `NoiseReductionApply`
7. **Gain Control**: Optionally applies PCAN gain control
8. **Log Scaling**: Converts to logarithmic scale with `LogScaleApply`

## Dependencies

The source file depends on these header/source modules:

- **bits.h**: Provides `MostSignificantBit32` for bit manipulation
- **Window module**: `WindowProcessSamples`, `WindowReset`
- **FFT module**: `FftCompute`, `FftReset`
- **Filterbank module**: Energy conversion, channel accumulation, square root scaling, and reset functions
- **Noise Reduction module**: Noise reduction application and reset
- **PCAN Gain Control module**: Optional gain control processing
- **Log Scale module**: Logarithmic scaling application

The implementation uses reusable buffers (particularly FFT output) to optimize memory efficiency.
```

   319→bool captureAudio() {
   320→  size_t bytes_read;
   321→  if (i2s_read(I2S_NUM_0, i2s_buffer, sizeof(i2s_buffer), &bytes_read, 10) != ESP_OK) {
   322→    return false;
   323→  }
   324→
   325→  int samples = bytes_read / 4;
   326→  for (int i = 0; i < samples && audio_buffer_pos < FEATURE_WINDOW_SAMPLES; i++) {
   327→    // Convert 32-bit I2S to 16-bit with gain
   328→    int32_t sample = i2s_buffer[i] >> 14;
   329→    audio_buffer[audio_buffer_pos++] = constrain(sample, -32768, 32767);
   330→  }
   331→
   332→  return true;
   333→}
   334→
   335→float runInference() {
   336→  // Generate features using microfrontend
   337→  size_t num_samples_read;
   338→  FrontendOutput frontend_output = FrontendProcessSamples(
   339→      &frontend_state, audio_buffer, FEATURE_WINDOW_SAMPLES, &num_samples_read);
   340→
   341→  if (frontend_output.size != FEATURE_BINS) {
   342→    return 0.0f;
   343→  }
   344→
   345→  // Copy features to input tensor with quantization
   346→  int8_t* input_data = input_tensor->data.int8;
   347→  float input_scale = input_tensor->params.scale;
   348→  int input_zero_point = input_tensor->params.zero_point;
   349→
   350→  for (size_t i = 0; i < frontend_output.size; i++) {
   351→    // Scale microfrontend output (uint16) to model input range
   352→    float value = frontend_output.values[i] * 0.0390625f;  // /25.6
   353→    int32_t quantized = (int32_t)(value / input_scale) + input_zero_point;
   354→    input_data[i] = constrain(quantized, -128, 127);
   355→  }
   356→
   357→  // Run inference
   358→  if (interpreter->Invoke() != kTfLiteOk) {
   359→    Serial.println("Invoke failed");
   360→    return 0.0f;
   361→  }
   362→
   363→  // Get output probability (dequantize if needed)
   364→  float probability;
   365→  if (output_tensor->type == kTfLiteInt8) {
   366→    int8_t output_value = output_tensor->data.int8[0];
   367→    probability = (output_value - output_tensor->params.zero_point) *
   368→                  output_tensor->params.scale;
   369→  } else {
   370→    probability = output_tensor->data.f[0];
   371→  }
   372→
   373→  return probability;
   374→}
   375→
   376→bool detectWakeword(float probability) {
   377→  // Add to sliding window
   378→  probability_window[window_pos] = probability;
   379→  window_pos = (window_pos + 1) % SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE;
   380→
   381→  if (window_pos == 0) {
   382→    window_filled = true;
   383→  }
   384→
   385→  // Don't trigger until window is filled
   386→  if (!window_filled) {
   387→    return false;
   388→  }
   389→
   390→  // Calculate average probability
   391→  float avg = 0.0f;
   392→  for (int i = 0; i < SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE; i++) {
   393→    avg += probability_window[i];
   394→  }
   395→  avg /= SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE;
   396→
   397→  // Debug output
   398→  static int count = 0;
   399→  if (++count >= 10) {
   400→    Serial.printf("prob: %.3f, avg: %.3f\n", probability, avg);
   401→    count = 0;
   402→  }
   403→
   404→  return avg >= PROBABILITY_CUTOFF;
   405→}

   408→  while (1) {
   409→    digitalWrite(LED_PIN, !digitalRead(LED_PIN));
   410→    delay(200);
   411→  }
   412→}

/*
 * microWakeWord Pretrained Test
 *
 * Tests "Hey Jarvis" wake word detection using microWakeWord TFLite model.
 * Uses EdgeNeuron library with microfrontend for audio preprocessing.
 *
 * Based on: https://github.com/kahrendt/microWakeWord
 * Model: /models/hey_jarvis.tflite on SD card
 *
 * Audio: 16kHz, 16-bit mono
 * Features: 40 bins, 30ms window, 10ms stride
 * Detection: Sliding window probability averaging
 */

#include <EdgeNeuron.h>
#include <driver/i2s.h>
#include <SD.h>
#include <SPI.h>

#include "tensorflow/lite/experimental/microfrontend/lib/frontend.h"
#include "tensorflow/lite/experimental/microfrontend/lib/frontend_util.h"

// Access EdgeNeuron's internal tensors for int8 quantized models
extern TfLiteTensor* tflInputTensor;
extern TfLiteTensor* tflOutputTensor;

// Pins (INMP441 microphone)
#define MIC_BCK  2
#define MIC_WS   4
#define MIC_DIN  18
#define SD_CS    41
#define LED_PIN  1

// Model path on SD card
#define MODEL_PATH "/models/hey_jarvis.tflite"

// Audio config
#define SAMPLE_RATE     16000
#define AUDIO_CHUNK_MS  10
#define AUDIO_CHUNK_SAMPLES (SAMPLE_RATE * AUDIO_CHUNK_MS / 1000)

// Feature config (matches microWakeWord training)
#define FEATURE_WINDOW_MS   30
#define FEATURE_STRIDE_MS   10
#define FEATURE_BINS        40
#define FEATURE_WINDOW_SAMPLES (SAMPLE_RATE * FEATURE_WINDOW_MS / 1000)

// Detection config (from hey_jarvis.json)
#define PROBABILITY_CUTOFF  0.97f
#define SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE 5
#define TENSOR_ARENA_SIZE   30000

// Globals
static uint8_t* tensor_arena = nullptr;
static uint8_t* model_data = nullptr;
static uint32_t model_size = 0;
static FrontendState frontend_state;

// Audio buffers
static int32_t i2s_buffer[512];
static int16_t audio_buffer[FEATURE_WINDOW_SAMPLES];
static int audio_buffer_pos = 0;

// Sliding window for probability averaging
static float probability_window[SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE];
static int window_pos = 0;
static bool window_filled = false;

// Forward declarations
bool initSD();
bool loadModelFromSD(const char* path);
bool initMicrophone();
bool initFrontend();
bool captureAudio();
float runInference();
bool detectWakeword(float probability);
void errorBlink();

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(115200);
  delay(1000);

  pinMode(LED_PIN, OUTPUT);
  digitalWrite(LED_PIN, LOW);

  Serial.println("\n=== microWakeWord Test ===");
  Serial.println("Wake word: \"Hey Jarvis\"");
  Serial.printf("Model: %s\n\n", MODEL_PATH);

  // Allocate tensor arena in PSRAM
  tensor_arena = (uint8_t*)ps_malloc(TENSOR_ARENA_SIZE);
  if (!tensor_arena) {
    Serial.println("ERROR: Arena allocation failed");
    errorBlink();
  }

  // Initialize SD card
  if (!initSD()) {
    Serial.println("ERROR: SD card init failed");
    errorBlink();
  }
  Serial.println("SD Card: OK");

  // Load model from SD
  if (!loadModelFromSD(MODEL_PATH)) {
    Serial.println("ERROR: Model load failed");
    Serial.printf("Copy hey_jarvis.tflite to SD:%s\n", MODEL_PATH);
    errorBlink();
  }
  Serial.printf("Model loaded: %u bytes\n", model_size);

  // Initialize TFLite with EdgeNeuron
  if (!initializeModel(model_data, tensor_arena, TENSOR_ARENA_SIZE)) {
    Serial.println("ERROR: TFLite init failed");
    errorBlink();
  }
  Serial.println("TFLite: OK");

  // Print tensor info
  Serial.printf("  Input: dims=[");
  for (int d = 0; d < tflInputTensor->dims->size; d++) {
    Serial.printf("%d%s", tflInputTensor->dims->data[d],
                  d < tflInputTensor->dims->size - 1 ? "," : "");
  }
  Serial.printf("], type=%d\n", tflInputTensor->type);

  Serial.printf("  Output: dims=[");
  for (int d = 0; d < tflOutputTensor->dims->size; d++) {
    Serial.printf("%d%s", tflOutputTensor->dims->data[d],
                  d < tflOutputTensor->dims->size - 1 ? "," : "");
  }
  Serial.printf("], type=%d\n", tflOutputTensor->type);

  // Initialize microphone
  if (!initMicrophone()) {
    Serial.println("ERROR: Microphone init failed");
    errorBlink();
  }
  Serial.println("Microphone: OK");

  // Initialize microfrontend
  if (!initFrontend()) {
    Serial.println("ERROR: Frontend init failed");
    errorBlink();
  }
  Serial.println("Frontend: OK");

  // Initialize probability window
  for (int i = 0; i < SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE; i++) {
    probability_window[i] = 0.0f;
  }

  Serial.println("\nListening for \"Hey Jarvis\"...");
  Serial.println("================================\n");
}

void loop() {
  // Capture audio and accumulate in buffer
  if (!captureAudio()) {
    return;
  }

  // Once we have enough audio, run inference
  if (audio_buffer_pos >= FEATURE_WINDOW_SAMPLES) {
    float prob = runInference();

    // Check detection with sliding window
    if (detectWakeword(prob)) {
      Serial.println("\n>>> HEY JARVIS DETECTED! <<<\n");
      digitalWrite(LED_PIN, HIGH);
      delay(500);
      digitalWrite(LED_PIN, LOW);

      // Reset window after detection
      for (int i = 0; i < SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE; i++) {
        probability_window[i] = 0.0f;
      }
      window_filled = false;
    }

    // Shift audio buffer by stride (keep overlap)
    int stride_samples = SAMPLE_RATE * FEATURE_STRIDE_MS / 1000;
    int overlap = FEATURE_WINDOW_SAMPLES - stride_samples;
    memmove(audio_buffer, audio_buffer + stride_samples, overlap * sizeof(int16_t));
    audio_buffer_pos = overlap;
  }
}

bool initMicrophone() {
  i2s_config_t config = {
    .mode = (i2s_mode_t)(I2S_MODE_MASTER | I2S_MODE_RX),
    .sample_rate = SAMPLE_RATE,
    .bits_per_sample = I2S_BITS_PER_SAMPLE_32BIT,
    .channel_format = I2S_CHANNEL_FMT_ONLY_LEFT,
    .communication_format = I2S_COMM_FORMAT_STAND_I2S,
    .intr_alloc_flags = ESP_INTR_FLAG_LEVEL1,
    .dma_buf_count = 4,
    .dma_buf_len = 256,
    .use_apll = false
  };

  i2s_pin_config_t pins = {
    .bck_io_num = MIC_BCK,
    .ws_io_num = MIC_WS,
    .data_out_num = I2S_PIN_NO_CHANGE,
    .data_in_num = MIC_DIN
  };

  return (i2s_driver_install(I2S_NUM_0, &config, 0, NULL) == ESP_OK &&
          i2s_set_pin(I2S_NUM_0, &pins) == ESP_OK);
}

bool initFrontend() {
  FrontendConfig config;
  config.window.size_ms = FEATURE_WINDOW_MS;
  config.window.step_size_ms = FEATURE_STRIDE_MS;
  config.filterbank.num_channels = FEATURE_BINS;
  config.filterbank.lower_band_limit = 125.0f;
  config.filterbank.upper_band_limit = 7500.0f;
  config.noise_reduction.smoothing_bits = 10;
  config.noise_reduction.even_smoothing = 0.025f;
  config.noise_reduction.odd_smoothing = 0.06f;
  config.noise_reduction.min_signal_remaining = 0.05f;
  config.pcan_gain_control.enable_pcan = 1;
  config.pcan_gain_control.strength = 0.95f;
  config.pcan_gain_control.offset = 80.0f;
  config.pcan_gain_control.gain_bits = 21;
  config.log_scale.enable_log = 1;
  config.log_scale.scale_shift = 6;

  return FrontendPopulateState(&config, &frontend_state, SAMPLE_RATE);
}

bool initSD() {
  SPI.begin(39, 40, 38, SD_CS);  // SCK, MISO, MOSI, CS
  return SD.begin(SD_CS);
}

bool loadModelFromSD(const char* path) {
  File f = SD.open(path);
  if (!f) {
    Serial.printf("Cannot open: %s\n", path);
    return false;
  }

  model_size = f.size();
  model_data = (uint8_t*)ps_malloc(model_size);
  if (!model_data) {
    Serial.println("Model allocation failed");
    f.close();
    return false;
  }

  f.read(model_data, model_size);
  f.close();
  return true;
}

bool captureAudio() {
  size_t bytes_read;
  if (i2s_read(I2S_NUM_0, i2s_buffer, sizeof(i2s_buffer), &bytes_read, 10) != ESP_OK) {
    return false;
  }

  int samples = bytes_read / 4;
  for (int i = 0; i < samples && audio_buffer_pos < FEATURE_WINDOW_SAMPLES; i++) {
    // Convert 32-bit I2S to 16-bit with gain
    int32_t sample = i2s_buffer[i] >> 14;
    audio_buffer[audio_buffer_pos++] = constrain(sample, -32768, 32767);
  }

  return true;
}

float runInference() {
  // Generate features using microfrontend
  size_t num_samples_read;
  FrontendOutput frontend_output = FrontendProcessSamples(
      &frontend_state, audio_buffer, FEATURE_WINDOW_SAMPLES, &num_samples_read);

  if (frontend_output.size != FEATURE_BINS) {
    return 0.0f;
  }

  // Copy features to input tensor (handle quantized int8)
  if (tflInputTensor->type == kTfLiteInt8) {
    int8_t* input_data = tflInputTensor->data.int8;
    float input_scale = tflInputTensor->params.scale;
    int input_zero_point = tflInputTensor->params.zero_point;

    for (size_t i = 0; i < frontend_output.size; i++) {
      float value = frontend_output.values[i] * 0.0390625f;  // /25.6
      int32_t quantized = (int32_t)(value / input_scale) + input_zero_point;
      input_data[i] = constrain(quantized, -128, 127);
    }
  } else {
    // Float model
    float* input_data = tflInputTensor->data.f;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < frontend_output.size; i++) {
      input_data[i] = frontend_output.values[i] * 0.0390625f;
    }
  }

  // Run inference
  if (!runModelInference()) {
    Serial.println("Invoke failed");
    return 0.0f;
  }

  // Get output probability (handle quantized int8)
  float probability;
  if (tflOutputTensor->type == kTfLiteInt8) {
    int8_t output_value = tflOutputTensor->data.int8[0];
    probability = (output_value - tflOutputTensor->params.zero_point) *
                  tflOutputTensor->params.scale;
  } else {
    probability = tflOutputTensor->data.f[0];
  }

  return probability;
}

bool detectWakeword(float probability) {
  // Add to sliding window
  probability_window[window_pos] = probability;
  window_pos = (window_pos + 1) % SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE;

  if (window_pos == 0) {
    window_filled = true;
  }

  // Don't trigger until window is filled
  if (!window_filled) {
    return false;
  }

  // Calculate average probability
  float avg = 0.0f;
  for (int i = 0; i < SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE; i++) {
    avg += probability_window[i];
  }
  avg /= SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE;

  // Debug output
  static int count = 0;
  if (++count >= 10) {
    Serial.printf("prob: %.3f, avg: %.3f\n", probability, avg);
    count = 0;
  }

  return avg >= PROBABILITY_CUTOFF;
}

void errorBlink() {
  while (1) {
    digitalWrite(LED_PIN, !digitalRead(LED_PIN));
    delay(200);
  }
}

# microWakeWord Pretrained Test

Tests wake word detection using pre-trained microWakeWord TFLite models with EdgeNeuron library.

**Wake word: "Hey Jarvis"**

## How It Works

1. **Audio capture**: INMP441 microphone at 16kHz, 16-bit mono
2. **Feature extraction**: Microfrontend generates 40-bin spectrogram features
3. **Inference**: EdgeNeuron runs TFLite model every 10ms
4. **Detection**: Sliding window averages probabilities, triggers at 97% threshold

## Setup

### 1. Install EdgeNeuron Library

Via Arduino Library Manager, search for "EdgeNeuron" by Consentium IoT.

Or install from: https://github.com/ConsentiumIoT/EdgeNeuron

### 2. Copy Model to SD Card

Create this folder structure on your SD card:
\```
SD Card/
└── models/
    └── hey_jarvis.tflite
\```

Copy the model from:
\```
_STASH_/micro-wake-word-models/models/v2/hey_jarvis.tflite
\```

### 3. Board Settings

- Board: ESP32S3 Dev Module
- PSRAM: OPI PSRAM
- Flash Size: 16MB

### 4. Upload and Test

1. Insert SD card with model
2. Upload sketch
3. Open Serial Monitor (115200 baud)
4. Say "Hey Jarvis" - LED lights up on detection

## Expected Output

\```
=== microWakeWord Test ===
Wake word: "Hey Jarvis"
Model: /models/hey_jarvis.tflite

SD Card: OK
Model loaded: 51234 bytes
TFLite: OK
  Input: dims=[1,1,40], type=9
  Output: dims=[1,1], type=9
Microphone: OK
Frontend: OK

Listening for "Hey Jarvis"...
================================

prob: 0.012, avg: 0.008
prob: 0.967, avg: 0.612
prob: 0.994, avg: 0.971

>>> HEY JARVIS DETECTED! <<<
\```

## Model Parameters

From `hey_jarvis.json`:
- **probability_cutoff**: 0.97 (97% confidence)
- **feature_step_size**: 10ms
- **sliding_window_size**: 5 frames
- **tensor_arena_size**: ~23KB

## Available Models

From [micro-wake-word-models](https://github.com/esphome/micro-wake-word-models):

| Model | Wake Word |
|-------|-----------|
| hey_jarvis.tflite | "Hey Jarvis" |
| okay_nabu.tflite | "Okay Nabu" |
| alexa.tflite | "Alexa" |
| hey_mycroft.tflite | "Hey Mycroft" |

Just copy a different model to `/models/` on SD and update `MODEL_PATH` in the sketch.

## Troubleshooting

### "Model load failed"
- Check SD card has `/models/hey_jarvis.tflite`
- Try reformatting SD card as FAT32

### "TFLite init failed"
- Increase TENSOR_ARENA_SIZE if needed
- Check serial for specific error

### No detection / false positives
- Adjust PROBABILITY_CUTOFF (lower = more sensitive)
- Check microphone gain
- Speak clearly, closer to microphone

## Sources

- [microWakeWord](https://github.com/kahrendt/microWakeWord)
- [micro-wake-word-models](https://github.com/esphome/micro-wake-word-models)
- [EdgeNeuron](https://github.com/ConsentiumIoT/EdgeNeuron)

## microWakeWord Overview

microWakeWord is an open-source wakeword library for detecting custom wake words on low power devices. It produces models that are suitable for using TensorFlow Lite for Microcontrollers.

### Streaming Model Architecture

The streaming model performs inferences every 30 ms, where the initial convolution layer strides over three 10 ms slices of audio. The model is a neural network using MixConv mixed depthwise convolutions suitable for streaming.(no content)Google Research published streaming keyword spotting approaches with source code that makes it easy to train models that predict the wake word in a streaming fashion. This approach saves a lot of computational effort, as the model does not reprocess older audio slices for every inference. microWakeWord was written to develop streaming wake word models suitable for ESP32-S3 devices.

### ESP32 Implementation

The ESPHome component adds support for detecting wake words on an ESP32-S3 device using quantized TensorFlow models created with microWakeWord.(no content)Wake word detection is done entirely with TensorFlow Lite Micro. The target devices are ESP32-S3 based with external PSRAM. It may run on a regular ESP32 but may not perform as well.(no content)The model executes an inference in under 10 ms on an ESP32-S3, much faster than the 20 ms stride length.

---

# TFLite Interpreter Initialization with Resource Variables

Yes, this code uses `MicroResourceVariables` for special handling of VAR_HANDLE operations.

## Initialization Process

The interpreter is created in `load_model_()` with resource variable support:

```cpp
this->interpreter_ =
    make_unique<tflite::MicroInterpreter>(tflite::GetModel(this->model_start_), 
                                          this->streaming_op_resolver_,
                                          this->tensor_arena_, 
                                          this->tensor_arena_size_, 
                                          this->mrv_);
```

## Resource Variables Setup

Before interpreter creation, the code establishes the resource variable infrastructure:

1. **Allocates a separate arena** for variable tensors:
   ```cpp
   this->var_arena_ = arena_allocator.allocate(STREAMING_MODEL_VARIABLE_ARENA_SIZE);
   ```

2. **Creates a MicroAllocator** for managing that arena:
   ```cpp
   this->ma_ = tflite::MicroAllocator::Create(this->var_arena_, 
                                              STREAMING_MODEL_VARIABLE_ARENA_SIZE);
   ```

3. **Instantiates MicroResourceVariables**:
   ```cpp
   this->mrv_ = tflite::MicroResourceVariables::Create(this->ma_, 20);
   ```

The `mrv_` object is then passed to the `MicroInterpreter` constructor, enabling support for variable handle operations registered via `AddVarHandle()` in the operation resolver.
