    urllib.request.urlretrieve(
        "https://mcdermottlab.mit.edu/Reverb/IRMAudio/Audio.zip", ir_zip)
    with zipfile.ZipFile(ir_zip, 'r') as z:
        z.extractall(MIT_IR_DIR)
print("Done!")</cell id="cell-10">
<cell id="cell-11"># Cell 8: Download AudioSet background noise
AUDIOSET_DIR = AUGMENTATION_DIR / 'audioset'
AUDIOSET_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
tar_file = AUDIOSET_DIR / 'unbal_train00.tar'

print("Downloading AudioSet subset...")
if not tar_file.exists():
    !wget -q --show-progress -O {tar_file} \
        'https://huggingface.co/datasets/agkphysics/AudioSet/resolve/main/data/unbal_train00.tar'

print("Done!")</cell id="cell-11">
<cell id="cell-12"># Cell 9: Download negative features from HuggingFace
from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download

NEGATIVE_DIR = FEATURES_DIR / 'negatives'
NEGATIVE_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

NEGATIVE_FILES = [
    'speech_features.npy',
    'dinner_party_train.npy', 
    'dinner_party_eval.npy',
    'nonspeech_features.npy'
]

print("Downloading negative features...")
for fname in NEGATIVE_FILES:
    try:
        hf_hub_download(
            repo_id='kahrendt/microwakeword',
            filename=f'features/{fname}',
            local_dir=str(NEGATIVE_DIR),
            repo_type='dataset'
        )
        print(f"  {fname}")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"  Failed {fname}: {e}")
print("Done!")</cell id="cell-12">
<cell id="cell-13"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## Step 4: Generate Spectrogram Features</cell id="cell-13">
<cell id="cell-14"># Cell 10: Configure augmentation
from microwakeword.feature_generation import Augmentation

augmentation = Augmentation(
    augmentation_duration=3.2,
    ir_paths=[str(MIT_IR_DIR / 'Audio')],
    background_paths=[str(AUDIOSET_DIR)],
    parametric_eq_probability=0.1,
    distortion_probability=0.1,
    pitch_shift_probability=0.1,
    band_stop_filter_probability=0.1,
    colored_noise_probability=0.1,
    background_noise_probability=0.75,
    gain_probability=1.0,
    ir_probability=0.5,
    snr_range=(-5, 10),
    jitter_range=(195, 205),
)
print("Augmentation configured")</cell id="cell-14">
<cell id="cell-15"># Cell 11: Generate spectrogram features
from microwakeword.feature_generation import Clips, SpectrogramGeneration
from mmap_ninja import RaggedMmap

POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR = FEATURES_DIR / 'positive'
POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

clips = Clips(str(training_dir))
print(f"Loaded {len(clips)} audio clips")

spec_gen = SpectrogramGeneration()

print("Generating training features...")
train_features_dir = POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR / 'train'
RaggedMmap.from_generator(
    out_dir=str(train_features_dir),
    sample_generator=spec_gen.generate_features(
        clips=clips,
        augmentation=augmentation,
        slide_frames=10,
    ),
    batch_size=1000,
    verbose=True
)

print("\nGenerating validation features...")
val_features_dir = POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR / 'val'
RaggedMmap.from_generator(
    out_dir=str(val_features_dir),
    sample_generator=spec_gen.generate_features(
        clips=clips,
        augmentation=None,
        slide_frames=1,
    ),
    batch_size=1000,
    verbose=True
)
print("\nDone!")</cell id="cell-15">
<cell id="cell-16"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## Step 5: Configure Training</cell id="cell-16">
<cell id="cell-17"># Cell 12: Create training config
import yaml

training_config = {
    'model_name': WAKE_WORD_ID,
    'window_step_ms': 10,
    'batch_size': 128,
    'training_steps': 10000,
    'learning_rate': 0.001,
    'positive_class_weight': 1,
    'negative_class_weight': 20,
    'datasets': {
        'positive_train': {'path': str(train_features_dir), 'sampling_weight': 2.0, 'penalty_weight': 1.0},
        'positive_val': {'path': str(val_features_dir), 'sampling_weight': 0.0, 'penalty_weight': 1.0},
        'speech_negatives': {'path': str(NEGATIVE_DIR / 'features/speech_features.npy'), 'sampling_weight': 10.0, 'penalty_weight': 1.0},
        'dinner_party_train': {'path': str(NEGATIVE_DIR / 'features/dinner_party_train.npy'), 'sampling_weight': 10.0, 'penalty_weight': 1.0},
        'nonspeech': {'path': str(NEGATIVE_DIR / 'features/nonspeech_features.npy'), 'sampling_weight': 5.0, 'penalty_weight': 1.0},
    },
    'eval_every_n_steps': 500,
    'selection_metric': 'average_viable_recall',
    'selection_maximize': True,
    'viable_loss_target': 0.9,
}

config_path = WORK_DIR / 'training_config.yaml'
with open(config_path, 'w') as f:
    yaml.dump(training_config, f, default_flow_style=False)

print(f"Config saved: {config_path}")</cell id="cell-17">
<cell id="cell-18"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## Step 6: Train the Model</cell id="cell-18">
<cell id="cell-19"># Cell 13: Train (~30-60 minutes)
print("Starting training...\n")

!python -m microwakeword.model_train_eval \
    --training_config='{config_path}' \
    --train 1 \
    --test_tflite_streaming_quantized 1 \
    --use_weights 'best_weights' \
    mixednet \
    --pointwise_filters_per_block '64,64,64,64' \
    --repeat_count_per_block '1,1,1,1' \
    --mixconv_kernel_sizes '[5], [7,11], [9,15], [23]' \
    --residual_connections '0,0,0,0' \
    --initial_filters 32 \
    --initial_kernel 5 \
    --stride 3 \
    --clip_duration_ms 1500</cell id="cell-19">
<cell id="cell-20"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## Step 7: Export Model</cell id="cell-20">
<cell id="cell-21"># Cell 14: Package trained model
import shutil

model_paths = list(Path('trained_models').rglob('stream_state_internal_quant.tflite'))

if not model_paths:
    print("ERROR: No trained model found!")
else:
    model_path = model_paths[0]
    output_model = MODEL_DIR / f'{WAKE_WORD_ID}.tflite'
    shutil.copy(model_path, output_model)
    print(f"Model: {output_model}")
    print(f"Size: {output_model.stat().st_size:,} bytes")</cell id="cell-21">
<cell id="cell-22"># Cell 15: Create manifest
manifest = {
    'type': 'micro',
    'wake_word': WAKE_WORD,
    'model': f'{WAKE_WORD_ID}.tflite',
    'version': 1,
    'micro': {'probability_cutoff': 0.5, 'sliding_window_average_size': 10}
}

manifest_path = MODEL_DIR / f'{WAKE_WORD_ID}.json'

print(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2))</cell id="cell-22">

import zipfile

print("Done!")</cell id="cell-10">

<cell id="cell-12"># Cell 9: Download negative features from HuggingFace
from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download

NEGATIVE_DIR = FEATURES_DIR / 'negatives'
NEGATIVE_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

NEGATIVE_FILES = [
    'speech_features.npy',
    'dinner_party_train.npy', 
    'dinner_party_eval.npy',
    'nonspeech_features.npy'
]

print("Downloading negative features...")
for fname in NEGATIVE_FILES:
    try:
        hf_hub_download(
            repo_id='kahrendt/microwakeword',
            filename=f'features/{fname}',
            local_dir=str(NEGATIVE_DIR),
            repo_type='dataset'

        print(f"  {fname}")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"  Failed {fname}: {e}")

<cell id="cell-13"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## Step 4: Generate Spectrogram Features</cell id="cell-13">
<cell id="cell-14"># Cell 10: Configure augmentation
from microwakeword.feature_generation import Augmentation

augmentation = Augmentation(
    augmentation_duration=3.2,
    ir_paths=[str(MIT_IR_DIR / 'Audio')],
    background_paths=[str(AUDIOSET_DIR)],
    parametric_eq_probability=0.1,
    distortion_probability=0.1,
    pitch_shift_probability=0.1,
    band_stop_filter_probability=0.1,
    colored_noise_probability=0.1,
    background_noise_probability=0.75,
    gain_probability=1.0,
    ir_probability=0.5,
    snr_range=(-5, 10),
    jitter_range=(195, 205),
)
print("Augmentation configured")</cell id="cell-14">
<cell id="cell-15"># Cell 11: Generate spectrogram features
from microwakeword.feature_generation import Clips, SpectrogramGeneration
from mmap_ninja import RaggedMmap

POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR = FEATURES_DIR / 'positive'
POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

clips = Clips(str(training_dir))
print(f"Loaded {len(clips)} audio clips")

spec_gen = SpectrogramGeneration()

print("Generating training features...")
train_features_dir = POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR / 'train'
RaggedMmap.from_generator(
    out_dir=str(train_features_dir),
    sample_generator=spec_gen.generate_features(
        clips=clips,
        augmentation=augmentation,
        slide_frames=10,
    ),
    batch_size=1000,
    verbose=True
)

print("\nGenerating validation features...")
val_features_dir = POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR / 'val'
RaggedMmap.from_generator(
    out_dir=str(val_features_dir),
    sample_generator=spec_gen.generate_features(
        clips=clips,
        augmentation=None,
        slide_frames=1,
    ),
    batch_size=1000,
    verbose=True
)
print("\nDone!")</cell id="cell-15">
<cell id="cell-16"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## Step 5: Configure Training</cell id="cell-16">
<cell id="cell-17"># Cell 12: Create training config
import yaml

training_config = {
    'model_name': WAKE_WORD_ID,
    'window_step_ms': 10,
    'batch_size': 128,
    'training_steps': 10000,
    'learning_rate': 0.001,
    'positive_class_weight': 1,
    'negative_class_weight': 20,
    'datasets': {
        'positive_train': {'path': str(train_features_dir), 'sampling_weight': 2.0, 'penalty_weight': 1.0},
        'positive_val': {'path': str(val_features_dir), 'sampling_weight': 0.0, 'penalty_weight': 1.0},
        'speech_negatives': {'path': str(NEGATIVE_DIR / 'features/speech_features.npy'), 'sampling_weight': 10.0, 'penalty_weight': 1.0},
        'dinner_party_train': {'path': str(NEGATIVE_DIR / 'features/dinner_party_train.npy'), 'sampling_weight': 10.0, 'penalty_weight': 1.0},
        'nonspeech': {'path': str(NEGATIVE_DIR / 'features/nonspeech_features.npy'), 'sampling_weight': 5.0, 'penalty_weight': 1.0},
    },
    'eval_every_n_steps': 500,
    'selection_metric': 'average_viable_recall',
    'selection_maximize': True,
    'viable_loss_target': 0.9,
}

config_path = WORK_DIR / 'training_config.yaml'
with open(config_path, 'w') as f:
    yaml.dump(training_config, f, default_flow_style=False)

print(f"Config saved: {config_path}")</cell id="cell-17">

!python -m microwakeword.model_train_eval \
    --training_config='{config_path}' \
    --train 1 \
    --test_tflite_streaming_quantized 1 \
    --use_weights 'best_weights' \
    mixednet \
    --pointwise_filters_per_block '64,64,64,64' \
    --repeat_count_per_block '1,1,1,1' \
    --mixconv_kernel_sizes '[5], [7,11], [9,15], [23]' \
    --residual_connections '0,0,0,0' \
    --initial_filters 32 \
    --initial_kernel 5 \
    --stride 3 \
    --clip_duration_ms 1500</cell id="cell-19">

<cell id="cell-0"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type># microWakeWord Training Notebook

Train a custom wake word detection model compatible with ESP32-S3.

## Overview

This notebook trains models compatible with `wakeword_pretrained_test.ino`:
- **Input**: 40-bin log-mel spectrogram features (30ms window, 10ms stride)
- **Architecture**: MixNet-based streaming model
- **Output**: Quantized TFLite model for ESP32

Based on: https://github.com/kahrendt/microWakeWord</cell id="cell-0">

        "https://mcdermottlab.mit.edu/Reverb/IRMAudio/Audio.zip", ir_zip)
    with zipfile.ZipFile(ir_zip, 'r') as z:
        z.extractall(MIT_IR_DIR)
print("Done!")</cell id="cell-10">

print("Downloading AudioSet subset...")

<cell id="cell-12"># Cell 9: Download negative features from HuggingFace
from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download

NEGATIVE_DIR = FEATURES_DIR / 'negatives'
NEGATIVE_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

NEGATIVE_FILES = [
    'speech_features.npy',

]

print("Downloading negative features...")
for fname in NEGATIVE_FILES:

<cell id="cell-13"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## Step 4: Generate Spectrogram Features</cell id="cell-13">
<cell id="cell-14"># Cell 10: Configure augmentation
from microwakeword.feature_generation import Augmentation

augmentation = Augmentation(
    augmentation_duration=3.2,
    ir_paths=[str(MIT_IR_DIR / 'Audio')],
    background_paths=[str(AUDIOSET_DIR)],
    parametric_eq_probability=0.1,
    distortion_probability=0.1,
    pitch_shift_probability=0.1,
    band_stop_filter_probability=0.1,
    colored_noise_probability=0.1,
    background_noise_probability=0.75,
    gain_probability=1.0,
    ir_probability=0.5,
    snr_range=(-5, 10),
    jitter_range=(195, 205),
)
print("Augmentation configured")</cell id="cell-14">
<cell id="cell-15"># Cell 11: Generate spectrogram features
from microwakeword.feature_generation import Clips, SpectrogramGeneration
from mmap_ninja import RaggedMmap

POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR = FEATURES_DIR / 'positive'
POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

clips = Clips(str(training_dir))
print(f"Loaded {len(clips)} audio clips")

spec_gen = SpectrogramGeneration()

print("Generating training features...")
train_features_dir = POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR / 'train'
RaggedMmap.from_generator(
    out_dir=str(train_features_dir),
    sample_generator=spec_gen.generate_features(
        clips=clips,
        augmentation=augmentation,
        slide_frames=10,
    ),
    batch_size=1000,
    verbose=True
)

print("\nGenerating validation features...")
val_features_dir = POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR / 'val'
RaggedMmap.from_generator(
    out_dir=str(val_features_dir),
    sample_generator=spec_gen.generate_features(
        clips=clips,
        augmentation=None,
        slide_frames=1,
    ),
    batch_size=1000,
    verbose=True
)
print("\nDone!")</cell id="cell-15">

training_config = {
    'model_name': WAKE_WORD_ID,
    'window_step_ms': 10,
    'batch_size': 128,
    'training_steps': 10000,
    'learning_rate': 0.001,
    'positive_class_weight': 1,
    'negative_class_weight': 20,
    'datasets': {
        'positive_train': {'path': str(train_features_dir), 'sampling_weight': 2.0, 'penalty_weight': 1.0},
        'positive_val': {'path': str(val_features_dir), 'sampling_weight': 0.0, 'penalty_weight': 1.0},
        'speech_negatives': {'path': str(NEGATIVE_DIR / 'features/speech_features.npy'), 'sampling_weight': 10.0, 'penalty_weight': 1.0},
        'dinner_party_train': {'path': str(NEGATIVE_DIR / 'features/dinner_party_train.npy'), 'sampling_weight': 10.0, 'penalty_weight': 1.0},
        'nonspeech': {'path': str(NEGATIVE_DIR / 'features/nonspeech_features.npy'), 'sampling_weight': 5.0, 'penalty_weight': 1.0},
    },
    'eval_every_n_steps': 500,
    'selection_metric': 'average_viable_recall',

}

# generate_samples.py Usage

Based on the documentation, the basic command structure is:

```
python3 generate_samples.py '<text>' --model <model_path> --max-samples <number> --output-dir <directory>
```

## Required Arguments

- **Text**: Pass the phrase to synthesize as the first argument in quotes (e.g., `'okay piper.'`)
- **`--model`**: Path to either a Piper voice file (`.onnx`) or generator model (`.pt`)
- **`--output-dir`**: Directory where WAV files will be saved

## Optional Arguments

The tool accepts several configuration options:

- **`--max-samples`**: Number of audio samples to generate
- **`--batch-size`**: Process multiple samples simultaneously (useful with GPU acceleration)
- **`--length-scales`**: Adjust speaking speeds
- **`--max-speakers`**: Limit speaker count (for generator model; recommend <904)
- **`--slerp-weights`**: Control speaker blending (generator only)

You can specify multiple `--model` arguments to cycle between different voices during generation. For detailed options, run with the `--help` flag.

<cell id="cell-0"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type># microWakeWord Training Notebook

Train a custom wake word detection model compatible with ESP32-S3.

## Overview

This notebook trains models compatible with `wakeword_pretrained_test.ino`:
- **Input**: 40-bin log-mel spectrogram features (30ms window, 10ms stride)
- **Architecture**: MixNet-based streaming model
- **Output**: Quantized TFLite model for ESP32

Based on: https://github.com/kahrendt/microWakeWord</cell id="cell-0">

<cell id="cell-14"># Cell 10: Configure augmentation
from microwakeword.feature_generation import Augmentation

augmentation = Augmentation(
    augmentation_duration=3.2,
    ir_paths=[str(MIT_IR_DIR / 'Audio')],
    background_paths=[str(AUDIOSET_DIR)],
    parametric_eq_probability=0.1,
    distortion_probability=0.1,
    pitch_shift_probability=0.1,
    band_stop_filter_probability=0.1,
    colored_noise_probability=0.1,
    background_noise_probability=0.75,
    gain_probability=1.0,
    ir_probability=0.5,
    snr_range=(-5, 10),
    jitter_range=(195, 205),
)
print("Augmentation configured")</cell id="cell-14">
<cell id="cell-15"># Cell 11: Generate spectrogram features
from microwakeword.feature_generation import Clips, SpectrogramGeneration
from mmap_ninja import RaggedMmap

POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR = FEATURES_DIR / 'positive'
POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

clips = Clips(str(training_dir))
print(f"Loaded {len(clips)} audio clips")

spec_gen = SpectrogramGeneration()

print("Generating training features...")
train_features_dir = POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR / 'train'
RaggedMmap.from_generator(
    out_dir=str(train_features_dir),
    sample_generator=spec_gen.generate_features(
        clips=clips,
        augmentation=augmentation,
        slide_frames=10,
    ),
    batch_size=1000,
    verbose=True
)

print("\nGenerating validation features...")
val_features_dir = POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR / 'val'
RaggedMmap.from_generator(
    out_dir=str(val_features_dir),
    sample_generator=spec_gen.generate_features(
        clips=clips,
        augmentation=None,
        slide_frames=1,
    ),
    batch_size=1000,
    verbose=True
)
print("\nDone!")</cell id="cell-15">

<cell id="cell-0"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type># Training a microWakeWord Model

This notebook steps you through training a basic microWakeWord model. It is intended as a **starting point** for advanced users. You should use Python 3.10.

**The model generated will most likely not be usable for everyday use; it may be difficult to trigger or falsely activates too frequently. You will most likely have to experiment with many different settings to obtain a decent model!**

In the comment at the start of certain blocks, I note some specific settings to consider modifying.

This runs on Google Colab, but is extremely slow compared to training on a local GPU. If you must use Colab, be sure to Change the runtime type to a GPU. Even then, it still slow!

At the end of this notebook, you will be able to download a tflite file. To use this in ESPHome, you need to write a model manifest JSON file. See the [ESPHome documentation](https://esphome.io/components/micro_wake_word) for the details and the [model repo](https://github.com/esphome/micro-wake-word-models/tree/main/models/v2) for examples.</cell id="cell-0">

<cell id="cell-4"># Downloads audio data for augmentation. This can be slow!
# Borrowed from openWakeWord's automatic_model_training.ipynb, accessed March 4, 2024
#
# **Important note!** The data downloaded here has a mixture of difference
# licenses and usage restrictions. As such, any custom models trained with this
# data should be considered as appropriate for **non-commercial** personal use only.


import datasets
import scipy
import os

import numpy as np

from pathlib import Path
from tqdm import tqdm

## Download MIR RIR data

output_dir = "./mit_rirs"
if not os.path.exists(output_dir):
    os.mkdir(output_dir)
    rir_dataset = datasets.load_dataset("davidscripka/MIT_environmental_impulse_responses", split="train", streaming=True)
    # Save clips to 16-bit PCM wav files
    for row in tqdm(rir_dataset):
        name = row['audio']['path'].split('/')[-1]
        scipy.io.wavfile.write(os.path.join(output_dir, name), 16000, (row['audio']['array']*32767).astype(np.int16))

## Download noise and background audio

# Audioset Dataset (https://research.google.com/audioset/dataset/index.html)
# Download one part of the audioset .tar files, extract, and convert to 16khz
# For full-scale training, it's recommended to download the entire dataset from
# https://huggingface.co/datasets/agkphysics/AudioSet, and
# even potentially combine it with other background noise datasets (e.g., FSD50k, Freesound, etc.)

if not os.path.exists("audioset"):
    os.mkdir("audioset")

    fname = "bal_train09.tar"
    out_dir = f"audioset/{fname}"
    link = "https://huggingface.co/datasets/agkphysics/AudioSet/resolve/main/data/" + fname
    !wget -O {out_dir} {link}
    !cd audioset && tar -xf bal_train09.tar

    output_dir = "./audioset_16k"
    if not os.path.exists(output_dir):
        os.mkdir(output_dir)

    # Save clips to 16-bit PCM wav files
    audioset_dataset = datasets.Dataset.from_dict({"audio": [str(i) for i in Path("audioset/audio").glob("**/*.flac")]})
    audioset_dataset = audioset_dataset.cast_column("audio", datasets.Audio(sampling_rate=16000))
    for row in tqdm(audioset_dataset):
        name = row['audio']['path'].split('/')[-1].replace(".flac", ".wav")
        scipy.io.wavfile.write(os.path.join(output_dir, name), 16000, (row['audio']['array']*32767).astype(np.int16))

# Free Music Archive dataset
# https://github.com/mdeff/fma
# (Third-party mchl914 extra small set)

output_dir = "./fma"
if not os.path.exists(output_dir):
    os.mkdir(output_dir)
    fname = "fma_xs.zip"
    link = "https://huggingface.co/datasets/mchl914/fma_xsmall/resolve/main/" + fname
    out_dir = f"fma/{fname}"
    !wget -O {out_dir} {link}
    !cd {output_dir} && unzip -q {fname}

    output_dir = "./fma_16k"
    if not os.path.exists(output_dir):
        os.mkdir(output_dir)

    # Save clips to 16-bit PCM wav files
    fma_dataset = datasets.Dataset.from_dict({"audio": [str(i) for i in Path("fma/fma_small").glob("**/*.mp3")]})
    fma_dataset = fma_dataset.cast_column("audio", datasets.Audio(sampling_rate=16000))
    for row in tqdm(fma_dataset):
        name = row['audio']['path'].split('/')[-1].replace(".mp3", ".wav")
        scipy.io.wavfile.write(os.path.join(output_dir, name), 16000, (row['audio']['array']*32767).astype(np.int16))
</cell id="cell-4">
<cell id="cell-5"># Sets up the augmentations.
# To improve your model, experiment with these settings and use more sources of
# background clips.

from microwakeword.audio.augmentation import Augmentation
from microwakeword.audio.clips import Clips
from microwakeword.audio.spectrograms import SpectrogramGeneration

clips = Clips(input_directory='generated_samples',
              file_pattern='*.wav',
              max_clip_duration_s=None,
              remove_silence=False,
              random_split_seed=10,
              split_count=0.1,
              )
augmenter = Augmentation(augmentation_duration_s=3.2,
                         augmentation_probabilities = {
                                "SevenBandParametricEQ": 0.1,
                                "TanhDistortion": 0.1,
                                "PitchShift": 0.1,
                                "BandStopFilter": 0.1,
                                "AddColorNoise": 0.1,
                                "AddBackgroundNoise": 0.75,
                                "Gain": 1.0,
                                "RIR": 0.5,
                            },
                         impulse_paths = ['mit_rirs'],
                         background_paths = ['fma_16k', 'audioset_16k'],
                         background_min_snr_db = -5,
                         background_max_snr_db = 10,
                         min_jitter_s = 0.195,
                         max_jitter_s = 0.205,
                         )
</cell id="cell-5">
<cell id="cell-6"># Augment a random clip and play it back to verify it works well

from IPython.display import Audio
from microwakeword.audio.audio_utils import save_clip

random_clip = clips.get_random_clip()
augmented_clip = augmenter.augment_clip(random_clip)
save_clip(augmented_clip, 'augmented_clip.wav')

Audio("augmented_clip.wav", autoplay=True)</cell id="cell-6">
<cell id="cell-7"># Augment samples and save the training, validation, and testing sets.
# Validating and testing samples generated the same way can make the model
# benchmark better than it performs in real-word use. Use real samples or TTS
# samples generated with a different TTS engine to potentially get more accurate
# benchmarks.

import os
from mmap_ninja.ragged import RaggedMmap

output_dir = 'generated_augmented_features'

if not os.path.exists(output_dir):
    os.mkdir(output_dir)

splits = ["training", "validation", "testing"]
for split in splits:
  out_dir = os.path.join(output_dir, split)
  if not os.path.exists(out_dir):
      os.mkdir(out_dir)


  split_name = "train"
  repetition = 2

  spectrograms = SpectrogramGeneration(clips=clips,
                                     augmenter=augmenter,
                                     slide_frames=10,    # Uses the same spectrogram repeatedly, just shifted over by one frame. This simulates the streaming inferences while training/validating in nonstreaming mode.
                                     step_ms=10,
                                     )
  if split == "validation":
    split_name = "validation"
    repetition = 1
  elif split == "testing":
    split_name = "test"
    repetition = 1
    spectrograms = SpectrogramGeneration(clips=clips,
                                     augmenter=augmenter,
                                     slide_frames=1,    # The testing set uses the streaming version of the model, so no artificial repetition is necessary
                                     step_ms=10,
                                     )

  RaggedMmap.from_generator(
      out_dir=os.path.join(out_dir, 'wakeword_mmap'),
      sample_generator=spectrograms.spectrogram_generator(split=split_name, repeat=repetition),
      batch_size=100,
      verbose=True,
  )</cell id="cell-7">

<cell id="cell-9"># Save a yaml config that controls the training process
# These hyperparamters can make a huge different in model quality.
# Experiment with sampling and penalty weights and increasing the number of
# training steps.

import yaml
import os

config = {}

config["window_step_ms"] = 10

config["train_dir"] = (
    "trained_models/wakeword"
)


# Each feature_dir should have at least one of the following folders with this structure:
#  training/
#    ragged_mmap_folders_ending_in_mmap
#  testing/
#    ragged_mmap_folders_ending_in_mmap
#  testing_ambient/
#    ragged_mmap_folders_ending_in_mmap
#  validation/
#    ragged_mmap_folders_ending_in_mmap
#  validation_ambient/
#    ragged_mmap_folders_ending_in_mmap
#
#  sampling_weight: Weight for choosing a spectrogram from this set in the batch
#  penalty_weight: Penalizing weight for incorrect predictions from this set
#  truth: Boolean whether this set has positive samples or negative samples
#  truncation_strategy = If spectrograms in the set are longer than necessary for training, how are they truncated
#       - random: choose a random portion of the entire spectrogram - useful for long negative samples
#       - truncate_start: remove the start of the spectrogram
#       - truncate_end: remove the end of the spectrogram
#       - split: Split the longer spectrogram into separate spectrograms offset by 100 ms. Only for ambient sets

config["features"] = [
    {
        "features_dir": "generated_augmented_features",
        "sampling_weight": 2.0,
        "penalty_weight": 1.0,
        "truth": True,
        "truncation_strategy": "truncate_start",
        "type": "mmap",
    },
    {
        "features_dir": "negative_datasets/speech",
        "sampling_weight": 10.0,
        "penalty_weight": 1.0,
        "truth": False,
        "truncation_strategy": "random",
        "type": "mmap",
    },
    {
        "features_dir": "negative_datasets/dinner_party",
        "sampling_weight": 10.0,
        "penalty_weight": 1.0,
        "truth": False,
        "truncation_strategy": "random",
        "type": "mmap",
    },
    {
        "features_dir": "negative_datasets/no_speech",
        "sampling_weight": 5.0,
        "penalty_weight": 1.0,
        "truth": False,
        "truncation_strategy": "random",
        "type": "mmap",
    },
    { # Only used for validation and testing
        "features_dir": "negative_datasets/dinner_party_eval",
        "sampling_weight": 0.0,
        "penalty_weight": 1.0,
        "truth": False,
        "truncation_strategy": "split",
        "type": "mmap",
    },
]

# Number of training steps in each iteration - various other settings are configured as lists that corresponds to different steps
config["training_steps"] = [10000]

# Penalizing weight for incorrect class predictions - lists that correspond to training steps
config["positive_class_weight"] = [1]
config["negative_class_weight"] = [20]

config["learning_rates"] = [
    0.001,
]  # Learning rates for Adam optimizer - list that corresponds to training steps
config["batch_size"] = 128

config["time_mask_max_size"] = [
    0
]  # SpecAugment - list that corresponds to training steps
config["time_mask_count"] = [0]  # SpecAugment - list that corresponds to training steps
config["freq_mask_max_size"] = [
    0
]  # SpecAugment - list that corresponds to training steps
config["freq_mask_count"] = [0]  # SpecAugment - list that corresponds to training steps

config["eval_step_interval"] = (
    500  # Test the validation sets after every this many steps
)
config["clip_duration_ms"] = (
    1500  # Maximum length of wake word that the streaming model will accept
)

# The best model weights are chosen first by minimizing the specified minimization metric below the specified target_minimization
# Once the target has been met, it chooses the maximum of the maximization metric. Set 'minimization_metric' to None to only maximize
# Available metrics:
#   - "loss" - cross entropy error on validation set
#   - "accuracy" - accuracy of validation set
#   - "recall" - recall of validation set
#   - "precision" - precision of validation set
#   - "false_positive_rate" - false positive rate of validation set
#   - "false_negative_rate" - false negative rate of validation set
#   - "ambient_false_positives" - count of false positives from the split validation_ambient set
#   - "ambient_false_positives_per_hour" - estimated number of false positives per hour on the split validation_ambient set
config["target_minimization"] = 0.9
config["minimization_metric"] = None  # Set to None to disable

config["maximization_metric"] = "average_viable_recall"

with open(os.path.join("training_parameters.yaml"), "w") as file:
    documents = yaml.dump(config, file)</cell id="cell-9">

# AudioSet Dataset Structure

Based on the webpage content, the AudioSet dataset contains **three main data directories**:

1. **bal_train** - Balanced training data
2. **eval** - Evaluation data
3. **unbal_train** - Unbalanced training data

## File Format

The dataset uses **Parquet format** for all files, as indicated by the recent conversion mentioned in the commit history "Convert to Parquet format (#5)" completed approximately one month ago.

## Dataset Size

The total dataset is **2.44 TB** in size, with a capacity range of "1M - 10M" entries, making it a substantial audio classification resource.

<cell id="cell-0"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type># microWakeWord Training Notebook

Train a custom wake word detection model compatible with ESP32-S3.

## Overview

This notebook trains models compatible with `wakeword_pretrained_test.ino`:
- **Input**: 40-bin log-mel spectrogram features (30ms window, 10ms stride)
- **Architecture**: MixNet-based streaming model
- **Output**: Quantized TFLite model for ESP32

Based on: https://github.com/kahrendt/microWakeWord</cell id="cell-0">

<cell id="cell-8"># Cell 6: Generate full training dataset
import subprocess
import shutil

training_dir = GENERATED_DIR / 'training'

# Clean up existing samples for fresh batch
if training_dir.exists():
    shutil.rmtree(training_dir)
training_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

SAMPLES_PER_VARIATION = 100  # Total: 9 variations * 100 = 900 samples

print(f"Generating {len(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS) * SAMPLES_PER_VARIATION} samples...")

for i, variation in enumerate(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS):
    print(f"  [{i+1}/{len(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS)}] '{variation}'")
    # Generate to temp dir to avoid filename collisions
    temp_dir = GENERATED_DIR / f'temp_{i}'
    temp_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    
    subprocess.run([
        'python3', 'piper-sample-generator/generate_samples.py',
        variation,

        '--batch-size', '10',
        '--output-dir', str(temp_dir),

    ], capture_output=True)
    
    # Move files with unique prefix
    for wav in temp_dir.glob('*.wav'):
        new_name = f"var{i}_{wav.name}"
        shutil.move(str(wav), str(training_dir / new_name))
    temp_dir.rmdir()

sample_count = len(list(training_dir.glob('*.wav')))
print(f"\nGenerated {sample_count} samples")</cell id="cell-8">

<cell id="cell-12"># Cell 9: Download pre-computed negative features from HuggingFace
import zipfile

NEGATIVE_DIR = FEATURES_DIR / 'negatives'
NEGATIVE_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

# These are pre-computed spectrogram feature files (not raw audio)
NEGATIVE_FILES = {
    'speech.zip': 'speech',
    'no_speech.zip': 'no_speech',
    'dinner_party.zip': 'dinner_party',
    'dinner_party_eval.zip': 'dinner_party_eval',
}

BASE_URL = 'https://huggingface.co/datasets/kahrendt/microwakeword/resolve/main'

print("Downloading negative features (this may take several minutes)...")
for zip_name, folder_name in NEGATIVE_FILES.items():
    zip_path = NEGATIVE_DIR / zip_name
    extract_dir = NEGATIVE_DIR / folder_name
    
    if not extract_dir.exists():
        print(f"  Downloading {zip_name}...")
        !wget -q --show-progress -O {zip_path} '{BASE_URL}/{zip_name}'
        
        if zip_path.exists() and zip_path.stat().st_size > 1000:
            print(f"  Extracting {zip_name}...")
            with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path, 'r') as z:
                z.extractall(NEGATIVE_DIR)
            zip_path.unlink()  # Remove zip to save space
        else:
            print(f"  WARNING: {zip_name} download failed")
    else:
        print(f"  {folder_name} already exists")

print("Done!")</cell id="cell-12">

augmentation = Augmentation(

)

<cell id="cell-15"># Cell 11: Generate spectrogram features
from microwakeword.feature_generation import Clips, SpectrogramGeneration
from mmap_ninja import RaggedMmap

POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR = FEATURES_DIR / 'positive'
POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

clips = Clips(str(training_dir))
print(f"Loaded {len(clips)} audio clips")

spec_gen = SpectrogramGeneration()

print("Generating training features...")
train_features_dir = POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR / 'train'
RaggedMmap.from_generator(
    out_dir=str(train_features_dir),
    sample_generator=spec_gen.generate_features(
        clips=clips,
        augmentation=augmentation,
        slide_frames=10,
    ),
    batch_size=1000,
    verbose=True
)

print("\nGenerating validation features...")
val_features_dir = POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR / 'val'
RaggedMmap.from_generator(
    out_dir=str(val_features_dir),
    sample_generator=spec_gen.generate_features(
        clips=clips,
        augmentation=None,
        slide_frames=1,
    ),
    batch_size=1000,
    verbose=True
)
print("\nDone!")</cell id="cell-15">

import yaml

training_config = {
    'model_name': WAKE_WORD_ID,
    'window_step_ms': 10,
    'batch_size': 128,
    'training_steps': 10000,
    'learning_rate': 0.001,
    'positive_class_weight': 1,
    'negative_class_weight': 20,
    'datasets': {
        'positive_train': {'path': str(train_features_dir), 'sampling_weight': 2.0, 'penalty_weight': 1.0},
        'positive_val': {'path': str(val_features_dir), 'sampling_weight': 0.0, 'penalty_weight': 1.0},
        'speech_negatives': {'path': str(NEGATIVE_DIR / 'speech'), 'sampling_weight': 10.0, 'penalty_weight': 1.0},
        'dinner_party_train': {'path': str(NEGATIVE_DIR / 'dinner_party'), 'sampling_weight': 10.0, 'penalty_weight': 1.0},
        'nonspeech': {'path': str(NEGATIVE_DIR / 'no_speech'), 'sampling_weight': 5.0, 'penalty_weight': 1.0},
    },
    'eval_every_n_steps': 500,
    'selection_metric': 'average_viable_recall',
    'selection_maximize': True,
    'viable_loss_target': 0.9,
}

config_path = WORK_DIR / 'training_config.yaml'
with open(config_path, 'w') as f:

<cell id="cell-0"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type># microWakeWord Training Notebook

Train a custom wake word detection model compatible with ESP32-S3.

## Overview

This notebook trains models compatible with `wakeword_pretrained_test.ino`:
- **Input**: 40-bin log-mel spectrogram features (30ms window, 10ms stride)
- **Architecture**: MixNet-based streaming model
- **Output**: Quantized TFLite model for ESP32

Based on: https://github.com/kahrendt/microWakeWord</cell id="cell-0">

<cell id="cell-8"># Cell 6: Generate full training dataset
import subprocess
import shutil

training_dir = GENERATED_DIR / 'training'

# Clean up existing samples for fresh batch
if training_dir.exists():
    shutil.rmtree(training_dir)
training_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

SAMPLES_PER_VARIATION = 100  # Total: 9 variations * 100 = 900 samples

print(f"Generating {len(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS) * SAMPLES_PER_VARIATION} samples...")

for i, variation in enumerate(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS):
    print(f"  [{i+1}/{len(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS)}] '{variation}'")
    # Generate to temp dir to avoid filename collisions
    temp_dir = GENERATED_DIR / f'temp_{i}'
    temp_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    
    subprocess.run([
        'python3', 'piper-sample-generator/generate_samples.py',
        variation,
        '--max-samples', str(SAMPLES_PER_VARIATION),
        '--batch-size', '10',
        '--output-dir', str(temp_dir),
        '--model', 'piper-sample-generator/models/en_US-libritts_r-medium.pt'
    ], capture_output=True)
    
    # Move files with unique prefix
    for wav in temp_dir.glob('*.wav'):
        new_name = f"var{i}_{wav.name}"
        shutil.move(str(wav), str(training_dir / new_name))
    temp_dir.rmdir()

sample_count = len(list(training_dir.glob('*.wav')))
print(f"\nGenerated {sample_count} samples")</cell id="cell-8">

# Spectrogram Feature Generation in the microWakeWord Notebook

## Imports and Classes

The notebook uses three primary classes from the `microwakeword` library for feature generation:

1. **Clips** - Loads and manages audio clip data
2. **Augmentation** - Applies audio transformations
3. **SpectrogramGeneration** - Converts augmented audio to spectrogram features

```python
from microwakeword.audio.augmentation import Augmentation
from microwakeword.audio.clips import Clips
from microwakeword.audio.spectrograms import SpectrogramGeneration
```

## Setup Code

The augmentation and feature generation workflow is configured as follows:

```python
clips = Clips(input_directory='generated_samples',
              file_pattern='*.wav',
              max_clip_duration_s=None,
              remove_silence=False,
              random_split_seed=10,
              split_count=0.1)

augmenter = Augmentation(augmentation_duration_s=3.2,
                         augmentation_probabilities = {
                            "SevenBandParametricEQ": 0.1,
                            "TanhDistortion": 0.1,
                            "PitchShift": 0.1,
                            "BandStopFilter": 0.1,
                            "AddColorNoise": 0.1,
                            "AddBackgroundNoise": 0.75,
                            "Gain": 1.0,
                            "RIR": 0.5},
                         impulse_paths = ['mit_rirs'],
                         background_paths = ['fma_16k', 'audioset_16k'])
```

## Spectrogram Generation

The spectrograms are created using:

```python
spectrograms = SpectrogramGeneration(clips=clips,
                                     augmenter=augmenter,
                                     slide_frames=10,
                                     step_ms=10)
```

The `spectrogram_generator()` method then feeds data into `RaggedMmap` for storage and batch processing during training.

<cell id="cell-0"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type># microWakeWord Training Notebook

Train a custom wake word detection model compatible with ESP32-S3.

## Overview

This notebook trains models compatible with `wakeword_pretrained_test.ino`:
- **Input**: 40-bin log-mel spectrogram features (30ms window, 10ms stride)
- **Architecture**: MixNet-based streaming model
- **Output**: Quantized TFLite model for ESP32

Based on: https://github.com/kahrendt/microWakeWord</cell id="cell-0">

<cell id="cell-3"># Cell 3: Setup directories
import os
import json
from pathlib import Path

WORK_DIR = Path('/content/wakeword_training')
WORK_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

GENERATED_DIR = WORK_DIR / 'generated_samples'
FEATURES_DIR = WORK_DIR / 'features'
AUGMENTATION_DIR = WORK_DIR / 'augmentation'
MODEL_DIR = WORK_DIR / 'trained_models'

from microwakeword.audio.clips import Clips

# Load audio clips
clips = Clips(
    input_directory=str(training_dir),
    file_pattern='*.wav',
    max_clip_duration_s=None,
    remove_silence=False,
    random_split_seed=10,
    split_count=0.1  # 10% for validation
)
print(f"Loaded {len(clips)} audio clips")

# Generate training features (with augmentation)

    clips=clips,

    slide_frames=10,
    step_ms=10
)

train_features_dir = POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR / 'train'
RaggedMmap.from_generator(

    batch_size=1000,

)

)

)
print("\nDone!")</cell id="cell-15">

# Clips Class API

## Constructor Parameters

The `Clips` class initializer accepts the following arguments:

- `input_directory` (str): Path to audio clip files
- `file_pattern` (str): File glob pattern for selecting audio clips
- `min_clip_duration_s` (float | None): Minimum clip duration in seconds
- `max_clip_duration_s` (float | None): Maximum clip duration in seconds
- `repeat_clip_min_duration_s` (float | None): Minimum duration before repeating clips
- `remove_silence` (bool): Enable webrtcvad to trim non-voice activity
- `random_split_seed` (int | None): Seed for splitting clips into sets
- `split_count` (int | float): Percentage/count for test and validation sets
- `trimmed_clip_duration_s` (float | None): Duration to trim long clips
- `trim_zeros` (bool): Remove leading and trailing zeros

## Public Methods

- `audio_generator(split, repeat)` – Generator yielding all loaded clips
- `get_random_clip()` – Returns a single random audio clip
- `random_audio_generator(max_clips)` – Generator yielding random clips indefinitely
- `repeat_clip(audio_samples)` – Repeats audio until exceeding minimum duration

## Key Properties

- `clips` – Dataset containing loaded audio clips
- `split_clips` – DatasetDict with train/test/validation splits (if seed provided)
```

# SpectrogramGeneration Class API

## Constructor Parameters

The `__init__` method accepts:

- **clips** (Clips): Object that retrieves audio clips
- **augmenter** (Augmentation | None, optional): Audio augmentation object; defaults to None
- **step_ms** (int, optional): Window step size in milliseconds for spectrogram features; defaults to 20
- **split_spectrogram_duration_s** (float | None, optional): Duration for splitting spectrograms into non-overlapping segments; defaults to None
- **slide_frames** (int | None, optional): Number of overlapping spectrograms via frame striding; defaults to None

## Class Definition

```python
class SpectrogramGeneration:
    def __init__(
        self,
        clips: Clips,
        augmenter: Augmentation | None = None,
        step_ms: int = 20,
        split_spectrogram_duration_s: float | None = None,
        slide_frames: int | None = None,
    ):
```

1. **get_random_spectrogram()** - Returns a 2D spectrogram array for a random (optionally augmented) audio clip

2. **spectrogram_generator()** - Generator method with signature:
```python
def spectrogram_generator(self, random=False, max_clips=None, **kwargs):

# SpectrogramGeneration Usage

Based on the notebook, `SpectrogramGeneration` is instantiated differently for each dataset split:

## Training Set
```python
spectrograms = SpectrogramGeneration(clips=clips,
                                     augmenter=augmenter,
                                     slide_frames=10,
                                     step_ms=10)
```

## Validation Set
```python
spectrograms = SpectrogramGeneration(clips=clips,
                                     augmenter=augmenter,
                                     slide_frames=10,
                                     step_ms=10)
```

## Testing Set
```python
spectrograms = SpectrogramGeneration(clips=clips,
                                     augmenter=augmenter,
                                     slide_frames=1,
                                     step_ms=10)
```

## Generator Parameters

The `spectrogram_generator()` method receives:
- **`split`**: Either `"train"`, `"validation"`, or `"test"`
- **`repeat`**: Integer controlling repetition counts (2 for training, 1 for validation/testing)

## Key Difference

The primary distinction involves `slide_frames`: training and validation use `10` (simulating streaming by repeating spectrograms shifted by one frame), while testing uses `1` since "the testing set uses the streaming version of the model, so no artificial repetition is necessary."

<cell id="cell-0"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type># microWakeWord Training Notebook

Train a custom wake word detection model compatible with ESP32-S3.

## Overview

This notebook trains models compatible with `wakeword_pretrained_test.ino`:
- **Input**: 40-bin log-mel spectrogram features (30ms window, 10ms stride)
- **Architecture**: MixNet-based streaming model
- **Output**: Quantized TFLite model for ESP32

Based on: https://github.com/kahrendt/microWakeWord</cell id="cell-0">

<cell id="cell-8"># Cell 6: Generate full training dataset
import subprocess
import shutil

training_dir = GENERATED_DIR / 'training'

# Clean up existing samples for fresh batch
if training_dir.exists():
    shutil.rmtree(training_dir)
training_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

SAMPLES_PER_VARIATION = 100  # Total: 9 variations * 100 = 900 samples

print(f"Generating {len(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS) * SAMPLES_PER_VARIATION} samples...")

for i, variation in enumerate(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS):
    print(f"  [{i+1}/{len(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS)}] '{variation}'")
    # Generate to temp dir to avoid filename collisions
    temp_dir = GENERATED_DIR / f'temp_{i}'
    temp_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    
    subprocess.run([
        'python3', 'piper-sample-generator/generate_samples.py',
        variation,
        '--max-samples', str(SAMPLES_PER_VARIATION),
        '--batch-size', '10',
        '--output-dir', str(temp_dir),
        '--model', 'piper-sample-generator/models/en_US-libritts_r-medium.pt'
    ], capture_output=True)
    
    # Move files with unique prefix
    for wav in temp_dir.glob('*.wav'):
        new_name = f"var{i}_{wav.name}"
        shutil.move(str(wav), str(training_dir / new_name))
    temp_dir.rmdir()

sample_count = len(list(training_dir.glob('*.wav')))
print(f"\nGenerated {sample_count} samples")</cell id="cell-8">

import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

AUDIOSET_DIR = AUGMENTATION_DIR / 'audioset'
AUDIOSET_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

# Check if we already have audio files
existing = list(AUDIOSET_DIR.glob('*.wav'))
if len(existing) >= 100:
    print(f"AudioSet already has {len(existing)} samples, skipping download")
else:
    try:
        from datasets import load_dataset
        import soundfile as sf
        print("Loading AudioSet subset via datasets library...")
        
        # Load balanced subset with streaming
        ds = load_dataset(
            "agkphysics/AudioSet", 
            split="train",
            streaming=True,
            trust_remote_code=True
        )
        
        # Save first 500 audio samples as wav files
        count = 0
        max_samples = 500
        
        for sample in ds:
            if count >= max_samples:
                break
            try:
                audio = sample['audio']
                wav_path = AUDIOSET_DIR / f"audioset_{count:04d}.wav"
                sf.write(str(wav_path), audio['array'], audio['sampling_rate'])
                count += 1
                if count % 100 == 0:
                    print(f"  Saved {count}/{max_samples} samples")
            except Exception:
                continue  # Skip problematic samples
        
        print(f"Done! Saved {count} background audio samples")

    except Exception as e:
        print(f"AudioSet loading failed: {e}")
        print("Background augmentation will use MIT impulse responses only.")</cell id="cell-11">

import zipfile

NEGATIVE_DIR = FEATURES_DIR / 'negatives'
NEGATIVE_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

# These are pre-computed spectrogram feature files (not raw audio)
NEGATIVE_FILES = {
    'speech.zip': 'speech',
    'no_speech.zip': 'no_speech',
    'dinner_party.zip': 'dinner_party',
    'dinner_party_eval.zip': 'dinner_party_eval',
}

BASE_URL = 'https://huggingface.co/datasets/kahrendt/microwakeword/resolve/main'

print("Downloading negative features (this may take several minutes)...")
for zip_name, folder_name in NEGATIVE_FILES.items():
    zip_path = NEGATIVE_DIR / zip_name
    extract_dir = NEGATIVE_DIR / folder_name
    
    if not extract_dir.exists():
        print(f"  Downloading {zip_name}...")
        !wget -q --show-progress -O {zip_path} '{BASE_URL}/{zip_name}'
        
        if zip_path.exists() and zip_path.stat().st_size > 1000:
            print(f"  Extracting {zip_name}...")
            with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path, 'r') as z:
                z.extractall(NEGATIVE_DIR)
            zip_path.unlink()  # Remove zip to save space
        else:
            print(f"  WARNING: {zip_name} download failed")
    else:
        print(f"  {folder_name} already exists")

print("Done!")</cell id="cell-12">

<cell id="cell-14"># Cell 10: Configure augmentation
from microwakeword.audio.augmentation import Augmentation

augmentation = Augmentation(
    augmentation_duration_s=3.2,
    augmentation_probabilities={
        "SevenBandParametricEQ": 0.1,
        "TanhDistortion": 0.1,
        "PitchShift": 0.1,
        "BandStopFilter": 0.1,
        "AddColorNoise": 0.1,
        "AddBackgroundNoise": 0.75,
        "Gain": 1.0,
        "RIR": 0.5,
    },
    impulse_paths=[str(MIT_IR_DIR / 'Audio')],
    background_paths=[str(AUDIOSET_DIR)],
)

from microwakeword.audio.clips import Clips
from microwakeword.audio.spectrograms import SpectrogramGeneration
from mmap_ninja import RaggedMmap

POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR = FEATURES_DIR / 'positive'
POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

# Load audio clips
clips = Clips(
    input_directory=str(training_dir),
    file_pattern='*.wav',
    max_clip_duration_s=None,
    remove_silence=False,
    random_split_seed=10,
    split_count=0.1  # 10% for validation
)
print(f"Clips loaded from {training_dir}")

# Generate training features (with augmentation)
print("Generating training features...")
train_spec_gen = SpectrogramGeneration(
    clips=clips,
    augmenter=augmentation,
    slide_frames=10,
    step_ms=10
)

if train_features_dir.exists():

    shutil.rmtree(train_features_dir)

RaggedMmap.from_generator(
    out_dir=str(train_features_dir),

)

# Generate validation features (no augmentation)

    augmenter=None,
    slide_frames=1,

)

    shutil.rmtree(val_features_dir)

RaggedMmap.from_generator(
    out_dir=str(val_features_dir),

)

<cell id="cell-16"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## Step 5: Configure Training</cell id="cell-16">
<cell id="cell-17"># Cell 12: Create training config
import yaml

training_config = {
    'model_name': WAKE_WORD_ID,
    'window_step_ms': 10,
    'batch_size': 128,
    'training_steps': 10000,
    'learning_rate': 0.001,
    'positive_class_weight': 1,
    'negative_class_weight': 20,
    'datasets': {
        'positive_train': {'path': str(train_features_dir), 'sampling_weight': 2.0, 'penalty_weight': 1.0},
        'positive_val': {'path': str(val_features_dir), 'sampling_weight': 0.0, 'penalty_weight': 1.0},
        'speech_negatives': {'path': str(NEGATIVE_DIR / 'speech'), 'sampling_weight': 10.0, 'penalty_weight': 1.0},
        'dinner_party_train': {'path': str(NEGATIVE_DIR / 'dinner_party'), 'sampling_weight': 10.0, 'penalty_weight': 1.0},
        'nonspeech': {'path': str(NEGATIVE_DIR / 'no_speech'), 'sampling_weight': 5.0, 'penalty_weight': 1.0},
    },
    'eval_every_n_steps': 500,
    'selection_metric': 'average_viable_recall',
    'selection_maximize': True,
    'viable_loss_target': 0.9,
}

config_path = WORK_DIR / 'training_config.yaml'
with open(config_path, 'w') as f:
    yaml.dump(training_config, f, default_flow_style=False)

print(f"Config saved: {config_path}")</cell id="cell-17">
<cell id="cell-18"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## Step 6: Train the Model</cell id="cell-18">
<cell id="cell-19"># Cell 13: Train (~30-60 minutes)
print("Starting training...\n")

!python -m microwakeword.model_train_eval \
    --training_config='{config_path}' \
    --train 1 \
    --test_tflite_streaming_quantized 1 \
    --use_weights 'best_weights' \
    mixednet \
    --pointwise_filters_per_block '64,64,64,64' \
    --repeat_count_per_block '1,1,1,1' \
    --mixconv_kernel_sizes '[5], [7,11], [9,15], [23]' \
    --residual_connections '0,0,0,0' \
    --initial_filters 32 \
    --initial_kernel 5 \
    --stride 3 \
    --clip_duration_ms 1500</cell id="cell-19">
<cell id="cell-20"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## Step 7: Export Model</cell id="cell-20">
<cell id="cell-21"># Cell 14: Package trained model
import shutil

model_paths = list(Path('trained_models').rglob('stream_state_internal_quant.tflite'))

if not model_paths:
    print("ERROR: No trained model found!")
else:
    model_path = model_paths[0]
    output_model = MODEL_DIR / f'{WAKE_WORD_ID}.tflite'
    shutil.copy(model_path, output_model)
    print(f"Model: {output_model}")
    print(f"Size: {output_model.stat().st_size:,} bytes")</cell id="cell-21">
<cell id="cell-22"># Cell 15: Create manifest
manifest = {
    'type': 'micro',
    'wake_word': WAKE_WORD,
    'model': f'{WAKE_WORD_ID}.tflite',
    'version': 1,
    'micro': {'probability_cutoff': 0.5, 'sliding_window_average_size': 10}
}

manifest_path = MODEL_DIR / f'{WAKE_WORD_ID}.json'
with open(manifest_path, 'w') as f:
    json.dump(manifest, f, indent=2)

print(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2))</cell id="cell-22">
<cell id="cell-23"># Cell 16: Verify model
import tensorflow as tf

interpreter = tf.lite.Interpreter(model_path=str(output_model))
interpreter.allocate_tensors()

inp = interpreter.get_input_details()[0]
out = interpreter.get_output_details()[0]

print(f"Input: {inp['shape']}, type={inp['dtype']}")
print(f"Output: {out['shape']}, type={out['dtype']}")

if inp['shape'][-1] == 40:
    print("\n✓ Compatible with ESP32 inference code")</cell id="cell-23">
<cell id="cell-24"># Cell 17: Download model
from google.colab import files

print(f"Download {WAKE_WORD_ID}.tflite -> copy to SD:/models/\n")
files.download(str(output_model))
files.download(str(manifest_path))</cell id="cell-24">

<cell id="cell-0"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type># microWakeWord Training Notebook

Train a custom wake word detection model compatible with ESP32-S3.

## Overview

This notebook trains models compatible with `wakeword_pretrained_test.ino`:
- **Input**: 40-bin log-mel spectrogram features (30ms window, 10ms stride)
- **Architecture**: MixNet-based streaming model
- **Output**: Quantized TFLite model for ESP32

Based on: https://github.com/kahrendt/microWakeWord</cell id="cell-0">

<cell id="cell-8"># Cell 6: Generate full training dataset
import subprocess
import shutil

training_dir = GENERATED_DIR / 'training'

# Clean up existing samples for fresh batch
if training_dir.exists():
    shutil.rmtree(training_dir)
training_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

SAMPLES_PER_VARIATION = 100  # Total: 9 variations * 100 = 900 samples

print(f"Generating {len(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS) * SAMPLES_PER_VARIATION} samples...")

for i, variation in enumerate(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS):
    print(f"  [{i+1}/{len(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS)}] '{variation}'")
    # Generate to temp dir to avoid filename collisions
    temp_dir = GENERATED_DIR / f'temp_{i}'
    temp_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    
    subprocess.run([
        'python3', 'piper-sample-generator/generate_samples.py',
        variation,
        '--max-samples', str(SAMPLES_PER_VARIATION),
        '--batch-size', '10',
        '--output-dir', str(temp_dir),
        '--model', 'piper-sample-generator/models/en_US-libritts_r-medium.pt'
    ], capture_output=True)
    
    # Move files with unique prefix
    for wav in temp_dir.glob('*.wav'):
        new_name = f"var{i}_{wav.name}"
        shutil.move(str(wav), str(training_dir / new_name))
    temp_dir.rmdir()

sample_count = len(list(training_dir.glob('*.wav')))
print(f"\nGenerated {sample_count} samples")</cell id="cell-8">

import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

AUDIOSET_DIR = AUGMENTATION_DIR / 'audioset'
AUDIOSET_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

# Check if we already have audio files
existing = list(AUDIOSET_DIR.glob('*.wav'))
if len(existing) >= 100:
    print(f"AudioSet already has {len(existing)} samples, skipping download")
else:
    try:
        from datasets import load_dataset
        import soundfile as sf
        print("Loading AudioSet subset via datasets library...")
        
        # Load balanced subset with streaming
        ds = load_dataset(
            "agkphysics/AudioSet", 
            split="train",
            streaming=True,
            trust_remote_code=True
        )
        
        # Save first 500 audio samples as wav files
        count = 0
        max_samples = 500
        
        for sample in ds:
            if count >= max_samples:
                break
            try:
                audio = sample['audio']
                wav_path = AUDIOSET_DIR / f"audioset_{count:04d}.wav"
                sf.write(str(wav_path), audio['array'], audio['sampling_rate'])
                count += 1
                if count % 100 == 0:
                    print(f"  Saved {count}/{max_samples} samples")
            except Exception:
                continue  # Skip problematic samples
        
        print(f"Done! Saved {count} background audio samples")

    except Exception as e:
        print(f"AudioSet loading failed: {e}")
        print("Background augmentation will use MIT impulse responses only.")</cell id="cell-11">

import zipfile

NEGATIVE_DIR = FEATURES_DIR / 'negatives'
NEGATIVE_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

# These are pre-computed spectrogram feature files (not raw audio)
NEGATIVE_FILES = {
    'speech.zip': 'speech',
    'no_speech.zip': 'no_speech',
    'dinner_party.zip': 'dinner_party',
    'dinner_party_eval.zip': 'dinner_party_eval',
}

BASE_URL = 'https://huggingface.co/datasets/kahrendt/microwakeword/resolve/main'

print("Downloading negative features (this may take several minutes)...")
for zip_name, folder_name in NEGATIVE_FILES.items():
    zip_path = NEGATIVE_DIR / zip_name
    extract_dir = NEGATIVE_DIR / folder_name
    
    if not extract_dir.exists():
        print(f"  Downloading {zip_name}...")
        !wget -q --show-progress -O {zip_path} '{BASE_URL}/{zip_name}'
        
        if zip_path.exists() and zip_path.stat().st_size > 1000:
            print(f"  Extracting {zip_name}...")
            with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path, 'r') as z:
                z.extractall(NEGATIVE_DIR)
            zip_path.unlink()  # Remove zip to save space
        else:
            print(f"  WARNING: {zip_name} download failed")
    else:
        print(f"  {folder_name} already exists")

print("Done!")</cell id="cell-12">

<cell id="cell-14"># Cell 10: Configure augmentation
from microwakeword.audio.augmentation import Augmentation

augmentation = Augmentation(
    augmentation_duration_s=3.2,
    augmentation_probabilities={
        "SevenBandParametricEQ": 0.1,
        "TanhDistortion": 0.1,
        "PitchShift": 0.1,
        "BandStopFilter": 0.1,
        "AddColorNoise": 0.1,
        "AddBackgroundNoise": 0.75,
        "Gain": 1.0,
        "RIR": 0.5,
    },
    impulse_paths=[str(MIT_IR_DIR / 'Audio')],
    background_paths=[str(AUDIOSET_DIR)],
)
print("Augmentation configured")</cell id="cell-14">

Augmentation configured

<cell id="cell-15"># Cell 11: Generate spectrogram features
from microwakeword.audio.clips import Clips
from microwakeword.audio.spectrograms import SpectrogramGeneration
from mmap_ninja import RaggedMmap

POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR = FEATURES_DIR / 'positive'
POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

# Load audio clips
clips = Clips(
    input_directory=str(training_dir),
    file_pattern='*.wav',
    max_clip_duration_s=None,
    remove_silence=False,
    random_split_seed=10,
    split_count=0.1  # 10% for validation
)
print(f"Clips loaded from {training_dir}")

# Generate training features (with augmentation)
print("Generating training features...")
train_spec_gen = SpectrogramGeneration(
    clips=clips,
    augmenter=augmentation,
    slide_frames=10,
    step_ms=10
)

train_features_dir = POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR / 'train'
if train_features_dir.exists():
    import shutil
    shutil.rmtree(train_features_dir)

RaggedMmap.from_generator(
    out_dir=str(train_features_dir),
    sample_generator=train_spec_gen.spectrogram_generator(split='train', repeat=2),
    batch_size=1000,
    verbose=True
)

# Generate validation features (no augmentation)
print("\nGenerating validation features...")
val_spec_gen = SpectrogramGeneration(
    clips=clips,
    augmenter=None,
    slide_frames=1,
    step_ms=10
)

val_features_dir = POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR / 'val'
if val_features_dir.exists():
    import shutil
    shutil.rmtree(val_features_dir)

RaggedMmap.from_generator(
    out_dir=str(val_features_dir),
    sample_generator=val_spec_gen.spectrogram_generator(split='validation', repeat=1),
    batch_size=1000,
    verbose=True
)
print("\nDone!")</cell id="cell-15">

<cell id="cell-17"># Cell 12: Create training config
import yaml

training_config = {
    'model_name': WAKE_WORD_ID,
    'window_step_ms': 10,
    'batch_size': 128,
    'training_steps': 10000,
    'learning_rate': 0.001,
    'positive_class_weight': 1,
    'negative_class_weight': 20,
    'datasets': {
        'positive_train': {'path': str(train_features_dir), 'sampling_weight': 2.0, 'penalty_weight': 1.0},
        'positive_val': {'path': str(val_features_dir), 'sampling_weight': 0.0, 'penalty_weight': 1.0},
        'speech_negatives': {'path': str(NEGATIVE_DIR / 'speech'), 'sampling_weight': 10.0, 'penalty_weight': 1.0},
        'dinner_party_train': {'path': str(NEGATIVE_DIR / 'dinner_party'), 'sampling_weight': 10.0, 'penalty_weight': 1.0},
        'nonspeech': {'path': str(NEGATIVE_DIR / 'no_speech'), 'sampling_weight': 5.0, 'penalty_weight': 1.0},
    },
    'eval_every_n_steps': 500,
    'selection_metric': 'average_viable_recall',
    'selection_maximize': True,
    'viable_loss_target': 0.9,
}

config_path = WORK_DIR / 'training_config.yaml'
with open(config_path, 'w') as f:
    yaml.dump(training_config, f, default_flow_style=False)

print(f"Config saved: {config_path}")</cell id="cell-17">

model_paths = list(Path('trained_models').rglob('stream_state_internal_quant.tflite'))

    model_path = model_paths[0]

<cell id="cell-22"># Cell 15: Create manifest
manifest = {
    'type': 'micro',
    'wake_word': WAKE_WORD,
    'model': f'{WAKE_WORD_ID}.tflite',
    'version': 1,

# Command Line Arguments

## Main Arguments

The script accepts these primary command-line arguments:

- `--training_config`: Path to training parameters YAML file (default: `trained_models/model/training_parameters.yaml`)
- `--train`: Integer flag; 1 runs training and testing, 0 runs only testing (default: 1)
- `--test_tf_nonstreaming`: Integer flag to evaluate nonstreaming SavedModel (default: 0)
- `--test_tflite_nonstreaming`: Integer flag to convert and evaluate nonstreaming TFLite model (default: 0)
- `--test_tflite_nonstreaming_quantized`: Integer flag for quantized nonstreaming TFLite (default: 0)
- `--test_tflite_streaming`: Integer flag for streaming TFLite model (default: 0)
- `--test_tflite_streaming_quantized`: Integer flag for quantized streaming TFLite (default: 1)
- `--restore_checkpoint`: Integer flag to resume interrupted training (default: 0)
- `--use_weights`: Specifies weight set: `best_weights` or `last_weights` (default: `best_weights`)
- `--verbosity`: Log level selection: `INFO`, `DEBUG`, `ERROR`, `FATAL`, or `WARN` (default: `INFO`)

## Model Selection

A required subcommand selects the model architecture:
- `inception`: Inception model
- `mixednet`: MixedNet model

## MixedNet Model Arguments

The code indicates MixedNet accepts model-specific parameters via `mixednet.model_parameters(parser_mixednet)`, but the actual parameter definitions are in the external `mixednet` module and are not shown in this script excerpt.

# Config Parsing and Structure

This file doesn't directly parse YAML; instead, the `FeatureHandler` class accepts a **pre-parsed dictionary** via its `__init__` method: `config: dict`.

## Expected Top-Level Keys

The config dictionary requires:
- `"features"` - an array of feature set configurations
- `"stride"` - stride value for the model's first layer
- `"window_step_ms"` - window step duration in milliseconds

## Features Array Structure

Each entry in the `"features"` array must include:

**Common fields for all types:**
- `"type"` - either `"mmap"` or `"clips"`
- `"truth"` - boolean label (wakeword or not)
- `"sampling_weight"` - float controlling selection frequency
- `"penalty_weight"` - float for penalizing incorrect predictions
- `"truncation_strategy"` - truncation method

**For `type: "mmap"`:**
- `"features_dir"` - directory path to Ragged MMaps
- `"fixed_right_cutoffs"` - optional list of integers (defaults to `[0]`)

**For `type: "clips"`:**
- `"clips_settings"` - dictionary passed to the `Clips` class
- `"augmentation_settings"` - dictionary for augmentation configuration
- `"spectrogram_generation_settings"` - dictionary for spectrogram generation

# Split Names and split_count Mechanism

The split names used are **'train'**, 'test', and 'validation'**.

## How split_count Works

When `random_split_seed` is provided, the code performs a two-stage split:

1. **First split**: The dataset is divided using `test_size=2 * split_count`. This means the training set receives `(1 - 2*split_count)` of the data, while the remainder is allocated for testing and validation.

2. **Second split**: The test portion is then split evenly in half, creating equal-sized test and validation sets.

For example, with the default `split_count=0.1`:
- Training: 80% of clips
- Testing: 10% of clips  
- Validation: 10% of clips

The resulting structure is stored in `self.split_clips` as a `DatasetDict` with keys for each of the three splits, allowing access via methods like `audio_generator(split='train')`.
```

# Load audio clips
clips = Clips(

    file_pattern='*.wav',
    max_clip_duration_s=None,
    remove_silence=False,
    random_split_seed=10,
    split_count=0.1
)

# Debug: Check if clips loaded

elif hasattr(clips, 'clips') and clips.clips is not None:
    print(f"  Total clips: {len(clips.clips)}")

# Generate training features (with augmentation)

    clips=clips,

    slide_frames=10,
    step_ms=10
)

train_features_dir = POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR / 'train'
if train_features_dir.exists():
    shutil.rmtree(train_features_dir)

RaggedMmap.from_generator(
    out_dir=str(train_features_dir),
    sample_generator=train_spec_gen.spectrogram_generator(split='train', repeat=2),
    batch_size=1000,
    verbose=True
)

# Generate validation features (no augmentation)

<cell id="cell-0"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type># microWakeWord Training Notebook

Train a custom wake word detection model compatible with ESP32-S3.

## Overview

This notebook trains models compatible with `wakeword_pretrained_test.ino`:
- **Input**: 40-bin log-mel spectrogram features (30ms window, 10ms stride)
- **Architecture**: MixNet-based streaming model
- **Output**: Quantized TFLite model for ESP32

Based on: https://github.com/kahrendt/microWakeWord</cell id="cell-0">

<cell id="cell-8"># Cell 6: Generate full training dataset
import subprocess
import shutil

training_dir = GENERATED_DIR / 'training'

# Clean up existing samples for fresh batch
if training_dir.exists():
    shutil.rmtree(training_dir)
training_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

SAMPLES_PER_VARIATION = 100  # Total: 9 variations * 100 = 900 samples

print(f"Generating {len(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS) * SAMPLES_PER_VARIATION} samples...")

for i, variation in enumerate(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS):
    print(f"  [{i+1}/{len(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS)}] '{variation}'")
    # Generate to temp dir to avoid filename collisions
    temp_dir = GENERATED_DIR / f'temp_{i}'
    temp_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    
    subprocess.run([
        'python3', 'piper-sample-generator/generate_samples.py',
        variation,
        '--max-samples', str(SAMPLES_PER_VARIATION),
        '--batch-size', '10',
        '--output-dir', str(temp_dir),
        '--model', 'piper-sample-generator/models/en_US-libritts_r-medium.pt'
    ], capture_output=True)
    
    # Move files with unique prefix
    for wav in temp_dir.glob('*.wav'):
        new_name = f"var{i}_{wav.name}"
        shutil.move(str(wav), str(training_dir / new_name))
    temp_dir.rmdir()

sample_count = len(list(training_dir.glob('*.wav')))
print(f"\nGenerated {sample_count} samples")</cell id="cell-8">

else:

        from datasets import load_dataset
        import soundfile as sf
        print("Loading AudioSet subset via datasets library...")
        
        # Load balanced subset with streaming
        ds = load_dataset(
            "agkphysics/AudioSet", 
            split="train",
            streaming=True,
            trust_remote_code=True
        )
        
        # Save first 500 audio samples as wav files
        count = 0
        max_samples = 500
        
        for sample in ds:
            if count >= max_samples:
                break
            try:
                audio = sample['audio']
                wav_path = AUDIOSET_DIR / f"audioset_{count:04d}.wav"
                sf.write(str(wav_path), audio['array'], audio['sampling_rate'])
                count += 1
                if count % 100 == 0:
                    print(f"  Saved {count}/{max_samples} samples")
            except Exception:
                continue  # Skip problematic samples
        
        print(f"Done! Saved {count} background audio samples")

    except Exception as e:
        print(f"AudioSet loading failed: {e}")
        print("Background augmentation will use MIT impulse responses only.")</cell id="cell-11">

NEGATIVE_FILES = {
    'speech.zip': 'speech',

    'dinner_party_eval.zip': 'dinner_party_eval',
}

BASE_URL = 'https://huggingface.co/datasets/kahrendt/microwakeword/resolve/main'

print("Downloading negative features (this may take several minutes)...")
for zip_name, folder_name in NEGATIVE_FILES.items():
    zip_path = NEGATIVE_DIR / zip_name
    extract_dir = NEGATIVE_DIR / folder_name
    
    if not extract_dir.exists():
        print(f"  Downloading {zip_name}...")
        !wget -q --show-progress -O {zip_path} '{BASE_URL}/{zip_name}'
        
        if zip_path.exists() and zip_path.stat().st_size > 1000:
            print(f"  Extracting {zip_name}...")
            with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path, 'r') as z:
                z.extractall(NEGATIVE_DIR)
            zip_path.unlink()  # Remove zip to save space
        else:
            print(f"  WARNING: {zip_name} download failed")
    else:
        print(f"  {folder_name} already exists")

print("Done!")</cell id="cell-12">

from microwakeword.audio.augmentation import Augmentation

augmentation = Augmentation(
    augmentation_duration_s=3.2,
    augmentation_probabilities={
        "SevenBandParametricEQ": 0.1,
        "TanhDistortion": 0.1,
        "PitchShift": 0.1,
        "BandStopFilter": 0.1,
        "AddColorNoise": 0.1,
        "AddBackgroundNoise": 0.75,
        "Gain": 1.0,
        "RIR": 0.5,
    },
    impulse_paths=[str(MIT_IR_DIR / 'Audio')],
    background_paths=[str(AUDIOSET_DIR)],
)

<cell id="cell-15"># Cell 11: Generate spectrogram features
from microwakeword.audio.clips import Clips
from microwakeword.audio.spectrograms import SpectrogramGeneration
from mmap_ninja import RaggedMmap
import shutil

POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR = FEATURES_DIR / 'positive'
POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

# Verify audio files exist
wav_files = list(training_dir.glob('*.wav'))
print(f"Found {len(wav_files)} wav files in {training_dir}")
if wav_files:
    print(f"  Sample: {wav_files[0].name}")

# Load audio clips
clips = Clips(
    input_directory=str(training_dir),
    file_pattern='*.wav',
    max_clip_duration_s=None,
    remove_silence=False,
    random_split_seed=10,
    split_count=0.1
)

# Debug: Check if clips loaded
print(f"Clips object created")
if hasattr(clips, 'split_clips') and clips.split_clips is not None:
    for split_name in clips.split_clips:
        print(f"  Split '{split_name}': {len(clips.split_clips[split_name])} clips")
elif hasattr(clips, 'clips') and clips.clips is not None:
    print(f"  Total clips: {len(clips.clips)}")

# Generate training features (with augmentation)
print("\nGenerating training features...")
train_spec_gen = SpectrogramGeneration(
    clips=clips,
    augmenter=augmentation,
    slide_frames=10,
    step_ms=10
)

train_features_dir = POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR / 'train'
if train_features_dir.exists():
    shutil.rmtree(train_features_dir)

RaggedMmap.from_generator(
    out_dir=str(train_features_dir),
    sample_generator=train_spec_gen.spectrogram_generator(split='train', repeat=2),
    batch_size=1000,
    verbose=True
)

# Generate validation features (no augmentation)
print("\nGenerating validation features...")
val_spec_gen = SpectrogramGeneration(
    clips=clips,
    augmenter=None,
    slide_frames=1,
    step_ms=10
)

val_features_dir = POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR / 'val'
if val_features_dir.exists():
    shutil.rmtree(val_features_dir)

RaggedMmap.from_generator(
    out_dir=str(val_features_dir),
    sample_generator=val_spec_gen.spectrogram_generator(split='validation', repeat=1),
    batch_size=1000,
    verbose=True
)

# Verify output
train_count = len(list(train_features_dir.glob('*'))) if train_features_dir.exists() else 0
val_count = len(list(val_features_dir.glob('*'))) if val_features_dir.exists() else 0
print(f"\nDone! Train features: {train_count} files, Val features: {val_count} files")</cell id="cell-15">

import tensorflow as tf

interpreter = tf.lite.Interpreter(model_path=str(output_model))
interpreter.allocate_tensors()

inp = interpreter.get_input_details()[0]
out = interpreter.get_output_details()[0]

print(f"Input: {inp['shape']}, type={inp['dtype']}")

<cell id="cell-0"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type># microWakeWord Training Notebook

Train a custom wake word detection model compatible with ESP32-S3.

## Overview

This notebook trains models compatible with `wakeword_pretrained_test.ino`:
- **Input**: 40-bin log-mel spectrogram features (30ms window, 10ms stride)
- **Architecture**: MixNet-based streaming model
- **Output**: Quantized TFLite model for ESP32

Based on: https://github.com/kahrendt/microWakeWord</cell id="cell-0">

<cell id="cell-8"># Cell 6: Generate full training dataset
import subprocess
import shutil

training_dir = GENERATED_DIR / 'training'

# Clean up existing samples for fresh batch
if training_dir.exists():
    shutil.rmtree(training_dir)
training_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

SAMPLES_PER_VARIATION = 100  # Total: 9 variations * 100 = 900 samples

print(f"Generating {len(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS) * SAMPLES_PER_VARIATION} samples...")

for i, variation in enumerate(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS):
    print(f"  [{i+1}/{len(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS)}] '{variation}'")
    # Generate to temp dir to avoid filename collisions
    temp_dir = GENERATED_DIR / f'temp_{i}'
    temp_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    
    subprocess.run([
        'python3', 'piper-sample-generator/generate_samples.py',
        variation,
        '--max-samples', str(SAMPLES_PER_VARIATION),
        '--batch-size', '10',
        '--output-dir', str(temp_dir),
        '--model', 'piper-sample-generator/models/en_US-libritts_r-medium.pt'
    ], capture_output=True)
    
    # Move files with unique prefix
    for wav in temp_dir.glob('*.wav'):
        new_name = f"var{i}_{wav.name}"
        shutil.move(str(wav), str(training_dir / new_name))
    temp_dir.rmdir()

sample_count = len(list(training_dir.glob('*.wav')))
print(f"\nGenerated {sample_count} samples")</cell id="cell-8">

<cell id="cell-0"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type># microWakeWord Training Notebook

Train a custom wake word detection model compatible with ESP32-S3.

## Overview

This notebook trains models compatible with `wakeword_pretrained_test.ino`:
- **Input**: 40-bin log-mel spectrogram features (30ms window, 10ms stride)
- **Architecture**: MixNet-based streaming model
- **Output**: Quantized TFLite model for ESP32

Based on: https://github.com/kahrendt/microWakeWord</cell id="cell-0">

<cell id="cell-8"># Cell 6: Generate full training dataset
import subprocess
import shutil

training_dir = GENERATED_DIR / 'training'

# Clean up existing samples for fresh batch
if training_dir.exists():
    shutil.rmtree(training_dir)
training_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

SAMPLES_PER_VARIATION = 100  # Total: 9 variations * 100 = 900 samples

print(f"Generating {len(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS) * SAMPLES_PER_VARIATION} samples...")

for i, variation in enumerate(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS):
    print(f"  [{i+1}/{len(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS)}] '{variation}'")
    # Generate to temp dir to avoid filename collisions
    temp_dir = GENERATED_DIR / f'temp_{i}'
    temp_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    
    subprocess.run([
        'python3', 'piper-sample-generator/generate_samples.py',
        variation,
        '--max-samples', str(SAMPLES_PER_VARIATION),
        '--batch-size', '10',
        '--output-dir', str(temp_dir),
        '--model', 'piper-sample-generator/models/en_US-libritts_r-medium.pt'
    ], capture_output=True)
    
    # Move files with unique prefix
    for wav in temp_dir.glob('*.wav'):
        new_name = f"var{i}_{wav.name}"
        shutil.move(str(wav), str(training_dir / new_name))
    temp_dir.rmdir()

sample_count = len(list(training_dir.glob('*.wav')))
print(f"\nGenerated {sample_count} samples")</cell id="cell-8">

        ds = load_dataset(
            "agkphysics/AudioSet", 
            split="train",
            streaming=True,
            trust_remote_code=True
        )
        
        # Save first 500 audio samples as wav files
        count = 0
        max_samples = 500
        
        for sample in ds:
            if count >= max_samples:
                break
            try:
                audio = sample['audio']
                wav_path = AUDIOSET_DIR / f"audioset_{count:04d}.wav"
                sf.write(str(wav_path), audio['array'], audio['sampling_rate'])
                count += 1
                if count % 100 == 0:
                    print(f"  Saved {count}/{max_samples} samples")
            except Exception:
                continue  # Skip problematic samples
        
        print(f"Done! Saved {count} background audio samples")

        print(f"AudioSet loading failed: {e}")

    augmentation_probabilities={
        "SevenBandParametricEQ": 0.1,
        "TanhDistortion": 0.1,
        "PitchShift": 0.1,
        "BandStopFilter": 0.1,
        "AddColorNoise": 0.1,
        "AddBackgroundNoise": 0.75,
        "Gain": 1.0,
        "RIR": 0.5,

)
